title: There are more signs the UFL could be leaving Birmingham
summary: Yes, the Stallions may be checking out of Birmingham.
full_text: Yes, the Stallions may be checking out of Birmingham. Beyond the conspicuous absence of Birmingham from the list of UFL teams looking for a head of business operations, UFL co-owner Mike Repole has made it clear that a relocation is possible if not likely. "Sitting in a senior leadership meeting planning the [the UFL] 2027 season, one thing is becoming very clear," Repole said Tuesday on Twitter. "The right market. The right sized venue. A passionate fan base. That’s the WINNING formula. I have a hard time seeing us back at Protective Stadium next year. It goes against one of the biggest principles we’re building this league around [. . .] smaller stadiums, packed houses, real energy and a true home field atmosphere. Birmingham, I am looking and need options and ideas." It's hardly a coincidence that the UFL posted notices for the head of business operations jobs at all teams except Birmingham that same day. A move out of Birmingham looks to be firmly in play. Will there be a Birmingham alternative to Protective Stadium? With a capacity of 47,100, that's way too big for the UFL. Repole wants venues that more easily reflect the presence of human beings in the building. So when Repole says, "Birmingham, I am looking and need options and ideas," the message could be not specifically for Birmingham but to another city that may be interested in pilfering the Stallions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Is Tom Brady laying the foundation for a presidential run?
summary: Brady's overexposure is either mid-life crisis run amok or part of a broader calculation.
full_text: Tom Brady's slow-motion pivot to pro wrestling proves that the GOAT is overexposed. But there's a chance his ever-expanding footprint is more about political strategy than deep-seated insecurity. Brady's play could be to lay the foundation for a presidential run. I don't know anything (as usual) about any potential aspirations along those lines. A reader mentioned it as a possible alternative to an apparent mid-life crisis run amok. The more I thought about it, the more sense it made. It would explain the effort to connect with wrestling fans, even if Brady apparently aspires to be a heel. (He could always turn face at the right time.) It also would fit with something that one of Brady's former business partners believed. The word "former" applies not because Brady and the former partner had a falling out but because the former partner currently is in prison. Before the house of cards known as FTX collapsed, founder Sam Bankman-Fried reportedly was trying to get Brady to run for the Republican nomination in 2024, against the current president. It supposedly went far enough to get Bankman-Fried to ask his team to conduct polling on the views of Americans regarding Brady as a presidential candidate. Not long ago, the idea of someone with no experience in politics running for the highest U.S. political office would have been dismissed as lunacy. After eleven years of lunacy come to life, it's a new path to power. Why spin your wheels in the House or the Senate when you can leverage fame and notoriety into an instant political base? Brady looks good (regardless of whether there are any pharmaceutical, of follicular, enhancements), he speaks better than he used to, he's rich and getting richer all the time. He craves competition (and some would say attention), which could make the political arena the perfect spot for the Man in the Arena. So stay tuned. Brady is creeping toward 50. And if/when he concludes that he'll never have the kind of cash needed to become the controlling owner of an NFL team (he most likely won't), Brady may decide to try to take control of the entire country.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals' Travis Vokolek retires at age 28 because of neck injury
summary: During a game last season, Cardinals tight end Travis Vokolek was taken off the field on a stretcher after a collision while blocking on a kickoff.
full_text: During a game last season, Cardinals tight end Travis Vokolek was taken off the field on a stretcher after a collision while blocking on a kickoff. That proved to be the last play of his career. Vokolek wrote on social media that he is retiring on doctors' advice because of the seriousness of the neck injury he suffered on that play. "After numerous visits with doctors and neurologists over the past couple of months, I have been advised to medically retire from the NFL due to a serious neck injury that I suffered this past season," Vokolek wrote. "I am extremely grateful and blessed to have been able to live out my childhood dream of playing football at the highest level for the past three years. Football has taught me many life lessons and given me unforgettable memories. I am forever grateful to all my teammates, coaches, trainers, and others who have supported my family and I along the way. A sincere thank you to the Arizona Cardinals training staff for being first class with the care and support they provided my family and I during this hard time. I am especially grateful for my wife who has been there the whole time through the many ups and downs of the NFL. She has never wavered and has been extremely supportive through it all. I have attacked everyday of being a professional football player with passion, determination, and discipline. I can say that I truly left everything out on the field. Thank you for all of the love and support. Lastly, thank you football!" Vokolek originally entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie with the Ravens in 2023. After spending most of that season on Baltimore's practice squad, he signed to the Cardinals' active roster late in 2023 and stayed in Arizona through last season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tyreek Hill says in rehab video he is trying to regain power in his left leg
summary: The free agent wide receiver had surgery to repair a serious knee injury 10 months ago.
full_text: '' Tyreek Hill remains a free agent and for good reason. The wide receiver released a rehab workout video on Wednesday, saying that after two surgeries he still has no power in his left leg. "So it's about 10 months after doing two surgeries," Hill said. "My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it's one day at a time." In the 1-minute, 38-second social media post, titled Cheetah, Reborn, Hill runs and jumps outside on turf, on a basketball court and in a pool at what appears to be his Florida home. "I ain't going to tell you what my timeline is, but timeline looking real good right now, man," Hill said. Hill dislocated his knee and tore multiple ligaments, including his ACL, in a Sept. 29 game against the Jets. He was hospitalized overnight and required surgery the next day. "You know, they told me I might not be able to walk again, and the doctor is like, 'Bro, we don't know what's going to happen with your future,' and now look at me. God is good," Hill said. "I feel good." The Dolphins released Hill on Feb. 16, making him a free agent.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Jimmy Garoppolo open to playing after considering retirement
summary: Free agent quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo considered retirement during the offseason, but Garoppolo has now decided he will come back to play in the right situation, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports.
full_text: ' Free agent quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo considered retirement during the offseason, but Garoppolo has now decided he will come back to play in the right situation, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports. Garafolo noted that nothing is imminent, and it might take a quarterback injury for Garoppolo to sign somewhere. Garoppolo spent the past two seasons with the Rams as Matthew Stafford's backup. Coach Sean McVay has kept the door open to Garoppolo's return despite the team's first-round selection of Ty Simpson. Garoppolo, 34, was a second-round pick of the Patriots in 2014 and also has played for the 49ers and Raiders in his 12 seasons. He has appeared in 85 games with 64 starts -- 55 coming with the 49ers — and is 43-21 as a starter. Garoppolo has totaled 15,828 passing yards, 96 touchdowns and 52 interceptions.
author: Charean Williams

title: Will the Chiefs' new stadium have grass? No decision has been made.
summary: As the Chiefs prepare to move to a new domed stadium in Kansas, the details made available to date don't address one key factor.
full_text: As the Chiefs prepare to move to a new domed stadium in Kansas, the details made available to date don't address one key factor. Will the playing surface be natural grass or artificial turf? Per the Chiefs, no official decision has been made as to the issue of grass or turf. The team's preference, however, is grass. If it's grass, the new venue will need to have a way to move the grass for the various other events that the stadium will host. That means either having a tray that slides out of the facility (like the Cardinals and Raiders use) or a more elaborate system that stores the grass surface underground. At a time when the NFL Players Association is pushing for grass in all NFL venues, the future of the Chiefs' playing surface becomes critical. They're currently one of 16 teams that play on grass. The union will want to keep it that way. The Chiefs currently do as well. It all comes down to how much it will cost to have a system for ensuring that a high-quality grass surface is available in what will be another building with a roof, and whether the money will be there to fund the difference in cost between having grass and rolling out the green carpet.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers have an ownership emergency option, if they'd ever need to use it
summary: The corporation could be dissolved and replaced with an expansion franchise.
full_text: '' During the slow time, the mind wanders. A question from a viewer during the summer run of #PFTPM sent my relaxed brain wandering in one specific direction. And with the annual Packers shareholder meeting coming on Monday, there's no time like now to trot it out. The seeds were planted, deliberately or not, by Packers president and CEO Ed Policy. In a March 2026 interview with Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal , Policy expressed an opinion that the current financial realities of NFL ownership make it harder for the only publicly-owned NFL franchise to compete. “If you think about any other team, they’ve got deep-pocketed owners , most of them are worth significantly more than that, and they could sell less than 10 percent of their team, give up no controlling interest, and raise a heck of a lot more than that,” Policy said. “Given the pace that the expenses have accelerated over the past few years, if we find ourselves falling behind, it’s going to be really hard to catch up. So, we have to keep ourselves in a position where we’re not falling behind.” So what if the Packers eventually do fall behind? What happens if, at some point, the powers-that-be decide that the current business model doesn't work? On the surface, there would seem to be nothing to do. The Packers are publicly owned. Because the shares can't be sold, it's impossible for anyone to buy up controlling interest in the company. Still, the potential solution is fairly simple. Green Bay Packers, Inc. could, in theory, dissolve, with the assets of the corporation sold to an expansion franchise. The proceeds would then go to charity. It's right there in the team's Article VI of Articles of Incorporation: "That should there be a dissolution of the Green Bay Packers, Inc., the players shall be subject to the National Football League Rules, but that the undivided profits and assets of the Green Bay Packers, Inc. shall go to the Green Bay Packers Foundation for distribution to community programs, charitable causes, and such other similar cause to which the Foundation deems appropriate." Of course, leadership of the corporation would first have to choose to dissolve. It would be an option utilized as a last-ditch effort, if/when the "deep-pocketed owners" to whom Policy referred become sufficiently rich to spend the Packers into oblivion. And, frankly, if the absence of a traditional owner were to convert the Packers into the perennial loser that they were for most of the '70s and '80s, the fans could get behind a radical change in ownership structure. What of the shareholders, you ask? Those folks who paid good money for a piece of memorabilia that's framed on the wall? The many stock certificates would continue to have the value they currently possess — none at all. The stock can't be sold. It doesn't appreciate in value. It has no real value. It gets the "owner" nothing more than the official piece of paper and an invitation to the annual shareholder meeting. Based on conversations with those in the know, the league at large wouldn't be upset if it happened. The transition from corporation to traditional owner would introduce another multi-billionaire into the club. And with an expansion fee of at least $10 billion (much more if it happens in the not-foreseeable future), the other owners would share that payment equally. There's another benefit. If the Packers convert from a publicly-owned corporation, the franchise's books would be sealed shut. There would be no way to know how much money any team makes, and no way to isolate the shared revenue and multiply it by 32 to know more about how much money the league is making. It won't happen unless and until the Board of Directors decides to do it. But if it's determined that the current structure is keeping the team from being competitive, it's an option for giving an oligarch who owns a cheesehead the opportunity to modernize the ownership structure and to keep the franchise on equal footing with its competitors. The challenge would be to ensure that the Packers would stay put. Perhaps a commitment would be secured that the team would never move. The Packers, after all, must be in Green Bay. Even with that limitation, someone with billions to burn would take over the team, if the Packers ever decide to make a dramatic change in their structure for the long-term good of the franchise.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori underwent ankle surgery but expected back for Week 1
summary: The Seahawks announced Monday that they had placed safety Nick Emmanwori on the active/physically unable to perform list.
full_text: ' The Seahawks announced Monday that they had placed safety Nick Emmanwori on the active/physically unable to perform list. His injury was unknown until Wednesday. Brady Henderson of ESPN reports that Emmanwori underwent right ankle surgery earlier this month and could miss some time in training camp. Emmanwori, though, is expected to be ready for Week 1. Emmanwori had participated in the offseason work with teammates but continued to experience soreness, leading to the arthroscopic procedure. The 2025 second-round pick had two injuries to his right ankle last season. He had a high-ankle sprain in the season opener that forced him to miss three games and then a low-ankle sprain before Super Bowl LX , which he played through. Emmanwori tallied 81 total tackles with nine tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, 11 passes defensed and an interception in 14 regular-season games in 2025. He added 13 total tackles with four passes defensed and a fumble recovery in Seattle’s three postseason games. The Seahawks can activate Emmanwori back to the 90-player roster as soon as he passes a physical.
author: Charean Williams

title: Terrion Arnold has arraignment hearing Aug. 13
summary: Former Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold has an arraignment hearing before a judge in Tampa scheduled for Aug. 13, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
full_text: Former Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold has an arraignment hearing before a judge in Tampa scheduled for Aug. 13, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. He faces eight felony charges of kidnapping and robbery from his arrest last month. The Lions released Arnold a day before he posted a $1 million bond and left the Hillsborough County (Florida) jail. He was arrested on four counts each of kidnapping and armed robbery, which could bring a life sentence if he is convicted. The former first-round pick has drawn interest from the Colts, Jets, Seahawks and Texans, his agent, Nicole Lynn, testified before a judge on July 10. He remains a free agent as training camps begin to open.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett reports to Cardinals training camp
summary: Brissett is looking for a revised contract in Arizona.
full_text: Jacoby Brissett has answered the first big question of Cardinals training camp. NFL Media reports that Brissett reported to camp along with the rest of the team's veterans on Wednesday. On Thursday, there should be more information about whether the quarterback just did that so he won't be fined. Brissett did not practice at all in the spring because he is looking for a revised contract that better reflects his status as the likely Week 1 starter in Arizona. Brissett did report to mandatory minicamp in order to avoid fines and his status at Thursday's practice will reveal whether he plans to hold in until the contract is addressed to his satisfaction. Brissett can make up to $5.39 million this season, but only $1.5 million of his salary is guaranteed. He spent most of last season as the team's starter and finished the year with 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns and eight interceptions, but the Cardinals went 1-11 over his 12 starts. Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck are the other quarterback options in Arizona.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots sign first-year TE Mitch Van Vooren
summary: The Patriots announced three roster moves on Wednesday.
full_text: The Patriots announced three roster moves on Wednesday. The signing of rookie free agent linebacker Riley Wilson was previously reported. The Patriots also signed first-year tight end Mitch Van Vooren and released fullback Brock Lampe. Van Vooren, 25, entered the NFL as a rookie free agent in 2025, signing with the Seahawks. Seattle cut him on June 13, 2025, and he signed with the Browns on Aug. 4 before they waived him on Aug. 24. Van Vooren earned first-team All-NACC honors during his final collegiate season at St. Norbert after recording 33 receptions for 510 yards and 10 touchdowns. He began his college career as a track athlete at Marquette, setting the school record in the 400-meter hurdles. Lampe, 23, signed with the Patriots in 2025 as an undrafted free agent out of Northern Illinois. He spent all of last season on injured reserve.
author: Charean Williams

title: Raiders rookie CB Jermod McCoy makes signing official
summary: The Raiders made the signing of fourth-round cornerback Jermod McCoy official, announcing the move Wednesday.
full_text: ''' The Raiders made the signing of fourth-round cornerback Jermod McCoy official, announcing the move Wednesday. The team made him the 101st overall pick this spring. McCoy spent two seasons at Tennessee after transferring from Oregon State (2023). He played 25 career games with 18 starts and totaled 75 tackles, 16 passes defensed and six interceptions during his career. He missed the 2025 season after tearing an ACL in January 2025 and elected to forego his final year of college eligibility to head to the NFL. McCoy earned All-SEC first-team, All-America second-team and was a Jim Thorpe Award semifinalist after his sophomore season in 2024. He started 13 games that season and led the Volunteers with 13 passes defensed and four interceptions, both marks ranking fourth in the SEC. In 2023, he appeared in 12 games with five starts as a true freshman at Oregon State and led the team with nine passes defensed and two interceptions while recording 31 tackles. The Raiders' rookies report to camp on Thursday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Undrafted free agent Riley Wilson to sign with Patriots
summary: The Patriots are signing undrafted free agent Riley Wilson, his representation, PM3 Sports Management, announced.
full_text: ''' The Patriots are signing undrafted free agent Riley Wilson, his representation, PM3 Sports Management, announced. He spent time with the Buccaneers this offseason after going undrafted. Wilson spent last season at the University of Arizona, where he posted 51 tackles, three sacks, two interceptions and four pass breakups. He began his college career as a tight end at Hawaii. During his freshman season in 2020, Wilson played in one game and caught a 2-yard pass against Boise State. In 2021, Wilson transitioned from tight end to linebacker and played as a core special teamer. He saw action in four games in 2022 and transferred to Montana for 2023. Wilson led Montana in sacks (8.5) and tackles for loss (15) that season. In 2024, he totaled 83 tackles, 4.5 sacks and seven quarterback hits. He transferred to Arizona the following season.
author: Charean Williams

title: UFL is hiring a head of business operations for seven of its teams (but not Birmingham)
summary: The UFL is in its offseason, and the UFL offseason a year ago was an occasion to move three teams of the eight teams.
full_text: ''' The UFL is in its offseason, and the UFL offseason a year ago was an occasion to move three teams of the eight teams. Another team could possibly be in potential jeopardy of relocation, based on a fairly significant hint the UFL has dropped, by implication. As noted by Mark Perry of UFL News Hub, seven teams are currently looking for a "head of business operations (team)." One team — the Stallions — is not included in the online listing . So why would seven teams be hiring a "head of business operations (team)" but not the eighth? The omission is glaring, and it could be an indication that Birmingham may not be long for the UFL. The Stallions averaged 8.248 fans per home game last year. The final three games didn't go well, with 4,705, 4,824, and 5,253 in attendance. Unless it was an oversight, it's hard to understand why the Stallions aren't included. Last year, the function was centralized. This year, it's being handled on a team-by-team basis. With only seven teams posting the opening, the absence of Birmingham will invite speculation as to whether the Stallions will be playing in a new city in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ryan Clark takes issue with suggestion he wasn't forced off air during show
summary: It's been well established that ESPN informed NFL analyst Ryan Clark that he was being let go while he was on the air.
full_text: ''' It's been well established that ESPN informed NFL analyst Ryan Clark that he was being let go while he was on the air. And Clark has chimed in on how it went down. On Tuesday night, TMZ (which was a little late to the party on this one) reiterated the reporting from Andrew Marchand of The Athletic regarding the decision to tell Clark while he was appearing on NFL Live . From the TMZ report: "Ryan did not come back on the air after being informed he was being let go ... obviously, the news rattled him, and we're told both Ryan and ESPN agreed it was better not to return ." The item went out with a headline and tweet that said Clark " wasn’t forced from air during commercial break." That caught Clark's eye, and it drew a response. Said Clark : "I wasn’t forced? I ask, 'should I be done now?' The answer was 'yes.'" ESPN could have given Clark the option to finish the show. It wouldn't have been easy, for anyone. And he may have had something to say that would have gone viral, to say the least. Still, as Clark tells it, it wasn't a mutual decision. He didn't even participate in it. He asked if he's done right now, and he was told that he was.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals OL Isaiah Adams arrested in Canada on four weapons charges
summary: Cardinals offensive lineman Isaiah Adams faces four weapons charges after his recent arrest in Canada, the Associated Press reports.
full_text: Cardinals offensive lineman Isaiah Adams faces four weapons charges after his recent arrest in Canada, the Associated Press reports. Adams, 25, was charged with possession of a firearm obtained in a crime, possession of a restricted/prohibited firearm, no license while in possession of a loaded firearm and possessing a prohibited device, according to the Durham Regional Police Service in Ontario. Three others were arrested along with Adams. "Isaiah is completely innocent in this matter," Adams' attorney Adam Weisberg said in a statement. "He had no knowledge of any firearm, and he will be fully exonerated." Police concluded an investigation on Friday into a male believed to be in possession of a firearm and involved in drug trafficking. Two other people arrested were charged with possession of fentanyl with intent to distribute. Adams was expected to report to training camp with the team on Thursday, according to the news service. "We are aware of the situation involving Isaiah Adams," the Cardinals said in a statement. "Out of respect for the process, we will refrain from commenting further at this time." Adams, who was born in Ajax, Ontario, was a third-round pick of the Cardinals out of Illinois in 2024. He started 11 games last season after starting five as a rookie.
author: Charean Williams

title: New ESPN article on Rooney Rule underscores importance of Brian Flores litigation
summary: The only way to effect change is through a jury verdict.
full_text: On one hand, the NFL has tried to keep the Brian Flores lawsuit from getting to the merits of the claims because it's the first page from the standard big-company-that-has-been-sued playbook. On the other hand, delaying the Flores case delays the best available path to a long-overdue reckoning. ESPN, which is now partially owned by the NFL, has posted an article regarding the Rooney Rule. The headline declares that coaches believe the process is “rigged” against them . (It's refreshing that ESPN has pursued an issue that the league would prefer be ignored; we'll see whether and to what extent ESPN promotes the article through its endless car wash of shows.) The starting point, and centerpiece, of the ESPN story is the runaround former Raiders defensive coordinator Patrick Graham experienced after he had served as the league-mandated second minority interview for the Jaguars head-coaching job that went to Liam Coen in early 2025. It was perceived to be yet another box-checking sham interview, aimed at allowing a team to comply with the Rooney Rule before hiring their preferred candidate. Here's the key paragraph from the ESPN article: "More than a dozen minority coaches declined to comment for this story, citing concerns that speaking candidly would jeopardize future opportunities. Among the 13 Black coaches who did speak -- some on the record but most anonymously -- the issue is clear: Even with hiring rules in place, they feel they cannot overcome ownership bias or the long-established relationships that shape hiring." Even Graham, who talked about his Jacksonville experience on the record to ESPN last year, declined to comment this time around. Meanwhile, the NFL faces political pressure to abandon "DEI" efforts, now that the acronym has been morphed into a slur in sheep's clothing. In Florida, attorney general James Uthmeier has been attacking the NFL over inclusion efforts. Nationally, the political winds continue to blow against the notion of placing diversity above merit. (As Jon Stewart observed earlier this week, "Meritocracy. It is a beautiful word. Where the fuck is it? ") Back to Flores. Along with Ray Horton and Steve Wilks, Flores has fended off the NFL's multi-year effort to vacuum their claims into the NFL's secret, rigged, kangaroo court of arbitration. Now, after more than four years, it's time to get down to talking to witnesses, gathering documents, and proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the NFL and many if not most of its teams make key hiring decisions with race being, consciously or not, a motivating factor. It could get messy, but civil litigation is often uncivil. Owners and Commissioner Roger Goodell will be grilled under oath during pre-trial depositions. Some or all of the 25 minority coaches who won't speak to ESPN reporters will receive a subpoena to testify under oath, which will not only protect them from retaliation but compel them to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The Flores case becomes the only way to allow the facts to be developed, presented, and evaluated. A jury will determine, based on all of the evidence, whether Flores and his colleagues have shown that the NFL's teams have a longstanding racial bias when it comes to hiring head coaches, offensive coordinators, and General Managers. Many will say (because they always do) that businesses can hire whomever they choose. That opinion is grossly misinformed; federal law and the laws of many states prevent certain factors from being considered when hiring (and firing) decisions are made. Real change can be effected in American society in one of three ways: the passage of legislation, the implementation of regulations, or the verdicts rendered through litigation. That's why large companies hate lawsuits. They can't control a process that could force them to change their ways by attaching a massive financial consequence for their past failures to do so. At some point, the NFL may realize that, win or lose, a public trial in open court will have significant negative consequences. The league and its teams could be tempted to make Flores and company a settlement offer they can't refuse. That's the key. Will the league make an offer so large that the individuals won't be able to reject it? Will they reject it anyway, realizing that taking their claims all the way to a verdict may be the only way to get the NFL and its teams to finally change their ways?
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay: Aaron Donald is thinking about this, will go through his process
summary: The Rams' HC addressed in a recent interview how the DT is contemplating coming out of retirement.
full_text: ' Is Aaron Donald really coming back? As of now, it's still an open question — one even Rams head coach Sean McVay does not have the answer to. " I have crossed paths with Aaron Donald ," McVay said in an interview with Jason LaCanfora of The Daily Flock podcast. "What’s special is, we have a really special relationship. It’s way bigger than football. I’ve heard him say it before and it means the world to me — and I feel the same — it’s family with us. He’s done so much for me. I love the man he is. I love the husband, the father, the son — he represents a lot of the things that are right. "And what he’s going to do is, he is thinking about this. He’s going to go through his process. And the one thing about Aaron Donald is, what he does, he does it full speed ahead." Donald was recently captured working out at the Rams' practice facility in Los Angeles. He's also posted plenty of pictures and video of himself working out throughout the offseason. ESPN's Adam Schefter noted this week that Donald is trying to get himself ready for the season, and it doesn’t seem like a definitive answer on his return is coming in the immediate future.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals place fourth-rounder Kaleb Proctor on injured reserve
summary: Cardinals fourth-round pick Kaleb Proctor will not see any game action during his rookie season.
full_text: '' Cardinals fourth-round pick Kaleb Proctor will not see any game action during his rookie season. The Cardinals placed Proctor on injured reserve Wednesday and the timing of the move means he will not be eligible to be activated at any point during the 2026 campaign. The defensive lineman tore his meniscus during the team's offseason program and head coach Mike LaFleur said in the spring that the injury could keep him out for the entire year. Arizona signed defensive lineman Coziah Izzard to fill the open spot on their 90-man roster. Izzard signed with the Chiefs after going undrafted out of Penn State in 2025. He also spent time with the Saints, but did not appear in any regular season games for either team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals, QB Carson Beck agree to terms
summary: Three rookie quarterbacks remain unsigned.
full_text: There had been four unsigned rookie quarterbacks. There are now three. Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Cardinals and quarterback Carson Beck have agreed to terms on a four-year, $7.4 million deal, as the Cardinals gather for training camp. The amount was never in question. It's slotted. There's nothing to negotiate. The question is whether he got more guarantees than others around him received, given the position he plays. Eventually, the contract will be reported and the full percentage of the guarantees will be known. For now, Beck is under contract. He can embark on an effort to disrupt the current plan to make veteran Jacoby Brissett the starter. And the chances of that could increase, if Brissett and the Cardinals don't work out a new deal before camp opens — and if Brissett declines to practice until they do. Three other rookie quarterbacks are unsigned: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, Rams quarterback Ty Simpson, and Steelers quarterback Drew Allar.
author: Mike Florio

title: Raiders are expected to "sprinkle" first-team reps for quarterback Fernando Mendoza
summary: The quarterback competition in Las Vegas won't be a competition if it never becomes one.
full_text: ''' The quarterback competition in Las Vegas won't be a competition if it never becomes one. If it's a truly open competition, the first overall pick in the draft presumably should be able to beat a 37-year-old veteran who had no clear starting opportunities elsewhere in the league. With all due respect to Kirk Cousins (who has been a very good quarterback and an even better businessman), the first overall pick in any draft should be able to win a full and fair competition with Cousins at this point in his career. (Unless the first overall pick isn't a quarterback.) One way to keep the veterans on the team from revolting when it comes to the decision to not use Mendoza would be to minimize Mendoza's chances to show that he's the better option. Which may explain the recent suggestion from Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated that the Raiders " will sprinkle Mendoza in with the first team " during training camp. Of course, if Mendoza makes the most out of the sprinkling, the flow could increase. If a limited apples-to-apples comparison makes it clear to the established players on the team (starting with defensive end Maxx Crosby and tight end Brock Bowers) that Mendoza could be the Johnny Appleseed for a forest of playoff appearances, the mood could shift, quickly. The balance for the Raiders, if they're committed to keeping Mendoza in the garage for a year, will be to get him practice reps without making it clear that he should get more. And more. And more. The Chiefs pulled it off nine years ago with Patrick Mahomes because they were a perennial playoff team under Alex Smith. The Raiders have been to the playoffs twice since the 2002 season. The players on the team will want the guy who gives them the best chance not to win later, but to win now. Cousins has said the better player should play. As camp prepares to open, the question is whether Mendoza will get much of a chance to prove it — and whether he does enough with the "sprinkling" he gets to force the issue to the front burner.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Morgan: "No plans" to sign fourth QB after Will Grier's retirement
summary: The Panthers' roster went down to three quarterbacks when Will Grier retired earlier this month.
full_text: ' The Panthers' roster went down to three quarterbacks when Will Grier retired earlier this month. The plan is now to hold that number at the position through training camp. In his Wednesday press conference, General Manager Dan Morgan told reporters that Carolina has "no plans" right now to bring in a fourth QB. “Obviously, wish Will and his family the best,” Morgan said. “In terms of his career, just playing as long as he did — just wish him the best moving forward.” So, Carolina will go through training camp with Kenny Pickett and Haynes King behind starter Bryce Young at quarterback. Grier, 31, had rejoined Carolina as a free agent in April. The Panthers had brought him into the league as a third-round pick back in 2019. But after participating in the club’s offseason program, Grier decided to hang up his cleats. Grier started just two games in his career, both of which came as a rookie for the Panthers. He also spent time with the Cowboys, Bengals, Patriots, Chargers, and Eagles.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks place Zach Charbonnet on PUP list
summary: Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet tore his ACL in the divisional round of the playoffs and the team confirmed that he's not ready to resume practicing on Wednesday.
full_text: '' Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet tore his ACL in the divisional round of the playoffs and the team confirmed that he's not ready to resume practicing on Wednesday. Charbonnet has been placed on the physically unable to perform list ahead of the start of training camp. Charbonnet can be activated from the list at any point in camp, but the timing of the injury means that it will likely be some time before the team will be moving him to the active roster. The Seahawks previously placed safety Nick Emmanwori, running back Kenny McIntosh, cornerback Tyrone Broden, and defensive tackle Deven Eastern on the PUP list. Charbonnet ran 184 times for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns last season. First-round pick Jadarian Price, George Holani, Emanuel Wilson, Velus Jones, and Jacardia Wright are the healthy options at running back in Seattle.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers put Ikem Ekwonu on PUP list, optimistic he'll return this season
summary: The Panthers are ready to start practicing at training camp, but left tackle Ikem Ekwonu isn't ready to join them on the field.
full_text: The Panthers are ready to start practicing at training camp, but left tackle Ikem Ekwonu isn't ready to join them on the field. Panthers GM Dan Morgan announced on Wednesday that Ekwonu will go on the physically unable to perform list to open camp. Ekwonu tore his patellar tendon during January's playoff loss to the Rams and the nature of the injury means there's still more rehab ahead for the 2022 first-round pick. Morgan told reporters that Ekwonu is in a good place with that rehab and that he's optimistic about having the tackle back during the regular season, but did not set any timeline for return. The Panthers also put right tackle Taylor Moton on the non-football injury list this week because of a blood clot in his lung. Moton is expected to be out into the regular season, which could leave Rasheed Walker and 2026 first-rounder Monroe Freeling as the team's top options at tackle. Morgan also announced that defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton will go on PUP due to a neck injury and that defensive lineman Bobby Brown is headed to NFI with a hamstring issue. Cornerback Jaylon Guilbeau was waived off the non-football injury list.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals EDGE BJ Ojulari: I can be a double-digit sack guy, have to showcase it
summary: Cardinals edge rusher BJ Ojulari returned from a torn ACL to play in eight games last season, but the 2023 second-round pick didn't feel all the way back from the injury that wiped out his second NFL season in August.
full_text: ''' Cardinals edge rusher BJ Ojulari returned from a torn ACL to play in eight games last season, but the 2023 second-round pick didn't feel all the way back from the injury that wiped out his second NFL season in August. Ojulari had one sack last year, but told Cardinals reporter Kyle Odegard that he began to feel back to himself during this year's offseason program. Ojulari has reframed his goals for the season as a result of that change in circumstances. “My motivation level is very high ," Ojulari said. "I believe I can be a double-digit sack guy. Now for me, it’s go showcase it. We had a lot of guys drafted in our edge class that are doing some great things, and I want to be another one of those guys. I believe in my ability.” Josh Sweat was the leading pass rusher in Arizona with 12 sacks last season, but the team was missing a reliable running mate for him off the edge. If Ojulari can provide that, the defense should be harder for opponents to handle in head coach Mike LaFleur's debut season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Jermod McCoy plans to sign rookie contract on Wednesday
summary: With training camp set to begin in the coming days, the Raiders will get an important piece of business done on Wednesday.
full_text: ' With training camp set to begin in the coming days, the Raiders will get an important piece of business done on Wednesday. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, cornerback Jermod McCoy plans to sign his rookie contract on Wednesday. McCoy was a fourth-round pick in this year’s draft. He missed the 2025 season after suffering a torn ACL in January 2025, electing to forego his final year of college eligibility to head to the next level. After beginning his collegiate career at Oregon State, McCoy transferred to Tennessee in 2024. He was a second-team All-SEC honoree for the Volunteers that year. Raiders rookies report to training camp on Thursday, with veterans reporting on July 28.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Chiefs release renderings of new stadium, a building "built for noise"
summary: The Chiefs will leave Arrowhead Stadium for a new indoor home in Kansas in 2031, but they're promising their fans will sound as loud as ever.
full_text: ' The Chiefs will leave Arrowhead Stadium for a new indoor home in Kansas in 2031, but they're promising their fans will sound as loud as ever. The team released renderings of the new stadium design today, and owner Clark Hunt said he's confident fans are going to like what they see — and hear. "Today we are excited to show Chiefs Kingdom a first look at our new home," Hunt said. "From the beginning, our goal has been to build something that improved the gameday experience for every single fan. This new stadium will do just that. It's spectacular. It honors the rich legacy of this franchise while setting a bold course for the future of Chiefs Kingdom. While we're still finalizing many of the details, there are a few things we know for sure: it will hold 70,000 fans, it will still be the best place in the world to tailgate, and the whole building will be built for noise." The indoor stadium represents another step away from football in the elements, with Kansas City no longer playing in the cold and snow in December and January, as they have for decades. The new stadium will have a translucent roof that the team describes as "maximizing visibility for military flyovers." The stadium is expected to cost $3 billion, of which taxpayers are paying $1.8 billion.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Buccaneers to wear 1976 throwbacks in Week 13
summary: The Buccaneers will break out their original uniforms again this season.
full_text: '' The Buccaneers will break out their original uniforms again this season. The team wore their 1976 duds twice in 2025 to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the franchise and initially said that there were no plans to continue wearing them in the future, but they announced a new plan on Wednesday. They will don the throwback white jerseys and helmets with their original Buccaneer logo against the Chargers at home in Week 13. Both games that featured the white-on-white uniforms ended with Bucs wins in 2025. They beat the Jets 29-27 in Week 3 and topped the Seahawks 38-35 in Week 5. The Seahawks also wore their original 1976 uniforms for that game. The team has not announced any future plans to wear the throwbacks, but another win against the Chargers probably wouldn't hurt the chances that we'll be seeing them again.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tom Pelissero confirms his NFL Network exit
summary: When news broke that ESPN would be laying off reporter Tom Pelissero with a year left on his NFL Network deal, it wasn't clear whether he had been informed of it before he read about it elsewhere.
full_text: '' When news broke that ESPN would be laying off reporter Tom Pelissero with a year left on his NFL Network deal, it wasn't clear whether he had been informed of it before he read about it elsewhere. (At least he wasn't told while, you know, on the air .) Pelissero confirmed his exit on Wednesday morning, with a post on Twitter. "Thanks to all of you who watched me the past nine years on NFL Network ," Pelissero said. "Thanks to all of my colleagues who made the job fun and pushed me on a daily basis. Thanks to my family, who constantly made sacrifices to support me in a life-consuming job. I’m so grateful. See you soon." It remains to be seen what "soon" means. In past layoffs, ESPN squatted on the former employee's contract, refusing to allow them to work elsewhere while still being paid by ESPN. In Ed Werder's case, he was asked to help cover the draft after he was let go while also prevented from working elsewhere. (ESPN later agreed to let Werder take a part-time gig with Westwood One.) And so the clunky, clumsy execution and implementation of layoffs by ESPN isn't new. While the latest round has revealed embarrassing lapses when it comes to internal discretion and confidentiality — leading to the ridiculous decision to inform Ryan Clark that he was being let go during a show on which he was appearing — the lack of humanity when dealing with the human beings who make up the workforce is a cultural phenomenon at the four-letter network. Folks like Clark and Pelissero have every right to utter one or more four-letter words. And while there's a long-term benefit in not going scorched earth as to a former employer (after all, a prospective employer is simply another inevitable future employer), it would be hard to fault Clark, Pelissero, or anyone else whose exit from a professional media outlet was handled in a grossly unprofessional way from saying so. Even if they don't, others can say it for them.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ranking all 191 first-round NFL Draft picks since 2020: Best, worst selections of the decade
summary: Five QBs rank among the top seven first-round choices since 2020, while Caleb Williams lands in the bottom third of our list
full_text:
Deep in the heart of the offseason, I was inspired by an exercise I saw on the NFL Stock Exchange podcast with Trevor Sikkema and Connor Rogers to take a look back at draft history, specifically evaluating and ranking the first-round picks this decade.
With a list this large, being clear about the methodology is important. I decided to evaluate each decision from the team's point of view , given the draft capital and options available on the board, rather than evaluating talent alone. This is an important distinction because I'm not simply ranking players.
For example, Kyle Pitts is a good player, but the decision to draft him No. 4 overall in 2021 was objectively not a good one considering the next six players off the board were Ja'Marr Chase , Jaylen Waddle , Penei Sewell , Jaycee Horn , Patrick Surtain II and DeVonta Smith . Obviously, with the 2026 draft class yet to play a snap in the NFL, it was not included. Even the 2025 class is difficult to rank this early in their careers, with very few players appearing at either edge of the spectrum. Let's get to the rankings first and then break them down team by team to evaluate how each franchise did over that span.
This is unfortunately how a franchise becomes a perennial bottom-feeder. The Cardinals have drafted one Pro Bowl player this decade in second-round tight end Trey McBride , and half of their first-rounders aren't even starters anymore. That's a difficult mess to overcome in one of the best divisions in the NFL.
Big hits with glaring holes is very much the story of the Falcons this decade. No hole has proven more difficult to overcome than the one Matt Ryan left at quarterback after the 2021 season. They tried to solve it in the loaded 2024 draft by taking Michael Penix Jr. eighth overall, but his checking in at No. 154 in these rankings tells you how that's gone. They've had a different leading passer every year since and look poised to do it for a fifth straight season with Tua Tagovailoa coming over from Miami this offseason.
The Ravens have been one of the NFL's best-run franchises since their inception, and that hasn't changed even after Ozzie Newsome retired in 2018. Eric DeCosta has been solid, albeit unspectacular, in his role as GM ever since. His eight first-round selections without a single one in the bottom third of this list are the most of any team.
The Bills may have the most wins of any team this decade, but their recent first-rounders haven't gotten them there. That said, the jury is still very much out on Maxwell Hairston and, to a degree, Dalton Kincaid. Maybe that's why Brandon Beane survived what many thought would be a complete front-office overhaul after another divisional-round exit.
A sad fact of the Panthers' draft track record this decade is that they've made an NFL-leading five top-eight picks over that span. Their only non-premium pick was also one of the worst first-rounders in terms of true impact, as Xavier Legette has already been relegated to backup status.
Caleb Williams' inclusion in the bottom third of this list may be controversial, but through two seasons, he's been outplayed by both quarterbacks selected immediately after him despite having arguably the best supporting cast. I would be more receptive to arguments that Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze are too low. I'd even agree that they're both likely to end up higher if we redo this exercise in a couple of years. Because both were premium picks with relatively modest production, though, I couldn't justify ranking them higher at this point.
While the Bengals' draft track record has rightfully drawn criticism of late, they started the decade with two franchise-changing picks in back-to-back drafts. The duo of Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase has dragged one of the most underachieving franchises in sports to the forefront of the national conversation more often than not over the past half-decade. The Achilles' heel for Duke Tobin in the draft this decade has been the defensive side of the ball, where the Bengals simply can't find consistent quality starters.
The Browns didn't have a first-rounder from 2022-24, which made life difficult for GM Andrew Berry, especially with his first two first-rounders being misses. The Jedrick Wills pick is particularly haunting given that the best left tackle in the NFL, Tristan Wirfs, was still on the board. So far, though, Berry doesn't seem to have many regrets about passing on Travis Hunter, as it ultimately netted them both Mason Graham and KC Concepcion.
The Cowboys get the first round right more often than not. That's partly because they are one of the NFL's most willing franchises to take offensive linemen, specifically on the interior, that highly. It wasn't their offensive line picks, however, that earned them the distinction of being the only team with two of the top 10 decisions on this list. The CeeDee Lamb and Micah Parsons selections were easily two of the best non-top-10 picks this decade.
The Russell Wilson trade meant GM George Paton had fewer than his share of first-rounders, but he's used them well. Bo Nix and Patrick Surtain II have turned out as well as, if not better than, anyone could have hoped at the time. And Denver's lowest-rated pick of the bunch, Jerry Jeudy, was John Elway's parting gift as GM.
One of the underrated aspects of Brad Holmes' rampant success as GM has simply been volume. The Lions' eight first-rounders from 2020-25 were the second-most in the NFL, and there's only one true eyesore of the bunch in Terrion Arnold. Of course, this analysis also includes the disastrous Bob Quinn era, which featured the worst non-quarterback draft pick on this list in Jeff Okudah.
The Packers' first-round track record under Brian Gutekunst features one Jordan Love heat check and then a lot of meh. I'm not even sure the Packers know exactly what they have yet in the likes of Devonte Wyatt, Lukas Van Ness, Jordan Morgan and Matthew Golden. They do, however, know what they had in Quay Walker and Eric Stokes, which amounted to a resounding plea from Packers fans to stop drafting Georgia defenders.
It obviously helps your hit rate to have three of your four first-rounders be top-three picks, but Nick Caserio couldn't have done much better than C.J. Stroud, Will Anderson Jr. and Derek Stingley Jr. Those three picks have set the stage for three straight playoff seasons. It's the other first-round pick, though, that I'm sure Caserio would prefer people forget.
Chris Ballard's first-round draft track record matches the lackluster state of the Colts franchise over that span. He hit a home run with Tyler Warren, but at a relatively low-value position. He also had a catastrophic miss in Anthony Richardson at the most valuable position in the NFL. Ultimately, Ballard's constant struggles at quarterback and edge rusher have defined his GM tenure. His vaunted 2018 draft class feels like a lifetime ago for Colts fans.
Jags fans have been through enough that I don't have to rehash all nine first-rounders here. Even their biggest hit in Trevor Lawrence has been a disappointment relative to expectations. The two guys who could really turn this thing around, Brian Thomas Jr. and Anton Harrison, have both flashed big-time talent throughout their careers, but consistency will determine whether they reach the top third by the time their rookie contracts are up.
It should be hard to find elite players without a single pick inside the top 20 from 2020-25, but the Chiefs did just that with Trent McDuffie and maybe Josh Simmons as well. GM Brett Veach has shown he's far more than a one-trick pony who pushed for Patrick Mahomes. He's consistently found value at every stage of the draft.
Not only do the Raiders have the highest rate of picks in the bottom third, but they also had three of the bottom 15 on this list. That's almost hard to do. Tyree Wilson, Alex Leatherwood and Damon Arnette were all unplayably bad during their time with the Silver and Black, with none making…
author: Mike Renner

title: Agent's Take: How high can Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson take a resurgent RB market?
summary: After years of depressed salaries, the running back market has rebounded with deals for Christian McCaffrey, Saquon Barkley and others
full_text:
The running back market had taken an economic downturn until Christian McCaffrey signed a two-year, $38 million contract extension averaging $19 million per year with the San Francisco 49ers during the 2024 offseason. McCaffrey was already the NFL's highest-paid running back with a four-year extension, averaging $16 million per year, which he received from the Carolina Panthers in 2020. He remained the only running back legitimately averaging more than $14 million per year under the 2024 extension.
Saquon Barkley became the league's first $20 million running back in 2025 when he signed a two-year, $41.2 million extension with the Philadelphia Eagles . The deal had a then-record-high $36 million in fully guaranteed compensation at signing.
Derrick Henry subsequently signed a two-year, $30 million extension averaging $15 million per year with the Baltimore Ravens despite his high mileage and being 31 years old. Barring an injury, it was a certainty that Henry would easily eclipse the 2,500-career-carry mark during the 2025 season.
Three running backs landed deals for more than $14 million per year this offseason. Kenneth Walker III signed a three-year, $43 million contract worth up to $45 million through incentives with the Kansas City Chiefs as an unrestricted free agent. Breece Hall , who was kept off the open market by a $14.3 million franchise tag, signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal worth a maximum of $45.75 million through incentives to stay with the New York Jets .
De'Von Achane received a four-year, $64 million extension with $32 million in guarantees from the Miami Dolphins . Incentives make the deal worth up to $68 million. At $16 million per year, Achane is the NFL's third-highest-paid running back.
Six running backs make more than $14 million per year. There could be as many as nine by the time the regular season starts in early September.
Jonathan Taylor has entered the final year of a three-year, $42 million extension with the Indianapolis Colts , signed early in the 2023 regular season after acrimonious negotiations in which he requested a trade. He is likely looking for a new deal near the top of the running back market.
Taylor probably thinks his place in the running back salary hierarchy shouldn't be any lower in a new deal than in 2023. For all practical purposes, Taylor was the NFL's second-highest-paid running back. Alvin Kamara's $15 million-per-year extension with the New Orleans Saints included a fifth new contract year worth $25 million for cosmetic purposes, artificially inflating his average yearly salary. The deal averaged $12.5 million per year through the first four new years. Doing the same thing would mean Taylor getting more than McCaffrey's $19 million per year.
Taylor was coming off an injury-plagued 2022 season in which he rushed for a then-career-low 861 rushing yards while dealing with a terrible economic climate for running backs, when he got the $14 million-per-year deal. That isn't the case this time around.
Taylor was selected to the Pro Bowl for the third time in his six NFL seasons in 2025. He was also named first-team All-Pro by The Sporting News, one of the three media outlets approved by the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement for honors incentives. Taylor was third in the NFL with 1,585 rushing yards last season. He led the league with 20 total touchdowns (18 rushing and two receiving).
Taylor will be a prime candidate for a franchise tag if he doesn't sign a new deal. It will cost the Colts $18.7 million, given how the prior year's salary provisions work with franchise tags. That's 120% of Taylor's $15.562 million 2026 cap number.
Jahmyr Gibbs and/or Bijan Robinson should reset the running market when signing new deals. Both are dual-threat, former first-round running backs.
Robinson led the NFL with 2,298 yards from scrimmage (combined rushing and receiving yards) last season. It was the 12th-best single-season mark in NFL history. He also earned first-team All-Pro honors for the first time. Gibbs recorded the league's fifth-most yards from scrimmage (1,839) in 2025. He earned Pro Bowl honors on the original ballot for the second straight year.
Since the Detroit Lions are more proactive than the Atlanta Falcons with contract extensions for first-round picks, Gibbs seems more likely to get a new deal this year. The Lions have a recent track record of signing first-round picks to early contract extensions. Offensive tackle Penei Sewell and wide receiver Jameson Williams got new deals after their third NFL seasons in 2024 and 2025, respectively. Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson's extension came during the middle of his fourth year last season.
Typically, the Falcons give first-round picks new deals after their fourth NFL season. That's what happened in recent seasons with guard Chris Lindstrom , cornerback A.J. Terrell and wide receiver Drake London . Kyle Pitts , 2021's fifth overall pick, played out his five-year rookie contract and was designated a franchise player in February before signing a deal making him the NFL's third-highest-paid tight end at $17.7 million per year in June.
Gibbs and Robinson should be looking to become the NFL's first $25 million-per-year running backs, which would represent a dramatic market increase. Getting to that mark would be 21.36% more than Barkley's $20.6 million per year.
Coach Dan Campbell hasn't done the Lions any favors with his public comments about Gibbs. He said Gibbs is just scratching the surface of his talent and is an offensive weapon rather than just a runner at the NFL's annual owners meeting in late March. Gibbs should be poised for a career year with the Lions. Campbell acknowledged in June that Gibbs will be the bell cow running back with David Montgomery's trade to the Houston Texans in March. Gibbs' camp will surely try to use Campbell's comments to their advantage in contract talks.
Something Gibbs and Robinson could focus on is how first-round running backs who got new deals after three years were treated in their respective negotiations. Todd Gurley , Ezekiel Elliott and McCaffrey became the league's highest-paid running backs in 2018, 2019 and 2020.
Elliott's $15 million-per-year extension equates to just over $24 million per year in the current $301.2 million salary cap environment. McCaffrey's 2020 deal, adjusted for salary cap inflation, is little more than $24.3 million per year. Gurley's $14.4 million per year, when factoring in the 69.98% increase in the salary cap since 2018, is nearly $24.5 million per year.
Gurley, in particular, can be viewed as a cautionary tale for big-money extensions with first-round running backs. The Rams released Gurley in 2020 following a lackluster 2019 campaign in which he rushed for 857 yards, his career low at that time, while being slowed by left knee troubles. Gurley didn't play any of his new-contract years, since his four-year extension ran from 2020 through 2023. He made out like a bandit from the deal. Gurley was $20 million better off from the extension than playing out his rookie contract.
Another reference point is the running back market moving by an average of 11.2% the last three times a new salary benchmark was set. Barkley's deal was 8.42% more than McCaffrey's. McCaffrey bettered his 2020 extension by 18.63% in 2024. The 2020 extension was 6.77% more than Elliott's contract. Applying this 11.2% increase to Barkley's $20.6 million per year would be almost $23 million per year.
Regardless of how much Gibbs and Robinson ultimately raise the financial bar for running backs, expect the deals to have significantly more than Barkley's $36 million fully guaranteed at signing. There's a quirk with running back salary guarantees because of the Arizona Cardinals selecting Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft .
Since first-round rookie contracts are fully guaranteed and strictly determined by draft position, Love's $53 million is the most guaranteed money ever in a running…
author: Joel Corry

title: Deebo Samuel landing spots: Raiders, Colts among potential fits for former All-Pro WR
summary: Samuel remains one of the most notable wide receivers available as NFL teams open training camp
full_text:
Every year around this time, the NFL sees veterans pick new homes. There are plenty of notable wide receivers still out on the market. Tyreek Hill , Stefon Diggs , DeAndre Hopkins and Keenan Allen are still free agents, as is former Pro Bowler Deebo Samuel .
In his one season with the Washington Commanders , Samuel caught 72 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns. Those 727 yards receiving led the team, as fellow wide receiver Terry McLaurin and quarterback Jayden Daniels missed extensive time due to injuries. Maybe Samuel, at 30 years old, is no longer a dynamic threat capable of being named First Team All-Pro, but he's clearly still a weapon that can help any offense.
Samuel recently posted a video on his YouTube page and said that this time has been hard for him. He's still waiting for that right opportunity to pop up -- something he's "more than ready" for.
"I'm going on Year 8 … I still feel like I got a lot, at least like three, four good years left," Samuel said. "It's kind of been tough, not even going to lie to you. All the free agency stuff going on, waking up in the morning, looking at your phone, seeing if your agent hit you and was like, 'This team is interested,' or things along those lines. And it's been kind of like a roller coaster. Been through a lot, not just ball. With me and how I play this game it's just like no matter what I'm going through, no matter what I'm doing, if I'm able to perform, I'm going to go out there and put it on the line for my team."
Where could Samuel sign in the near future? Let's take a look at a few options.
This was a logical landing spot floated by CBS Sports analyst JP Acosta . The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the most-improved teams on paper. They added Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza to the quarterback room, then Kwity Paye , Quay Walker , Nakobe Dean , Taron Johnson and Treydan Stukes on defense.
Headlined by Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor , Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr , receiver may still be an area of weakness. Pairing a veteran slot weapon like Samuel with a veteran signal-caller like Cousins makes sense. As it stands, Brock Bowers is the only offensive weapon that can be relied on in Sin City.
The Indianapolis Colts looked like the best team in football for the first few weeks of the season with the motivated Daniel Jones under center and electric Jonathan Taylor toting the rock. However, this wide receiving group could use some help.
The Colts re-signed Alec Pierce with the largest contract in free-agency history for a wide receiver, but traded Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers . As it stands, Pierce, Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin are expected to be the starting wideouts. Downs has played primarily in the slot, but coach Shane Steichen admitted his team would look to play him more on the outside. Could that open the door for a veteran slot player?
This landing spot was recommended by CBS Sports' Mike Renner. Some would claim the Cincinnati Bengals have one of the best wide receiving corps in the NFL with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , but apart from those two pass-catchers, it's questionable. Andrei Iosivas is the No. 3, followed by players like Mitchell Tinsley , Charlie Jones and the rookie Colbie Young . Imagine Joe Burrow operating out of 11 personnel with Chase, Higgins and then Samuel running around in the slot.
If the San Francisco 49ers have no interest in bringing Samuel back, maybe he could sign with their chief rival in the Los Angeles Rams . Sean McVay has Puka Nacua and Davante Adams catching passes from reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford , but that didn't stop the Rams from showing interest in A.J. Brown this offseason. Samuel wouldn't serve as a major pillar for one of the best offenses in the NFL, but the perfect versatile playmaker to be sprinkled in on a well-timed reverse or third-and-short.
The Los Angeles Chargers ' offense is undergoing a major facelift with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. In his one season as the OC with San Francisco back in 2021, Samuel led the NFL with 18.2 yards per reception while racking up 1,770 yards from scrimmage and 14 touchdowns. It was Samuel's best NFL season, and a reunion with McDaniel could make some sense.
The Chargers have Ladd McConkey , Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris as their lead receivers alongside a fantastic tight end room that includes Oronde Gadsden II , David Njoku, and Charlie Kolar , but Samuel would just give McDaniel and Justin Herbert another weapon to utilize.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: MLB trade deadline predictions; Aaron Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season
summary: Plus, offseason grades for every NBA team in the Western Conference
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Football is right around the corner. Yesterday, we crossed the 50-day mark in the countdown to the NFL season. To celebrate the milestone, our Zach Pereles identified 50 lesser-known players who could help define the campaign . The unheralded contributors fell into six categories, from "under-recognized players ready to make a star leap" to "supporting a star."
The very first player that came to mind for this exercise was Bengals cornerback DJ Turner .
Here is one other player from every category that you should get to know over the next 49 days:
Quarterbacks were excluded from the list because of the high-profile nature of their position. We did not entirely leave them out of the conversation in our 50-day preview, though. Garrett Podell named the most overrated and underrated signal-callers heading into the campaign.
Yesterday, we shared our grades for every Eastern Conference team's offseason. Today, our focus shifts to the West . That's where the Clippers have shined over the first month of the summer with their flurry of trades and team-friendly free agency acquisitions. Everything is contingent on the Kawhi Leonard trade eventually going through, but assuming it does, this is an "A-" summer for Los Angeles, according to our Sam Quinn.
At the opposite end of the report card are the Trail Blazers, who built themselves a logjam in the backcourt. How are they going to find enough playing time and touches for everyone after trading for Ja Morant ? Each of Morant, Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson, Shaedon Sharpe and Deni Avdija need the ball in their hands to be effective.
Here's a taste of the other grades we handed out in the Western Conference:
The MLB trade deadline is now less than two weeks away, and it is still not fully clear which teams will buy and which will sell. There is no bigger domino that could potentially fall than Tigers ace Tarik Skubal . As disappointing as Detroit has been this year, it remains in the playoff hunt thanks to the weakness of the American League, and that reportedly has the front office thinking it should hold on to Skubal for the rest of the season.
Our baseball experts chimed in with predictions on where each of the trade deadline's biggest potential movers could land , and amid the Tigers' modest turnaround this summer, the majority of them now think Skubal will stick around in the Motor City. One of them, Mike Axisa, dissented and said the Dodgers will make an offer the Tigers cannot resist.
The panel only reached a consensus on one player, Aroldis Chapman , who looks destined to stay in Boston now that the Red Sox are in the midst of a historic 14-game winning streak and suddenly alive and well in the wild-card race.

title: Ranking the NFL rookie running backs best positioned for instant production
summary: From Jeremiyah Love in Arizona to late-round sleepers, we rank the five rookie running backs projected to make the biggest fantasy football impact
full_text:
Although Ashton Jeanty of the Raiders was the only running back selection in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft , nine rookies logged at least 100 carries last season. CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project just three to cross that threshold this time around.
From 2016-21, the NFL averaged 10 rushers with 1,000-plus rushing yards each season, which perhaps supported an overarching notion that the position was being devalued. Carries were being distributed more evenly among teams. Over the past four years, the league has averaged 15 rushers of at least 1,000 yards.
As part of the 2026 NFL Draft, there were only three running backs taken in the top-100 overall. Which rookie running backs will be the most productive in 2026? Here are five candidates:
There were some others who had been considered for the final spot, including Nick Singleton ( Titans ) and Adam Randall ( Ravens ).
There is a path for Coleman to receive a large share of Denver's carries. J.K. Dobbins has battled injuries throughout his career and R.J. Harvey may not possess the ideal size to be a feature back.
Coleman was the fourth-highest drafted running back in his class at No. 108 overall. He was proficient in the pass game while at Washington, which makes him a three-down back.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project Coleman to rush for 134 yards and one touchdown on 32 carries, equivalent to 25.4 fantasy points.
Washington was a favorite throughout the pre-draft process. He has size, burst and the capability to impact the game on all three downs. Last year's No. 6 overall selection, Ashton Jeanty, will be the bell cow for the AFC franchise, but Washington can be the thunder to Jeanty's lightning.
Jeanty had all but 41 of Las Vegas' running back carries last season, so one would think the new coaching staff will want to transfer some of the burden elsewhere. The Seahawks had two running backs with 180-plus carries last season.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project Washington to carry 97 times for 340 yards and two touchdowns, equivalent to 89 fantasy points.
There is a clear gap between the top two running backs and the rest of this list. Opportunity will dictate how the second tier shakes out.
The 49ers faced backlash over the selections of Ole Miss wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling and Black, prompting surly responses from Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch during press conferences. San Francisco may be inclined to funnel touches to Black in an effort to justify the selection, but past tendencies suggest it is an exercise in overthinking. San Francisco has used Day 2 selections on running backs Ty Davis-Price and Trey Sermon in the past. Those two players combined for 81 total carries during their brief careers in the Bay Area.
The franchise churns through running backs over the course of a regular season. Jordan James , Isaac Guerendo and Black are backups to Christian McCaffrey , who, aside from an injury-riddled 2024 season, has missed one total game in three of his last four seasons.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project Black as the third-highest scoring rookie running back with 592 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 152 carries, equivalent to 114.9 fantasy points.
Seattle employed a platoon system at the running back position with Zach Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III . Walker signed with the Chiefs in free agency, and Charbonnet suffered a significant late-season injury. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are capable of giving Price a breather until Charbonnet returns, but the rookie may get a larger volume of touches in September as a result.
Outwardly, it felt as though the Seahawks were willing to wait and take the Notre Dame product No. 32 overall despite better value existing elsewhere.
There have been 13 running backs drafted in the first round over the past 10 years. Of those, 12 played at least 13 games -- Omarion Hampton was the exception -- and averaged 1,181.2 yards and 8.2 touchdowns on 265.4 carries.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project 228 carries for 977 yards and eight touchdowns, as well as 20 receptions for 222 yards and one touchdown. His projected 187 fantasy points are the second-most among rookie running backs.
Arizona signed Tyler Allgeier and also returns James Conner . They have a few physical backs that can share some of the wear and tear with Love. The Cardinals received ample criticism for taking a running back rather than a premium position No. 3 overall. There may be motivation to quickly validate that decision. Although I did not view Love as being of similar caliber to Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs , he was among the best prospects available in what appeared to be a weak draft class at the top.
There have been six running backs taken in the top 10 overall over the last ten years. Those players averaged 144.8 carries for 636.4 yards and 4.6 touchdowns as rookies. Believe it or not, the inclusion of Christian McCaffrey brought those figures down harshly.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project 214 carries for 1,025 yards and eight touchdowns, as well as 42 receptions for 352 yards and two touchdowns; the equivalent of 232 fantasy points in a PPR league.
