title: Lions News: Detroit plummets in ESPN’s under-25 rankings
summary: For years, the Detroit Lions have been hailed as one of the teams with the most young and promising talent. After years of great drafts from general manager Brad Holmes, Detroit not only had blue-chip players, but blue-chip players that would be in Detroit for years and years to come. But is that era coming […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 04: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 4, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images For years, the Detroit Lions have been hailed as one of the teams with the most young and promising talent. After years of great drafts from general manager Brad Holmes, Detroit not only had blue-chip players, but blue-chip players that would be in Detroit for years and years to come. But is that era coming to an end? Aaron Schatz of ESPN ranked NFL teams by the amount of talent they had that is under 25 years old. After placing sixth in the rankings last year, the Lions fell all the way to 23rd. Per Schatz, the Lions only have a single blue-chip player under 25 years old: running back Jahmyr Gibbs. But he does mention some players who could take a big step toward being key fixtures in Detroit. “Wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa is also 24, while Blake Miller , a first-round rookie tackle, is 22,” Schatz wrote. “On defense, safety/nickelback Brian Branch will likely be back on the field after recovering from an Achilles tear when he turns 25 in October. Last year’s first-round pick, defensive tackle Tyleik Williams , is still 23. Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. , who has battled injuries, is 24, while second-round rookie edge rusher Derrick Moore is 23.” Of course, it’s worth noting that 25 years old is a pretty arbitrary cut-off, and it specifically hurts the Lions this year. That’s because Penei Sewell, Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta, Aidan Hutchinson Jack Campbell, and Kerby Joseph are all currently 25 years old. All of those players have the opportunity to play in Detroit for a long time and still have plenty of time left in their prime. At the same time, it does feel like this is a strike against the Lions’ two most recent draft classes. In 2024, the misses on Terrion Arnold, Ennis Rakestraw, and Giovanni Manu are starting to hurt. It’s far too early to judge the 2025 draft class, but if Tyleik Williams, Tate Ratledge, and Isaac TeSlaa don’t take Year 2 jumps, it could leave the Lions in a tough spot. Young, cheap talent is critical to offset Detroit’s aging and expensive core players. At this point, I wouldn’t put too much stock into this ranking given how much 25-year-old talent Detroit has. However, if they continue to plummet in these rankings in the years to come, there will be some serious questions to answer. title: Why Jared Goff believes Amon-Ra St. Brown is the NFL’s best WR
summary: ESPN just concluded it’s positional ranking series, the NFL is still counting down their top-100 players of the 2026 season, and our roster ranking is near its end. But Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff doesn’t care about any of those lists. He’s got his own list of NFL wide receivers, and it’s one person long. […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Jared Goff #16 and Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions celebrate a touchdown against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN just concluded it’s positional ranking series, the NFL is still counting down their top-100 players of the 2026 season, and our roster ranking is near its end. But Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff doesn’t care about any of those lists. He’s got his own list of NFL wide receivers, and it’s one person long. During an interview with NFL Network this week, Goff explained why he thinks there’s no better receiver in football than Amon-Ra St. Brown. “I think he’s the best wide receiver in the league,” Goff said. “I think he’s the only guy who catches with it, runs with it, blocks—does everything. He can do it all. It’s a lot of fun to work with him, play with him. The way he works in practice, he makes me want to give him the ball. He makes me want to reward him for all of his hard work. It makes everyone around him work harder. He’s such a great teammate, great player, great person, and I love playing with him.” Statistically, you can certainly make a case that St. Brown is one of the best receivers in football. Since 2022, among wide receivers, St. Brown ranks: 1st in receptions (457) 4th in receiving yards (5,340) 3rd in receiving touchdowns (39) On top of that, he’s tied for the most First-Team All Pro honors (two) and Pro Bowl nods (four) over that time. St. Brown’s value goes beyond his statistics and honors. As Goff points out, he’s also a model in practice that raises the bar for the entire team. And his blocking is among the best for a receiver. That checks out when looking at PFF blocking grades, as well. Last year, St. Brown ranked t-seventh among wide receivers in run blocking grade (70.0) and fourth in pass blocking (79.0—although on only five snaps). Despite all of those accomplishments, St. Brown is often not considered among the top-three receivers in the NFL. Players like Justin Jefferson, Ja’Marr Chase, and CeeDee Lamb regularly top St. Brown in annual rankings. Goff was asked why St. Brown doesn’t always seem to get the kind of credit he likely deserves. In typical Goff fashion, he returned the question back to sender. “I don’t know, man. That’s your guys’ job,” Goff said. You can catch Goff’s entire interview below: From The Insiders on @NFLNetwork : #Lions QB Jared Goff joined @wyche89 and @StaceyDales to give an outlook on his 2026 season and discuss some changes in Detroit. pic.twitter.com/aVq2Er3bHr — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 20, 2026

title: Top 10 players for the Detroit Lions’ 2026 season: Part 1 (10-6)
summary: We are finally cracking the top-10 players for the 2026 Detroit Lions season. As a reminder, this list was created by having eight different staff members rank the entire roster from 90 to 1 and averaging out each ballot to create a consensus list. This year’s top-10 includes nine players who made the same list […]
full_text: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) runs for a touchdown against Green Bay Packers during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Thursday, Nov. 27, 2025. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images We are finally cracking the top-10 players for the 2026 Detroit Lions season. As a reminder, this list was created by having eight different staff members rank the entire roster from 90 to 1 and averaging out each ballot to create a consensus list. This year’s top-10 includes nine players who made the same list last year. The one newcomer shot all the way into the top five. But for this article, we’re only tackling the players we ranked 10 through 6, all of whom made last year’s top-10. Previously: Players ranked 90-81 Players ranked 80-71 Players ranked 70-61 Players ranked 60-51 Players ranked 50-41 Players ranked 40-31 Players ranked 30-21 Players ranked 20-11 10. Alim McNeill (Highest: 7 Lowest: 13) Last year’s ranking: 9 McNeill drops only a spot after last year’s disappointing but understandable season. Many were eager for McNeill’s return from his ACL injury, and while that first game back provided some serious hope, it was clear Detroit’s star defensive tackle still wasn’t quite himself. He’s entering 2026 with a determination to prove he is still a top interior defender in this league, but with only a couple of seasons to show for it, there is some understandable skepticism—particularly after that 2024 ACL tear. 9. TE Sam LaPorta (Highest 7; Lowest: 10) Last year’s ranking: 8 LaPorta, too, drops a spot after an injury-hampered 2025 campaign. The outlook is much brighter for LaPorta, however, as he has been fully cleared of his back injury prior to training camp , and there’s no reason to believe he can’t return to form immediately. That said, back injuries very rarely just go away forever, so it’ll be something to monitor. Still, LaPorta was producing like a top-five tight end, and his blocking also took several strides prior to his injury. If he can put all of that together in 2026, he’ll not only likely climb toward the top-five next year, but there’s likely a contract extension waiting for him, as well. 8. S Brian Branch (Highest: 4; Lowest: 13) Last year’s ranking: 5 Continuing the theme of injuries causing a drop in the rankings, Brian Branch falls out of the top-five after tearing his Achilles late last season. Branch is not expected to be ready to start the season, and it wouldn’t be surprising to see him miss at least half of the year. That makes him a tough player to rank in this year’s countdown, especially since we have no idea how he’ll look in his first on-field action. But Branch is still widely respected for his ability to come down and defend the box, his instincts in the passing game, and his hard-hitting mentality. There’s a reason that despite his injury, NFL execs and coaches still have Branch as the No. 4 safety in the NFL . 7. WR Jameson Williams (Highest: 6; Lowest: 10) Last year’s ranking: 10 After taking yet another step, Williams climbs a few spots in our rankings. Last year, Williams set career highs in receptions (65), yards (1,117), and tied his career high in touchdowns (7). Statistically, that put him among the top-10 receivers in the league. Williams has gone from an inconsistent, big-play threat to a trusted, versatile player who has a very strong case for the best No. 2 receiver in the NFL. His developmental curve is one of the biggest I’ve personally witnessed, and there’s a belief he still has a lot left in the tank we haven’t seen. 6. QB Jared Goff (Highest: 5; Lowest: 12) Last year’s ranking: 7 So begins the annual tradition of debating whether Jared Goff is a top-five player on the team or not. On one hand, he’s produced statistically as a top-five quarterback in each of the last four seasons, and it’s hard to imagine someone being better or more important on the team than a top-five quarterback. On the other hand, Goff is generally not regarded as a top-five quarterback in the league, while the remaining players on this list (in no order: Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Penei Sewell, Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell) are all almost universally believed to be top-five players at their position. It’s a fun debate to have, but look at it this way: Detroit may have a top-five quarterback in the league, and the fact that our staff believes he may not be a top-five player on the team just shows how much ridiculous top-end talent this squad has.

title: Survey: How many receiving yards will Sam LaPorta have in 2026?
summary: Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host surveys for NFL fans, sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question centers around an important player returning from injury: Sam LaPorta. LaPorta burst onto the scene as a rookie, setting […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (87) makes a catch against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, November 2, 2025. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host surveys for NFL fans, sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question centers around an important player returning from injury: Sam LaPorta. LaPorta burst onto the scene as a rookie, setting multiple records for tight ends in franchise history, including registering 889 receiving yards for the season. In year two, LaPorta’s production was scaled back (726 receiving yards) as he focused on rounding out his overall game, which included stark improvements as a blocker. Last year, a significant back injury limited him to just nine games and 489 receiving yards before he was placed on injured reserve. LaPorta required surgery on his back, and questions surrounding his ability to fully recover swirled. In the spring, the Lions remained positive, and coach Dan Campbell told the media that the Pro Bowl tight end was “trending the right way” toward playing training camp. On Tuesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler confirmed expectations and reported that LaPorta had been “fully cleared (from injury) earlier this month” and that he was indeed on track to participate in training camp. Returning for 2026 healthy is terrific news for LaPorta, but the good news doesn’t end there for the fourth-year tight end. Waiting for LaPorta in Allen Park is new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, a coach with a lengthy history of featuring and elevating tight ends. Petzing spent the last three seasons in Arizona and quickly elevated the play of tight end Trey McBride. After a 2022 rookie season that saw McBride secure 265 receiving yards over 16 games (13 starts), Petzing helped raise his production to 825 receiving yards in 2023, 1146 receiving yards in 2024, and 1239 receiving yards in 2025. McBride was selected to the Pro Bowl each of the last two seasons and was a first-team All-Pro in 2025. With Petzing now in Detroit, expectations are sky high for LaPorta in 2026, including some publications suggesting a career year is on the horizon . Even McBride reached out to LaPorta to tell him how excited he should be to have Petzing in Detroit : “I was like, ‘Man, you’re going to love it. You’re going to eat, you’re going to have a great career,’ I’m excited for him.” While the hype train is certainly picking up some heavy steam this offseason for LaPorta, it’s important to keep in mind that McBride was the top target in the Cardinals offense, while LaPorta has to share the ball with several other terrific players in the Lions’ offense, including All-Pro wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. Ball distribution, along with maybe some lingering injury concerns, could be why FanDuel Sportsbook is listing LaPorta’s projected receiving yards at a moderate 650.5 (-114). And with that, it’s time to vote. Make sure to vote in the survey below, share your feedback in the comment section of this article or THE FEED post connected to the poll , and check back with Pride of Detroit later in the week for the results. If you want to get these surveys emailed to you weekly, you can sign up here , and don’t forget to check out FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

title: The 2025 Packers played a record-low number of possessions
summary: We’re only a week away from training camp, but we’re still finding out new information about the 2025 Green Bay Packers, if you can believe it. I’m sure the news that the Packers tried to keep their possessions low in 2025 isn’t going to be a shock to fans who watched the team’s games last […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 02: Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers in the game at Lambeau Field on November 02, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re only a week away from training camp, but we’re still finding out new information about the 2025 Green Bay Packers, if you can believe it. I’m sure the news that the Packers tried to keep their possessions low in 2025 isn’t going to be a shock to fans who watched the team’s games last year, but the rate at which they did so is eye-popping. Shoutout to Rich Hribar of Sharp Football Analysis, who unearthed this stat: The Packers’ 8.9 possessions per game (that didn’t end in kneeldowns) were the lowest rate of any team in any season since at least 1999. The 2025 Packers averaged 8.9 possessions per game that did not end in kneel downs. That is the fewest for a team in any season I have going back to 1999. — Rich Hribar (@LordReebs) July 17, 2026 This was a byproduct of multiple things: Green Bay wanting to operate a run-first offense, which ran time off the clock and led to long offensive drives. Green Bay playing a bend-don’t-break defense, which was a result of opposing offenses not wanting to do anything but throw quick game passes and run the ball when Micah Parsons was inserted into the lineup. Green Bay’s run defense fell short, which led to opposing offenses staying on the field for long drives. This might be the second-most telling stat of the 2025 Packers’ season, only behind the one below, which shows that Green Bay was essentially a top-5 defense in every major category over their first two drives of games in 2025 before they collapsed to one of the worst defenses in football from drive #3 and on: green: first two drives of every gamered: everything else — charles (young QB agnostic) mcdonald (@fourverts.bsky.social) 2026-01-09T23:04:12.420Z If we’re doing the autopsy of the 2025 Packers, it’s that they got worn out quickly on defense and opposing offenses were able to hold onto the ball at will, which led to extremely short-possession games. If Green Bay wants to continue to play this way, they either need to get much more efficient on offense (particularly in the run game) or need to be able to stop the run better in 2026.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Packers’ ‘young’ talent is starting to grow up
summary: For years the Packers have been one of the youngest teams in the NFL. They still are, but their young core — especially the ultra-young players — has begun to age up a bit. This is no longer baby’s first NFL season for most of the youngsters, who have grown into significant roles, by and […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles is tackled by Evan Williams #33 and Lukas Van Ness #90 of the Green Bay Packers in the fourth quarter during the NFC Wild Card Playoff at Lincoln Financial Field on January 12, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images For years the Packers have been one of the youngest teams in the NFL. They still are, but their young core — especially the ultra-young players — has begun to age up a bit. This is no longer baby’s first NFL season for most of the youngsters, who have grown into significant roles, by and large. But where does that leave the developmental group, the true young up-and-comers who are mostly potential at this point? If you ask ESPN, at least, it leaves the Packers pretty close to the bottom of the league. Our first link today has ESPN ranking the entire NFL by how strong their under-25 cohort of players are, and the Packers (spoiler alert) rank third from the bottom. The reasoning makes sense in the context of the piece: a lot of the true young talent has aged out of that bracket (Lukas Van Ness and Tucker Kraft, for instance), but it also dings the Packers for having young players that haven’t proven themselves yet…which is kind of the point of young players at the developmental stage of their career. After all, how do you get young stars? They have to be young non-stars first. That said, the Packers’ youngest players are pretty unproven. I think there’s good reason to be excited about Brandon Cisse and Chris McClellan from this year’s draft class, and I’m as high on Matthew Golden as anybody, but you can’t really get around the fact that none of them have really done anything yet. The whole book on Golden to this point is that he did very little as a rookie. There’s a lot of ground to cover for these guys. The better question might be how the Packers’ under-25 players will change over the course of the season. That’s a trend worth watching, and how it turns out could determine how the Packers’ season plays out. title: The Road to Perdition: How it could all go wrong for the 2026-27 Houston Texans
summary: To say that there are high expectations for the Houston Texans this season is to understate the obvious. After a less-than-satisfying end to a strong 2025-26 season, Houston did a lot to shore up the team strengths (re-signing/extending key defensive stalwarts) and spent a lot of draft capital/free agent dollars to try to once against […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: C.J. Stroud #7 and Calen Bullock #2 of the Houston Texans walk off the field after a 28-16 loss against the New England Patriots in the AFC Divisional Playoff game at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images To say that there are high expectations for the Houston Texans this season is to understate the obvious. After a less-than-satisfying end to a strong 2025-26 season, Houston did a lot to shore up the team strengths (re-signing/extending key defensive stalwarts) and spent a lot of draft capital/free agent dollars to try to once against improve the offensive line, as well as adding weapons via trade (David Montgomery). Houston will look to not only reclaim the AFC South Division title but to finally breakthrough the Division Round ceiling. There is a lot of reason for optimism. However, any Houston fan knows all too well that the negatives can easily come to the forefront. Promise and pressure can sometimes be too much. With that in mind, here are some pre-mortem causes should Houston’s season fails to live up to its hopes and dreams. The fall of CJ Stroud: No Texan entered the offseason facing more questions about his future than QB CJ Stroud. After a rookie season for the ages, Stroud has spent the last two seasons struggling to live up to that opening act. It is not as if he has been horrible, with playoff wins in each of his three seasons. It is also not as if it is all on him, as the team has struggled mightily to provide a consistently solid offensive line, leaving him with one of the worst run games in the league and under a significant amount of duress. However, if the adage “you are only as good as your last performance” is a truth, then Stroud left the world with the worst version of himself. That 4 INT performance in New England likely prevented him from signing a big contract extension. The team has not sat idly by, revamping the offensive line and bringing in better running back talent in David Montgomery. In theory, improvements in protection and the running game should only help Stroud and the offense writ large. Yet, what of the psychological? While Stroud’s sack numbers were down last season, his pressure rate was still among the worst in the league. Also, he had arguably two of his worst ever QB games in the two playoff game in Pittsburgh and New England. The season may start out well, but what happens after that first bad play? The first INT? Can he still shake it off and more forward, or will the negativity build on itself? If it does, and Stroud can’t get out of his own head, then all of the moves the team made will prove null and void. This would then begat some very difficult questions within Reliant Stadium about the future of Stroud and the franchise. The offense doesn’t help Stroud at all: There is always the possibility that the offseason offensive upgrade are not, in fact, upgrades. Branden Smith and Wyatt Teller, in theory, are superior OLs to the men they replaced. However, Smith is overcoming some significant injuries and Teller is not the same guard he was a couple of seasons ago. Ed Ingram arguably earned his extension, but what if his performance was a fluke? Also, the whole offensive line, even with Ingram and Ersary, was not all that great. Additionally, even as Caley did improve somewhat as a play-caller, he was far from perfect in his play-calls, and the offensive line coaching and performance may not completely improve. The running game is also tied into the Oline performance, but even then, the RBs are no sure bet. Montgomery should be a strong starter, but it is telling that Detroit let him go, as he had fallen behind Gibbs on the depth chart. What if Detroit dumped damaged goods on Houston? Marks showcased toughness most didn’t think he had, but he did not make it through a lot of games unscathed. Marks works better as a third-down/change-of-pace back. He could close out games, but he doesn’t profile as a back that can do that game in and game out for a long stretch of time. Maybe 2025-26 is different with a healthy Joe Mixon, but the team really needs Montgomery to be the best version of himself. The injury gods claim key defenders: Last season, Houston had arguably the best defense in the league. Their DE duo (Anderson and Hunter) terrorized QBs to no end, and the secondary of Stingley, Lassiter, Bullock and Pitre constituted their own no-fly zone. Aside from talent, a key reason was a lack of significant injuries to the defensive starters. Anderson finally played a full regular season, having missed games in his 1st two seasons. Of the main starters, only Pitre (3 games), Lassiter (1) and Al-Shaair (1), missed any games due to injury. Such fortune does not remain constant. The big reason why Houston’s defense was so dominant was that their best players, who are among the best at their respective positions, actually played. Take Anderson, Hunter, Stingley, Lassiter, et al off the field for multiple games, and it is likely that the squad would have seen a massive drop off in defensive performance. With so much of Houston’s hopes riding on that defense, their stars must stay on the field. If they suffer any significant injuries, especially to the main stars, that could upend a lot of assumptions, making Houston’s quest to move to the conference title game that much more difficult. Another bad start to the year. Last season, Houston got off to an 0-3 start. While remarkable that they went 12-2 to end the regular season, that is not something the squad can count on again. The schedule does not include the NFC West, but there are no shortages of challenges on the calendar. Houston does not exactly ease into the season, for while they have 3 of their first 4 games at home, those home games are against Buffalo, Cincinnati, and Dallas. Those games are winnable, but those teams possess some of the most dangerous offenses in the league. If the defense can’t find its footing and the offense is still playing like it is 2025, then the team could be looking at another bad start. Yes, Houston has bounced back from a 0-3, 1-4 type start to get the playoffs, but in a competitive AFC, that is not the path to long-term success. The Black Swan: Clearly, we don’t know what it might be. In retrospect, it will be obvious, but right now, it is hard to predict where the Black Swan event might hit, if it hits at all. Previous versions for this team involved everything from injuries from [KITTEN] to unexpected player legal woes to a pandemic to an over-his-head-not-good-with-power-football-Ayatollah-wannabe. However, one can’t discount a “Black Swan” occurrence. Could a season with high expectations disintegrate ala 2013? Always possible. This is not all-inclusive, nor a prediction of what will happen. However, if multiple conditions presented here happen, success might not be a part of the upcoming Texans’ season.

title: Chiefs News: KCK Mayor says Chiefs’ new stadium location still unknown

On Wednesday, renderings of what the new home of the Chiefs will look like were released. KCK mayor reacts to Chiefs stadium renderings, says exact location still unknown | KCTV5 Kansas City, Kansas Mayor Christal Watson said she is excited by the six renderings the Kansas City Chiefs released Wednesday of their planned domed stadium — but acknowledged she has no answers yet on where exactly within the Star Bond District the facility will be built. “The renderings look wonderful,” Watson said. “There’s this old and new look to them, keeping the integrity of Arrowhead, but yet this new little twist, which is the dome.” Watson said the city has no role in determining the stadium’s precise location within the financing district. Kansas City Chiefs Select Manica To Design New Domed Stadium | Forbes Fully enclosed with a translucent ETFE roof, Manica hopes to improve on many of the team’s traditions. The more than 20,000 parking spaces in the lot will be designed to specifically enhance the tailgating experience. The stadium’s size, shape and roof geometry were determined after audio engineers studied the design to maximize crowd noise. The seating bowl design is reminiscent of the current Arrowhead Stadium with a Drum Deck for celebrations and a prominent placement of the Chiefs Ring of Honor above the bowl. Preview every WR on the KC Chiefs’ 90-man roster before training camp | Chiefs Wire The Chiefs gave Remigio playing time as a kick/punt returner last year, but the experiment largely failed. As a receiver, Remigio only managed to record one reception for 24 yards in 2025. After those three (Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, in order), the next options are guys like Tyquan Thornton, fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen, backup tight end Noah Gray and Jalen Royals. In short, this team is not flush with pass-catching options, and if Patrick Mahomes can return healthy, someone’s going to have to step up, especially if Kelce really is over the age cliff and/or Rice can’t get his head on right. A longshot hope for spiral walkways World Cup fans learned just how fun that can be after a game, and Chiefs fans think it’s a big part of their gameday experience. “Spiral walkways with unnecessary cladding we can bang on before and after the game or I’m out,” one wrote. Wish they were never leaving, but if we’re gonna leave might as well do it right.” Around the NFL Seahawks’ Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 | ESPN According to a source, the Seahawks knew that Emmanwori might eventually require surgery. After returning from his initial ankle injury, Emmanwori emerged as a versatile playmaker and a key part of Seattle’s top-ranked scoring defense. title: 54 Days until Chiefs football, we are ‘Brian Waters’ days away
summary: We are 54 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 54 jersey was most recently worn by linebacker Leo Chenal, who signed a contract with the Washington Commanders in free agency this offseason. No one is assigned that number ahead […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - OCTOBER 22: Guard Brian Waters #54 of the Kansas City Chiefs points during the game against the San Diego Chargers on October 22, 2006 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. The Chiefs won 30-27. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are 54 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 54 jersey was most recently worn by linebacker Leo Chenal, who signed a contract with the Washington Commanders in free agency this offseason. No one is assigned that number ahead of Chiefs training camp, although it was the number linebacker Nick Bolton wore as a rookie. In franchise history, linebackers Tray Simien (1991 – 1997) and Damien Wilson (2019 – 2020) have made their marks as defensive starters in the uniform, but it’s an offensive lineman who represents the number in franchise lore: The all-time No. 54 in franchise history Brian Waters (2000 – 2010) Originally undrafted from North Texas in 2000, Brian Waters turned into the team’s starting left guard by the end of 2001. By 2004, he was a first-team All-Pro, the first of two such honors. He would go on to make six Pro Bowls and win the 2009 “Walter Payton Man of the Year” award. His coolest accomplishment, however, was earning the AFC Offensive Player of the Week award after the Chiefs beat the Atlanta Falcons 56-10 with eight rushing touchdowns in 2004. He started through the 2010 season, aiding that year’s team in winning the AFC West. He would go on to make a Pro Bowl with the New England Patriots as well. He was inducted into the Chiefs’ Ring of Honor in 2019. 54: The number of points accounted for by Kareem Hunt last season The eight touchdowns scored by running back Kareem Hunt accounted for 54 points, the most of any Chiefs player besides kicker Harrison Butker last season. Hunt is still a free agent at 30 years old; should he still be an option in the backfield by the time Kansas City gets to Week 1? With training camp starting this week, the team will be evaluating the new batch of running backs behind lead back Kenneth Walker. If the team is lacking the powerful, short-yardage skillset that made Hunt so reliable near the goal line and in short-yardage situations last year, should he return for those specific scenarios?

title: Chiefs with the highest career stakes this season: Felix Anudike-Uzomah
summary: In this series, we will look at established players — virtual locks to make this year’s Kansas City Chiefs squad — with the most riding on the 2026 season. On April 27, 2023, with the NFL Draft being held at Kansas City’s Union Station, the Chiefs announced a selection that had the look of a generational feel-good […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 15: Felix Anudike-Uzomah #97 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs onto the field at halftime against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 15, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images In this series, we will look at established players — virtual locks to make this year’s Kansas City Chiefs squad — with the most riding on the 2026 season. On April 27, 2023, with the NFL Draft being held at Kansas City’s Union Station, the Chiefs announced a selection that had the look of a generational feel-good story. Coming off of a victory months earlier in Super Bowl LVII, team chairman Clark Hunt took the stage to announce the final selection in the first round. Kansas State edge rusher Felix Anudike-Uzomah — a Lee’s Summit, Missouri, native who was actually in the hometown crowd that night — joined the Chiefs. Three years later, unfortunately, the move has aged poorly. Anudike-Uzomah was relegated to a rotational role over his first two seasons and delivered only three career sacks. He then missed his third season after a preseason hamstring injury a year ago. The Chiefs officially declined Anudike-Uzomah’s fifth-year option this spring, meaning he will become an unrestricted free agent after the season. Still only 24, Anudike-Uzomah suddenly finds himself playing to stay in the league for a fifth season, while the Chiefs are hoping the local product delivers at least partial dividends on the investment. As the roster currently stands, the team appears to have no choice but to give Anudike-Uzomah significant defensive snaps. Barring injury, veteran George Karlaftis will lead the team in edge-rush snaps. He will presumably be joined in the starting lineup by second-year pro Ashton Gillotte, who took at least half the defensive snaps in Kansas City’s final five games last season. The Chiefs added rookie R Mason Thomas in this year’s draft, but he will likely be limited to obvious pass rush snaps early in his career. Several veteran edge rushers remain unsigned and may simply plan to sign after some of the hot summer training camp practices have passed. The Chiefs could very well plan to add a veteran defensive end, similar to adding Carlos Dunlap early in 2022’s camp. Without such a move, Anudike-Uzomah by default appears set to blow past the 31% of defensive snaps he played in 2024. Even if he doesn’t break out in his fourth season, Anudike-Uzomah will probably latch on somewhere in the NFL for 2027. The 2022 draft class can show us why. Of 2022’s first-round selections, 13 had their fifth-year option declined (or had been previously released from their rookie contract). Despite entering free agency earlier than expected, 11 of those players are currently signed to NFL rosters. This includes current Chiefs cornerback Kaiir Elam, the class’s 23rd overall selection to the Buffalo Bills . Seven such first-rounders from 2021 — including Chiefs backup quarterback Justin Fields — are still hanging on. From the 2020 draft, 11 first-round selections who had their fifth-year options declined remain on team rosters. One player from 2020 offers hope for Anudike-Uzomah, despite the woeful start to his career. Former LSU pass rusher K’Lavon Chaisson — the 20th overall selection — underwhelmed in four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars . After totaling just five sacks on his rookie contract, Chaisson has gotten to the quarterback 12.5 times over his past two seasons split between the Las Vegas Raiders and the New England Patriots . The Washington Commanders rewarded the once-notorious draft bust this offseason with an $11.5 million contract for 2026. Similar to Anudike-Uzomah, Chaisson entered the league at a very young age and will play his seventh season at only 27 years old. Pass rushers generally get several opportunities to extend their careers because of the lack of talent at the position. Even so, most perceived draft busts never share the label, making Chaisson a rare exception. If Anudike-Uzomah will find a similar modest career turnaround, it would certainly be helpful if it came for his original team instead of at his next stop. What happens in 2026 will determine if Anudike-Uzomah is offered a moderate amount of guaranteed salary for 2027 or has to prove himself on a veteran minimum agreement. His performance in the early stages of the Chiefs’ training camp and preseason may also determine how aggressively the team searches for reinforcements at defensive end.

title: Chiefs News: Is 2026 ‘The Last Dance’ for Travis Kelce?
summary: The latest There was a stretch of time earlier this offseason when it was unclear whether Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce would be returning to the field or retiring from the sport. That has been cleared up since with a one-year deal, but it’s hard to imagine the same scenario playing out next […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) warms up an NFL game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Sept. 28, 2025, at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. (Emily Curiel/Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest There was a stretch of time earlier this offseason when it was unclear whether Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce would be returning to the field or retiring from the sport. That has been cleared up since with a one-year deal, but it’s hard to imagine the same scenario playing out next year. If the 2026 season already felt like the final chapter in Kelce’s career, the team around him only added to that narrative with an Instagram post. Travis Kelce’s Longtime Trainer Drops Major Hint About His NFL Future | Sports Illustrated It was Carter’s message across the image, however, that immediately commanded attention. “Andrew and I started with Travis before his rookie year in the NFL,” Carter wrote. “Know the [GOAT] is preparing for THE LAST DANCE. Next stop Canton/HOF.” Kelce has not announced that the 2026 season will be his last. Still, the deliberate “Last Dance” reference, coupled with Carter’s mention of the Pro Football Hall of Fame, made the post difficult to dismiss as an ordinary training-camp tribute. Chiefs to Host Training Camp Kingdom XP Video Gaming Pop-Up Event | The Mothership Fans will have the opportunity to test their skills with five stations, including over 40 consoles featuring premier titles such as Madden, Mario Kart, Super Smash Bros., and others, along with two racing simulators, for a chance to compete for prizes. Additionally, fans will have the opportunity to challenge gaming influencers, including Adrian Armour, BigCamIAm, The Epitome KC, Rhido, Equus, and Jay Todd Talks in 1-on-1 Fortnite battles. Fans can access the Kingdom XP Video Gaming Pop Up with their training camp tickets, which are reserved on a first-come, first-served basis. For more information, visit www.chiefs.com/trainingcamp. NFL offseason power rankings: No. 12 Kansas City Chiefs get to answer whether their dynasty is over | Yahoo! Sports In 2024, the Chiefs went 11-0 in games decided by seven points or less, counting playoffs, and 6-0 in games decided by three or less. They set an NFL record for consecutive wins in one-score games. Then, last season, their record was 1-9 in games decided by seven points or less and 1-6 when games were decided by three or less. While regression is a real thing, that big of a shift makes no logical sense. Kansas City Chiefs’ offensive players with the most to gain (or lose) during 2026 NFL training camp in St. Joe | A to Z Sports Brashard Smith, a former wide receiver turned running back, might have the most to lose. He was the only holdover in a room that has been transformed under DeMarco Murray and Eric Bieniemy. Smith was tasked with adding strength this offseason, and the question remains whether the coaching staff envisions him as a running back with a defined role or a tweener stuck between a murky receiver competition and a fierce backfield battle. Chiefs Rookie WR Put on Notice Ahead of Training Camp | Heavy Sports During a July interview with 32BeatWriters, KSHB 41 Chiefs media member and producer Nick Jacobs was very honest about what he saw from Caldwell this spring. “Caldwell hasn’t really stood out yet,” Jacobs began, putting the rookie on notice. “I mean heightwise, he’s obviously the tallest receiver there,” the KC reporter continued. “He looks like a tight end in terms of height, but in terms of him kind of separating himself right now, that hasn’t necessarily occurred.” Around the NFL John Harbaugh on Cam Skaettebo’s botched backflip: ‘Dude, at least stick it’ “My reaction was — I haven’t talked to him yet; I’m going to talk to him, I’m sure. My reaction was this: Dude, at least stick it. I mean, land the thing if you’re going to do it, you know?” Harbaugh said, chuckling. “That was my first reaction.” It’s easy for Harbaugh to make jokes after Skattebo came out of the flub unscathed. If an injury occurs during his next backward spin, it would be no laughing matter – something surely the coach will express when he does talk to the running back about the incident. Dolphins, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension | ESPN We’re going to take a flier on Fulton, who was impressive under Jesse Minter with the Chargers in 2024 before earning a two-year, $20 million deal with the Chiefs in free agency. Injuries cost him most of his debut season in Kansas City, though it never seemed that he persuaded defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo to give him more significant playing time. The Chiefs are rebuilding their cornerback room, but I’d expect Mansoor Delane, L’Jarius Sneed and Nohl Williams to be the top three options, opening up the opportunity to add Fulton or former Dolphins starter Kader Kohou to this lineup. Karl Ravech, Tom Pelissero among ESPN layoffs in latest round of cuts: Sources | The Athletic On Monday, ESPN laid off NFL analyst Ryan Clark as part of the cuts. ESPN declined further comment. ESPN also severed ties with former NFL MVP Cam Newton, longtime SportsCenter stalwart David Lloyd, injury expert Stephania Bell, former All-Pro linebacker and talk show host Bart Scott, as well as NFL Network analyst Charles Davis. News of the Bell, Lloyd and Scott layoffs were first reported by Front Office Sports; Outkick initially mentioned the Newton decision. Chiefs special teams coordinator Dave Toub highlighted Johnson as a player to watch in the return game last month, saying that he was excited to see how Johnson fit in with the new kickoff rules in the NFL. title: 3 Chargers questions to answer during training camp
summary: Chargers rookies report to training camp this week! It’s time to get excited! Here are three questions I’ll be looking to get answers to when the entire team gets together and things start rolling next week. 1.) Who will win the starting left guard spot? Through OTAs and mandatory minicamps, it has been free-agent signing […]
full_text: Jun 17, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers center Jacob Spomer (left) and guard Kayode Awosika (74) participate in blocking drills during minicamp at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Chargers rookies report to training camp this week! It’s time to get excited! Here are three questions I’ll be looking to get answers to when the entire team gets together and things start rolling next week. 1.) Who will win the starting left guard spot? Through OTAs and mandatory minicamps, it has been free-agent signing Kayode Awosika who has received the lion’s share of the snaps with the first team at left guard. Behind him, rookie Jake Slaughter has been the left guard for the second team while also seeing snaps at center. Trevor Penning, a holdover from last year’s group, was not present for much of the offseason and when he was, he was with the third-stringers. Now what we’ve seen so far does not necessarily mean that that will stay the case once training camp gets rolling. Jake Slaughter was not ever going to stick with the ones the moment he was drafted. He hasn’t played guard since high school and for the sake of a smooth offseason program, it’s likely that Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel let Awosika take the snaps with the ones to let Slaughter take his time getting into the swing of the new position. The thing is, there’s a real shot that Awosika actually does stick with the ones and ultimately win the starting job in camp. He has experience in a similar offensive system when he was with the 49ers playing for Kyle Shanahan. Slaughter looks like a perfect fit on paper for McDaniel’s offense, but the Chargers can’t have any wasted time for him to get ahead of the curve. That doesn’t mean Slaughter won’t END the season as the starter, but to coming out of the gates for a campaign expected to carry a ton of hype for the Chargers, the offense most certainly needs to avoid any hiccups as they begin their first season under a new play-caller. 2.) How will the snap split work out in the backfield? Omarion Hampton is set to the Chargers RB1 in McDaniel’s offense. The hope is that he stays healthy for an entire season en route to what could be one of the most-productive rushing seasons for a Chargers running back since Austin Ekeler had 1,677 yards from scrimmage and 18 total touchdowns during the 2022 season. It’s a foregone conclusion that Hampton will lead the backfield in snaps, but Kimani Vidal showed he can tote the rock when needed and the team added former Ravens speedster Keaton Mitchell in free agency. Mitchell is a better fit for being a changeup back in McDaniel’s zone run scheme, that’s for sure, but that doesn’t mean that Vidal is just going to be cast aside. He broke his fair share of runs outside the tackles in 2025 so the abilities to perform his new duties has been shown already. If I know McDaniel well enough, he’s going to be thinking about PLAYERS more than he’s going to think about faceless plays. He will know which plays to get the most out of Hampton, Vidal, and Mitchell. He’ll do everything in his power to set up each of them with the best chance of success in a given situation. Now, if I was a guessing man, I would actually guess that after Hampton, it will be Mitchell to get the second-most snaps. McDaniel will not shy from trying to break off a home run intermittently while Hampton is grinding down the defense over the course of a drive. 3.) How will Genesis Smith fit into the safety? Smith was drafted in the fourth round of this year’s draft and while he enters a fairly full safety room, that’s a high enough of a draft placement to lead you to believe he’s expected to see the field as a rookie. His skillset ultimately sets him apart from the top four players ahead of him on the depth chart. He’s a lengthy centerfielder who can and should only play in the deep parts of the field. The other four — Derwin James, Elijah Molden, Tony Jefferson, and R.J. Mickens — can all move around the defense if needed. But, neither aside from James have the athleticism to be a single-high player for an entire game. That’s why I like Smith to find his way onto the field earlier than expected. But, that’s with the assumption he can clean up his tackling. Do you all remember JT Woods? All the athleticism he dripped that Brandon Staley raved about when he was selected in the third round? He was beyond a liability as a tackler and that’s why his NFL career was so short-lived. I have a feeling that Joe Hortiz has a better eye for that position than Tom Telesco did. At the end of the day, I can see a clear picture for Smith with the Chargers. Whether Chris O’Leary sees the same thing remains to be seen, however.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 27: Troy Dye #43 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates a play against the Houston Texans during the third quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on December 27, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Basics Height: 6’3 Weight: 231 pounds College: Oregon Experience: 6 Troy Dye is a born-and-bred California boy who grew up in Norco, CA and attended Norco High School. There, he was a productive safety, racking up over 200 tackles and five interceptions across his junior and senior seasons. He’d graduate as a three-star prospect who earned First-Team All-CIF and All-State honors before committing to play his collegiate ball at the University of Oregon. Dye saw the field right away for the Ducks as he started nine of 11 games in 2016. He led the team with 92 total tackles to go with 13 tackles for loss 6.5 sacks, an interception, and one pass breakup. The 2017 season saw him start all 13 games, leading the team once again with 107 tackles. He also posted a new career-high 13.5 tackles for loss with four sacks, another pick, four pass breakups, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovered for a touchdown. The 2018 saw Dye lead Oregon in tackle for the third-straight season as he racked up a new career-high 115 stops to go with eight tackles for loss, a pair of sacks, one more interception, and a career-high seven pass breakups. Dye would end his career with a 2019 campaign that ended in a Rose Bowl Defensive MVP award after helping the Ducks topple Wisconsin alongside now- Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. He’d finish the year with 84 tackles, 9.5 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, two picks, four pass breakups, and two forced fumbles. Following the season, Dye would go on to be selected in the fourth round by the Minnesota Vikings in the 2020 NFL Draft . In four years with the Vikings, Dye has been a core special teams player while maintaining a rotational role on defense. From 2020-2023, he’s accumulated eight total starts while playing in 60 total games. His career statistics currently sit at 80 total tackles, one tackle for loss, one sack, two pass breakups, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. On March 18, 2024, Dye signed a free agent contract to join the Chargers. In his first year with the Bolts, Dye started five games out of 17 games played (tying a career high) and turned that into a career-high 57 tackles with two tackles or loss and 1.5 sacks. This past season, Dye started a new career-high seven games while filling in for the injured Denzel Perryman. He turned in 58 total tackles and five tackles for loss (both career highs) with a sack, four pass breakups, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. The Good Dye has been a very reliable backup for the Chargers which has been huge given the injuries that have hit the position in recent years. He’s also a contributor on special teams which truly raises his value to a higher level than most backups on the team. Dye makes up for lack of ideal size with sideline-to-sideline athleticism that helps him stay around the football whenever he’s on the field. The Bad Dye has been at his best when coming off the bench. His play does not age well the more snaps he plays in a single game. Per Pro Football Focus, in the four games in which Dye graded at a 80.0 or higher, he played 14 or less snaps in three of them. In the one outlier, he played 38 snaps. 2026 Outlook Dye is a lock to make the Chargers’ final roster, whether or not Junior Colson returns from injury 100 percent. With how much time Colson has missed in his first two seasons, Dye should be set squarely as the team’s third linebacker behind Daiyan Henley and Denzel Perryman.

Stetson Bennett is currently the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Jimmy Garoppolo #11 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on before the NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It seems Aaron Donald is not the only ex-member of the Los Angeles Rams that is considering unwinding his retirement. Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reported that Jimmy Garoppolo is open to playing in 2026 after mulling hanging up his cleats this spring. From The Insiders: Jimmy Garoppolo considered retirement this spring but is very much open to playing this season in the right situation. Nothing imminent but he’s an experienced, veteran QB available for a team that might need one in the near future. pic.twitter.com/Q60E9tFCXD — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) July 22, 2026 The Rams could still use Garoppolo’s services. Stetson Bennett is currently the primary understudy to Matthew Stafford in a year when expectations for LA are Super Bowl or bust. Bennett has never taken a regular season snap. Garoppolo brings a seasoned resume that can keep the team afloat if Stafford misses extended time. One complication is the fact that Los Angeles drafted Ty Simpson in the first round this spring. Garoppolo may not want to join a quarterback room where he is in danger of losing playing time to a highly drafted rookie. There could be more appealing options for the veteran once training camp gets underway. Each year there is a notable preseason injury or lackluster training camp performance that could open a path to playing time for someone like Garoppolo. They say good things come to those that wait, and that is generally true for free agent quarterbacks in July and August. Is Garoppolo’s reconsideration of retirement a positive development for the Rams? Yes, especially if they have concerns about Bennett’s ability to step in for Stafford. LA can easily move on from Bennett in favor of a quarterback with a wealth of starting experience. Are the Rams the most attractive destination for a quarterback who is nearing the end of his career and probably wants a chance to play? Well, that answer is more complicated after the addition of Simpson. Stay tuned at Turf Show Times for any updates on Garoppolo and training camp. Players report later this week.

title: The Rams are the only NFL team to win championships in 3 different cities
summary: No matter where they go, the Rams have always found success: The Cleveland Rams won the NFL Championship in 1945, the St Louis Rams won the 1999 championship in Super Bowl XXXIV, and the Los Angeles Rams won the 2021 championship in Super Bowl LVI. No other franchise has ever won a championship in three […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - January 01: before the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium on Friday, Jan. 1, 2021 in Inglewood, CA.(Wally Skalij / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) No matter where they go, the Rams have always found success: The Cleveland Rams won the NFL Championship in 1945, the St Louis Rams won the 1999 championship in Super Bowl XXXIV, and the Los Angeles Rams won the 2021 championship in Super Bowl LVI. No other franchise has ever won a championship in three different cities. How did the Rams go there and get here? The Cleveland Rams were founded in 1936 by attorney and businessman Homer H. Marshman and former Ohio State player-coach Damon “Buzz” Wetzel as part of the second American Football League and joined the NFL in 1937. Nine years later, on December 16th, the Rams defeated the Washington Redskins 15-14 while playing in front of the home crowd. A temperature of −8 °F led to a low-scoring game, and a play that prompted a significant rule change provided the margin of victory. Washington had the ball at their own 5-yard line when Hall of Fame QB Sammy Baugh dropped back to pass, but the ball hit the goalpost, which, in those years, was situated right on the goal line, and fell back into the end zone, resulting in a safety and two points. It was the margin of victory in a one-point game. The St. Louis Rams In 1946, the Rams moved from Cleveland to Los Angeles, where they played until the end of the 1994 season. They then moved to St. Louis, where five years later, the Greatest Show on Turf under head coach, Mike Martz, wreaked havoc on NFL defenses for the next three years. During that time, they rewrote numerous offensive records, had three MVPs-QB Kurt Warner with two, and RB Marshall Faulk with the other. The team also made two Super Bowl appearances, winning one. In 1999, the Rams won Super Bowl XXXIV. They barely hung on to win by a score of 23-16 to beat the Tennessee Titans. When I say barely hung on, it came down to a 73-yard bomb to Isaac Bruce in overtime, followed by Titans receiver Kevin Dyson being stopped two feet short of the goal line as time expired—one of the most exciting games ever. After the 2015 NFL season, the team sought and received approval from the other owners to move back to Los Angeles in time for the 2016 NFL season. It was, to say the least, heartbreaking for the St Louis fans, many of whom remain bitter to this day. On to Los Angeles In 2016, under Jeff Fisher, the Rams traded significant draft capital to select Jared Goff. After a dismal start, the Rams fired Fisher as head coach 13 games into the season. That’s where Sean McVay comes in. In McVay’s first two years, he made the playoffs, ultimately losing in SB LIII, a significant turnaround, but Goff couldn’t deliver everything McVay wanted from him, and the team missed the playoffs the following year. Back in the playoffs in 2020, they were summarily dispatched by the Green Bay Packers. McVay had had it with Goff, and one of the biggest offseason trades ever went down that winter, leading to the acquisition of Matthew Stafford. 2021 was the culmination of a career spent toiling for the Detroit Lions, one of the worst franchises in the game, for Matthew Stafford. Finally hooking up with a coach who could unlock his talents, Stafford blossomed. It was as if he and McVay had some kind of Vulcan mind meld the way they both saw the game. In terms of symbiotic relationships, this is the poster child. It seemed like destiny that the Rams would go on to win Super Bowl LVI in their home stadium. In a classic game, they beat the Cincinnati Bengals 23-20 But you probably knew that.
author: John Newman

title: Will Braden Fiske ask for a trade if Aaron Donald returns?
summary: Braden Fiske was selected by the Los Angeles Rams as the second piece to usher in the post-Aaron Donald era. After Donald’s retirement, the Rams immediately invested premium draft capital in rebuilding the defensive line, pairing Fiske with Kobie Turner as two of the franchise’s foundational interior defenders. But what if that transition never truly […]
full_text: Braden Fiske was selected by the Los Angeles Rams as the second piece to usher in the post-Aaron Donald era. After Donald’s retirement, the Rams immediately invested premium draft capital in rebuilding the defensive line, pairing Fiske with Kobie Turner as two of the franchise’s foundational interior defenders. But what if that transition never truly happened? What if Donald decides to return for this season? While the possibility still remains, it raises an intriguing question: would Braden Fiske welcome the opportunity to play alongside arguably the greatest defensive tackle in NFL history, or would he seek a trade if it significantly reduced his role? There are compelling arguments on both sides. Why a trade request won’t happen… The most obvious reason is also the simplest: very few young defensive tackles would pass up the opportunity to learn from Aaron Donald. Donald wasn’t just an elite player—he redefined what the position could be. His preparation, practice habits, hand usage, leverage, conditioning, and relentless pursuit of perfection have been praised by teammates and opponents throughout his career. For a player entering just his third NFL season, spending every day alongside Donald could accelerate Fiske’s development more than any amount of playing time elsewhere. Even if Donald reclaimed a starring role, Fiske would still benefit from seeing firsthand how the future Hall of Famer studies film, prepares during the week, and attacks offensive linemen on Sundays. That type of mentorship cannot be replicated. The other reason is that the Rams suddenly have one of the deepest defensive fronts in football with Donald, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, and Poona Ford. Rather than forcing someone into a reserve role, defensive coordinator Chris Shula could become more creative with his personnel packages. The Rams could frequently deploy four defensive tackles across the line against run-oriented offenses. Turner has already shown enough athleticism to align at multiple spots, while Donald has historically played anywhere from defensive tackle to defensive end depending on the matchup. Fiske’s motor and versatility also make him capable of handling multiple alignments. Instead of taking snaps away from one another, the Rams could simply rotate four starting-caliber defensive tackles throughout the game, keeping everyone fresh over a 17-game season. Considering how physically demanding the position has become, reducing individual snap counts may actually improve overall production while limiting injuries. If the Rams successfully expanded their defensive packages, Fiske could still receive plenty of meaningful snaps while simultaneously learning from Donald. Why a trade request could happen… The opposite scenario is just as realistic. If the Rams continue operating primarily out of the same base and nickel defenses they used last season, someone has to leave the field. Donald, Garret, Young, and Turner would likely be locked into starting roles. Poona Ford was signed to stabilize the run defense and has proven himself as one of the league’s better interior run defenders. That leaves Fiske potentially becoming the odd man out despite being one of the organization’s recent premium draft investments. For a young player still trying to establish himself, losing hundreds of defensive snaps could significantly impact his development and future earning potential. NFL players understand that production leads to contracts. Heading into what would eventually become Year 3, Fiske could begin looking around the league and realize another franchise may be willing to make him a full-time starter. Rather than serving as a rotational piece behind one of the greatest defensive lines ever assembled, he could maximize his value elsewhere before becoming extension-eligible. That doesn’t necessarily mean Fiske would be unhappy with the Rams. It simply reflects the business side of the NFL. Players entering their prime often prioritize opportunities to prove they can handle every-down responsibilities, especially before negotiating a second contract. If Los Angeles isn’t willing to adjust its defensive structure to maximize all four interior defenders, requesting a trade could become a logical career decision rather than an emotional one. Braden Fiske might be the odd-man out of the defensive line-up if Aaron Donald unretires to re-join the Rams in 2026. 📸 Gary A. Vasquez, Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images https://t.co/lMqy5M9VPN pic.twitter.com/oxE8vkvxzY — Rams Wire (@TheRamsWire) July 9, 2026 Verdict Whether Braden Fiske would request a trade ultimately comes down to one question: How much would Aaron Donald’s return impact Braden Fiske’s role? If the Rams evolve their defense to consistently feature Donald, Turner, Fiske, and Ford together while maintaining meaningful playing time for all four, there may not be a better environment for Fiske’s long-term growth. Learning from Donald while competing on a championship-caliber defensive line could be the ideal situation. However, if Donald’s return simply pushes Fiske to the sideline in traditional personnel groupings, the conversation changes dramatically. A talented young defensive tackle with starting potential may eventually decide that the best way to maximize his career is somewhere that offers both opportunity and snaps. My prediction is that Braden Fiske stays with the Rams. Donald’s return would likely only be for one year. Fiske still has two years remaining on his rookie contract. They can’t afford to part with Fiske without receiving plenty of compensation. Doing so would leave a significant void at the defensive tackle position in 2027.
author: Steven Ridings

title: McVay addresses Aaron Donald rumors
summary: The Los Angeles Rams won’t know if Aaron Donald is returning until Aaron Donald makes a final decision, but head coach Sean McVay is clearly ready to welcome the defensive tackle back with open arms if he wants to play in 2026. After weeks of speculation that Donald could return to the Rams following the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 22: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay and Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams during the third quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at SoFi Stadium on October 22, 2023 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams won’t know if Aaron Donald is returning until Aaron Donald makes a final decision, but head coach Sean McVay is clearly ready to welcome the defensive tackle back with open arms if he wants to play in 2026. After weeks of speculation that Donald could return to the Rams following the trade for Myles Garrett, McVay sounded like Vin Diesel talking about family in the Fast and the Furious movies when he was asked about AD’s potential un-retirement : “ I have crossed paths with Aaron Donald ,” McVay said in an interview with Jason LaCanfora of The Daily Flock podcast. “What’s special is, we have a really special relationship. It’s way bigger than football. I’ve heard him say it before and it means the world to me — and I feel the same — it’s family with us. He’s done so much for me. I love the man he is. I love the husband, the father, the son — he represents a lot of the things that are right. “And what he’s going to do is, he is thinking about this. He’s going to go through his process. And the one thing about Aaron Donald is, what he does, he does it full speed ahead.” Donald has not played since 2023 and his $30 million pending paycheck could be another obstacle to clear before he suits up for the Rams again . Adam Schefter also reported on Wednesday that no decision by Donald is expected any time soon . The wait could drag on for weeks, maybe months, but if Donald feels like his body is ready for the game again, we know that McVay is ready to welcome him back into the family. One quarter mile at a time.
