title: Colby Parkinson’s late-season surge can carry over into 2026
summary: Following a quiet start to his Los Angeles Rams tenure, tight end Colby Parkinson broke out over the second half of last season. Parkinson’s breakout was a welcome sight for Rams fans, yet can he maintain his strong production moving into the 2026 campaign? The reason Parkinson can maintain his production is that he’s received […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Colby Parkinson #84 of the Los Angeles Rams stiff arms Derick Hall #58 of the Seattle Seahawks as he runs with the ball during an NFC Championship NFL football game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a quiet start to his Los Angeles Rams tenure, tight end Colby Parkinson broke out over the second half of last season. Parkinson’s breakout was a welcome sight for Rams fans, yet can he maintain his strong production moving into the 2026 campaign? The reason Parkinson can maintain his production is that he’s received more opportunities in Hollywood in the passing game than he did in his first four years in Seattle. In his final two years with the Seahawks, he was targeted 68 times, compared to 105 times with L.A. Parkinson had the best season of his career in 2025 after taking advantage of Tyler Higbee being out of the lineup, which heavily contributed to his breakout. From Weeks 12-17, when Higbee was sidelined, he had 24 receptions on 32 targets for 249 yards and four touchdowns. That compares to his 15 receptions on 17 targets for 123 yards and two receiving touchdowns, with Higbee mainly in the lineup from Weeks 1-11. Parkinson went from being largely forgotten in the Rams offense to becoming one of Matthew Stafford’s go-to guys outside of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Much of that was attributed to his elite production in the red zone. According to Rams.com staff writer Wyatt Miller , Parkinson ranked first team-wide in red zone catches (15) and yards (118), and trailed Adams in touchdowns (six) and targets (22) inside the 20. Adams was a known threat in the red zone last season, yet that helped the Rams’ TE fly under the radar so often. He was additionally a major threat in yards after the catch per reception, ranking fourth-highest among tight ends in that department. COLBY PARKINSON, @RamsNFL TE Parkinson averaged 6.8 Yards After the Catch per Reception in 2025 – ranking the 4th HIGHEST of any @NFL TE, min. 45 targets (Per @NextGenStats ) #RamsHouse #Rams #LosAngelesRams #LARams #LARvsCAR #NFL #NFLPlayoffs #NFLDraft #NFLTwitter #nflx #NFLNews pic.twitter.com/5qHkFhwNx0 — Pro Football Hall of Fame Ambassador (@PFHOFAmbassador) January 10, 2026 His production even carried over into the postseason. Despite Higbee returning in the regular season finale against Arizona, Parkinson started all three games in the playoffs, finishing with eight receptions on 14 targets for 152 yards and a touchdown. At the same time, Higbee had four receptions on six targets for 84 yards and no scores. Parkinson’s game-winning touchdown against the Panthers on Wild Card Weekend was the highlight of an excellent finish to his second season in Los Angeles. OMG STAFFORD TO PARKINSON FOR THE LEAD! LARvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qLSKKdmoBO — NFL (@NFL) January 11, 2026 Parkinson has received recognition from Pro Football Focus for his late-season efforts, ranking 15th in the outlet’s tight end rankings ahead of the season. Here’s what PFF’s Dalton Wasserman and Max Chadwick said about the veteran, whom they placed between the Ravens’ Mark Andrews and Seahawks’ AJ Barner: “After a ho-hum first five seasons, Parkinson enjoyed the best season of his career in 2025. His 77.2 PFF receiving grade placed ninth among all tight ends, while his eight touchdown catches tied for third. Parkinson was a weapon after the catch, averaging 6.4 yards after the catch per reception (sixth). His 30 positively-graded plays as a run-blocker were sixth at the position as well.” Parkinson is not going to transform into a top tight end like George Kittle or Trey McBride, yet his strong second half to the season, including the playoffs, shows how valuable he is to the Rams’ offense. His promising finish to the year indicates that he can build on it moving into the 2026 season as L.A. aims for another deep playoff run.
author: Evan Craig

title: Alabama writer: Ty Simpson has far more upside than people realize
summary: Ty Simpson is not your typical former five-star recruit, neither in how long it took him to become a starter at Alabama, nor in the fact that his time on the bench to prevent him from becoming a first-round pick. Despite spending his first three years as a backup, including two behind a starter whose […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CA - JUNE 02: Rams quarterback Ty Simpson (15) during the Los Angeles Rams OTA on June 02, 2026, at the The Rams Village in Woodland Hills, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ty Simpson is not your typical former five-star recruit, neither in how long it took him to become a starter at Alabama, nor in the fact that his time on the bench to prevent him from becoming a first-round pick. Despite spending his first three years as a backup, including two behind a starter whose accuracy was a significant hindrance to the team, Simpson has been tabbed as the heir apparent to Matthew Stafford. The Los Angeles Rams believe in Simpson’s talent. And so do some of the people who followed his unusual journey over four years at Alabama. Brent Taylor is a writer at the SB Nation’s Alabama blog Roll Bama Roll and he’s been through the entire Simpson experience over the last four seasons, from being one of the more unheralded five-star QB recruits of his time, to finally getting his shot to start three years later, until his body was nearly coming apart at the seams by the end. I asked Brent about what it was like, from the fan’s experience, to track Simpson from recruit, to competing for the most important job on the team, to his one season as the starter. “There was a large contingent of Alabama fans who really wanted to see Simpson in early 2023 when Jalen Milroe first won that job (me included). It went kind of weirdly… ” As well as if he’s surprised that Simpson went 13th overall and what the quarterback’s greatest strength and greatest weakness will be going into the most important job on the Rams. “It’s something that you just don’t see from college QBs often these days…” Here’s what he had to tell me about Simpson, then and now. Q: What was the feeling among fans when Ty Simpson committed as a recruit in 2022? Where does he rank among Saban’s QB recruits all-time? Brent Taylor: Simpson was relatively under-the-radar for a 5-star QB recruit. Cade Klubnik and Drew Allar were the big two that year, and Simpson, despite a #29 overall ranking, was a guy that was coming from a small school in Tennessee, and it just didn’t really draw the hype you usually get from a 5-star passer. Still, there were a lot of high expectations for him, despite most of us knowing he was a guy that would likely take a couple of years to adjust to college speed (he made a LOT of hay in high school just running read options, scrambling around, and being a better athlete than everyone on the field). As far as where he fit in the All-Time Saban recruit rankings, there was Blake Barnett in 2015 (major bust), Tua Tagovailoa in 2017, and #1 overall recruit Bryce Young in 2020 that all out-ranked him in terms of recruiting rankings and fan expectations. You could also throw in current Ohio State QB Julian Sayin on that list on a technicality, since he did sign with Nick Saban…. he just also transferred a month later when Saban retired. All that to say, Simpson wasn’t some chump that managed to have a solid senior season, he was always someone who we thought could/should be elite. Q: The elephant in the room for me is spending three years on the bench, including two behind Jalen Milroe, who was a solid college quarterback but not someone that most of us remember being Tim Tebow or Cam Newton in college. What was the feeling there when Simpson spent 2 years behind Milroe and why didn’t he transfer? BT : The short answer is that it was a weird situation, and it was compounded by Ty Simpson reportedly (and through his own admission later) struggling with confidence and emotions, and that led to him just not being ready. The very long answer: There was a large contingent of Alabama fans who really wanted to see Simpson in early 2023 when Jalen Milroe first won that job (me included). It went kind of weirdly… Nick Saban always loved to start the most veteran QB at the beginning of the season opener when there was a QB battle, then rotate through the game until he picked a starter in a week or two. Well, game 1 that year, Milroe scored on nearly every possession against some scrub school, then the Tide just played kill-the-clock when Simpson came in. The next week, the Tide played Texas and got behind early, and Saban just said later that he felt like Alabama was close and didn’t want to kill continuity. Week 3 was the tipping point, when Alabama played South Florida in a torrential downpour. Saban decided before the game that Milroe wasn’t cutting it and that Simpson and transfer veteran QB Tyler Buchner would both get a shot. Well, Buchner was an abject disaster and the Tide was LOSING to USF when Simpson got the shot to take over and win. He did just that, completing a few downfield passes and ultimately leading a couple of scoring drives. He also got sacked like 7 times. At the time, I personally thought that Simpson showed enough in those horrific playing conditions that I thought he should be given a second look at getting playing time over Milroe. However, Saban didn’t see things that way, and we had Milroe the rest of the way. Ultimately, I think it was more about Milroe’s X-factor as a runner (the Alabama offense was struggling to pass and to run….. But they just kept scoring because Milroe could house it from 50 yards out on any given play). 2024 rolls around, and Alabama now has Kalen Deboer. Milroe was pretty much the key voice in the offseason supporting the new coach and giving it his all to keep the roster together and team morale up . With that level of leadership in circumstances where the entire roster could have just…left… It only made sense to stick with Milroe. Still, as 2024 wore on and the Alabama offense got worse and worse, we were pretty much all calling for Ty Simpson to get a shot. Again, I think the combination of loyalty and Milroe’s ability to run when nothing else was working is what kept that change from ever happening. I also don’t think that Milroe would have kept that starting job if he had tried to come back in 2025 rather than going to the NFL. For what it’s worth, Simpson has spoken candidly about his frustration with those years and that it would have made all the sense in the world to transfer. Ultimately, he’s just kept saying that he loved Alabama and wanted nothing more than to leave a legacy there, rather than being viewed as a guy who left when things were hard. And I think that personality is something that the Rams valued highly. Q: What’s Simpson’s super power, the trait that will make him successful in the NFL? And what’s his Achilles heel, the one thing that could stop him from ever becoming a starter? BT : His best trait is how good he is coverage processing, accuracy in the intermediate areas, and a willingness to trust those two things and just let the ball rip. It’s something that you just don’t see from college QBs often these days now that college offenses are all so focused on pre-snap decisions and one-read passes. The trait that might doom him? Pocket awareness and subsequent injury concerns. When we first saw him on the field a few years ago, he was nearly oblivious to his offensive linemen getting beat or edge blitzes. He improved in his year as a starter, but his internal clock still runs way too long and he’s way too trusting of his OL (and don’t get it twisted, Alabama’s OL was atrocious last year). He takes way too many sacks from behind as he hangs in the pocket absolutely forever. On one hand, it was nice to have a QB who wasn’t a happy feet scrambler after 4 years of Bryce Young and Jalen Milroe. On the other, I did a lot of screaming at Ty to just DO SOMETHING. Throw in NFL defenders that he can’t just outrun like he did pretty often in college, and he could wind up spending a whole season on his back if his team doesn’t have a good OL. title: L.A. Rams News: Reports they were interested in a receiver during draft
summary: Reports are that the Los Angeles Rams were interested in drafting De’Zhaun Stribling during the 2026 NFL Draft, but Stribling was selected by the San Francisco 49ers in the second-round well before the Rams had a chance to take him. Some critics say that the 49ers reached for Stribling. Maybe. Odds are that the 49ers […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - MAY 8: De'Zhaun Stribling #15 of the San Francisco 49ers poses for a photo during Rookie Minicamp at SAP Performance Facility on May 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Reports are that the Los Angeles Rams were interested in drafting De’Zhaun Stribling during the 2026 NFL Draft, but Stribling was selected by the San Francisco 49ers in the second-round well before the Rams had a chance to take him. Some critics say that the 49ers reached for Stribling. Maybe. Odds are that the 49ers took Stribling before another team could, so if it was a reach, it was a risk the 49ers were willing to take to get their guy. I think that’s good management, in theory. Get who you want. Now, we’ll see if they can make the pick work, but I don’t doubt the 49ers will be able to incorporate Stribling as long as he stays healthy, we’ll see. This topic may be worth a re-visit later. Either way, the Rams took a receiver in CJ Daniels later in the draft, and some have high hopes for him . The Rams likely do which is why they took him. Always interesting to hear reports like this after the draft and seeing what teams actually thought or wanted during their respective drafts. Of course, we don’t know that all of these reports are facts, per se, but interesting nonetheless. It’s Wednesday. Please comment on whatever you want and thank you for checking out Turf Show Times! Report: Rams had interest in WR before he was drafted in 2nd round (ramswire) “According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Rams were one of the teams that “had eyes” on Ole Miss receiver De’Zhaun Stribling. But before L.A. could land the receiver (their next pick after No. 13 was at No. 61) , the San Francisco 49ers swooped in to secure Stribling at No. 33. “There were a couple of teams that I spoke to leading up to the draft that felt like that De’Zhaun Stribling was the best wide receiver in the draft. Another team, supposedly the Los Angeles Rams had eyes on him as well,” Schefter said this week. “The 49ers didn’t just come up with this pick out of nowhere, they knew that there were other teams that had a very high grade on Stribling when the 49ers declined to trade out the top draft slot in the second round and take him there.” Schefter: ‘Going to be a while’ before Aaron Donald decides on comeback (ramswire) “What’s going on right now is he’s trying to get back into football shape,” Schefter said on the Pat McAfee Show. “My understanding is it’s going to be a while before we hear a final decision about him coming back. When he comes back, he’s going to want to be Aaron Donald and he’s not going to come back unless he feels like he’s Aaron Donald. And that’s why it sounds like it’s not going to be a quick verdict from him – that he’s going to be ramping up all during training camp and this may go towards the start of the regular season before we hear that he has or hasn’t signed with the team. He’s going through it all right now. This is his own pre-training camp routine.” Puka Nacua has most to prove of any Rams player in 2026 for off-field reasons (sportingnews) “ Nate Atkins of The Athletic noted how Nacua is the one player on the Rams with the most on the line in 2026. With a looming contract that could be north of $160 million total, Nacua needs to prove his off-field issues are behind him. Rams’ Puka Nacua has off-field question to answer during 2026 season “Nacua spent weeks this offseason in a holistic care facility to try to curb some of these issues, and the Rams are making it clear to him that he will need a pattern of strong behavior to undo the concerns in order to earn the payday that his production justifies,” Atkins writes.“

title: Advanced quarterback projection stat has Las Vegas Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza as 4th-best prospect since 2021
summary: Ever since the Las Vegas Raiders landed the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft, a popular question in Raider Nation has been: “How does Fernando Mendoza compare to quarterbacks from previous draft classes?” Or some variation of that. Of course, the answer is subjective and can vary from person to person, and even […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 02: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass during the team's rookie minicamp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 02, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by David Becker/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ever since the Las Vegas Raiders landed the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft , a popular question in Raider Nation has been: “How does Fernando Mendoza compare to quarterbacks from previous draft classes?” Or some variation of that. Of course, the answer is subjective and can vary from person to person, and even statistic to statistic. But FTN’s Aaron Schatz , who has developed several popular statistical models to predict or add context to what’s going on in the NFL, offered an interesting finding in the Raiders’ chapter of FTN’s Annual Football Almanac . Schatz’s QBASE and TDYAR/R have Mendoza ranked as the fourth-best quarterback prospect since the 2021 draft class. To add some context to what that ranking means, below are brief explanations of the two metrics from FTN : “QBASE 2.0 is a combination of Andrew Healy’s (2015) original QBASE model and Alexandre Olbrecht and Jeremy Rosen’s (2018) functional mobility model. It factors in a quarterback’s college passing statistics adjusted for the quality of his teammates and opponents, plus how many years he started in college. It also incorporates his rushing ability, and while it rewards improvements over time, it penalizes one-year wonders. “…A value of 0 Total Defense-adjusted Yards Above Replacement per Attempt (TDYAR/A) is replacement-level, whereas any value over 1.5 is indicative of a Hall of Fame career. We run 50,000 simulations to provide a distribution of the number of times that each quarterback falls within a particular range.” The 2025 Heisman Trophy winner’s TDYAR/A is 0.57, trailing 2021 No. 1 pick Trevor Lawrence (0.73), 2024 first overall selection Caleb Williams (0.61) and 2021 second pick Zach Wilson (0.60). In the almanac, Schatz notes: “Look, the COVID season was weird,” to humorously explain how Wilson is an outlier in the Top 3. So, according to this metric, Las Vegas’s new quarterback would be the second-best option if the last three quarterback classes were combined. That includes the highly regarded 2024 class, which produced six first-rounders, with Jayden Daniels (0.34) being the next closest to Mendoza from that year. The list proceeds as follows: J.J. McCarthy (0.26), Drake Maye (0.03), Bo Nix (-0.08) and Michael Penix Jr. (-0.43). When it comes to last year’s first-round QBs, Mendoza is one spot ahead of Cam Ward (0.38) and several places above Jaxson Dart (0.20, 10th since 2021). Schatz offered some context into the difference between the last two No. 1 overall picks in the Almanac. “Last year, the QBASE projection system felt higher on Ward than the consensus of the scouting big boards. Ward led college football with 39 touchdown passes and 10.52 adjusted yards per attempt, but Mendoza led college football with 41 touchdown passes and 10.78 adjusted yards per attempt. And yet, the scouting consensus is that Mendoza was a slam-dunk No. 1 overall pick. Ward was eighth on Arif Hasan’s [media consensus] big board at Wide Left , and with a variance of 173.1—higher than any other player in the draft. Mendoza was No. 1. “Outside analysts that weren’t as high on Mendoza by comparison, like [The Athletic’s] Dane Brugler, were slotting him around third overall on their big boards. There were hits to pick in the Mendoza college tape—he does get sacked quite a bit—but it was hard to make a real argument that he wasn’t a top-five player in the class. “The difference may simply be explained by the truism: Size matters. Both Mendoza and Ward are effective and willing scramblers, but not physical outliers at the position. It’s just that Mendoza, at 6-foot-5 and 236 pounds, reminds us more of Justin Herbert in the open field than anyone else. His fourth-and-4 gallop into the end zone to put Indiana up 24-14 with 9:18 left in the National Championship Game didn’t leave jaws agape. It was merely a big, fast player wanting it more.” When looking at just this year’s class, the difference between the top pick and the next quarterback to come off the board wasn’t even close. Ty Simpson (-0.37) is well below a replacement-level TDYAR/A, ranking third to last and in a category with Mac Jones (-0.14), Penix (-0.43) and Anthony Richardson (-0.95). So, despite ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky’s infamous pre-draft take , the gap between Mendoza and Simpson is/was significant. Again, this is just one piece of information to take into account. But if you’re wondering how the new face of the Raiders’ franchise compares to other recently drafted quarterbacks, the answer is quite favorable when it comes to this model. If you’re interested in diving into more statistics like this to preview the upcoming Raiders’ season, follow this link to purchase a copy of FTN’s Football Almanac 2026 .

title: Las Vegas Raiders Summer Scouting: QB Rankings
summary: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. These rankings are extremely early, […]
full_text: ORLANDO, FL - DECEMBER 31: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns runs with the ball during the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl game between the Michigan Wolverines and the Texas Longhorns on December 31, 2025 at Campting World Stadium in Orlando, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. These rankings are extremely early, and they will evolve over not only the summer but the next 8-10 months throughout the season, and into draft season. Some lists will feature 10, 15, 20, or more ranked prospects but I’ll include others on the list below to note. The Raiders likely won’t need a QB, but it’s still crucial to know the class, and the Raiders will be doing the exact same thing Dante Moore, Oregon – 6’3, 208, R-Jr Moore has the makings of a franchise quarterback, and he could have declared in 2026 but a rough end of the year likely made the decision easier to return to Oregon. He has a prototypical frame, good athleticism, works the pocket well, and Moore is great when diagnosing pre snap pressure, coverages, and he’ll use his eyes to manipulate the defense well. He shows a good ability to operate out of structure, has a ton of arm talent, drives the ball well, and overall in terms of pure traits he’s the best in the class. Like others, Moore struggles in his post snap situations, he’ll be fooled by CBs outside the numbers, he forces throws, struggles when pressured, and he needs to do better not looking for the home run throw. Arch Manning, Texas – 6’4, 219, Jr Manning has been viewed as the best QB in the 2027 class since he was a high school senior, and while he has more development to go Manning has all the traits. He’s coming off his first starting season with a 62% completion rate, 3163 yards, 26 TD, and 7 interceptions. Manning has a great frame, he’s exceptionally athletic, works the pocket well, is able to diagnose pressure, and Manning shows tremendous pre snap tendences to ID coverages, backside angles, and manipulate defenders. He needs to do better at preventing forced throws, he’s inconsistent over the middle, and Manning doesn’t catch up to his pre snap tendencies as often as you’d like. He’ll likely continue to develop, and 2027 is a big season for him to cement himself at the top of the class. CJ Carr, Notre Dame – 6’3, 210, R-So I am a bit higher on Carr here, I also think Carr has a good shot to go back to college for the 2028 class. While not related to Derek Carr, there’s a lot of similar traits as a passer. Carr has a good frame, rocket of an arm, is able to layer and manipulate throws, he’s shown good accuracy, and his entire passing form is fluid, consistent, and clean. Carr drives his legs through the throw, generates a ton of velocity, shows a ton of pre snap tendencies, and understands coverages well. He’s a young quarterback, and continuing to build on his 2025 season will be crucial. Carr’s biggest struggle in 2026 was his consistent look to be “the guy” and he had a few bad reads when trying to play hero ball, he’ll also need to improve in the pocket, but coming off a 67% completion rate, 2741 yard, 24 TD, and 6 INT season there’s a ton of room. Drake Lindsey, Minnesota – 6’6, 230, R-So Lindsey is someone to note, and he should rise quicker than others believe. 2025 was his first year as a starter with 2400 yards, 18 TD, and 6 interceptions on a 63% completion rate. Lindsey has inconsistent technique, he’s not overly mobile, but he does understand the pocket well and can work to create room during the pass. Lindesy is smart, he reads defenses well both pre and post snap, maintains his composure under pressure, and mainly he has a rocket launcher on his arm. Lindesy generates a ton of velocity, has the ability to hit most throws on the field, works backside well, can lead receivers, shows good layering on throws, and he’s able to manipulate defenders. He’s a prototypical pocket passer, and in an era moving away from such his future may be tough to read but the talent and mental tendencies are NFL ready. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State – 6’4, 215, Jr Mestemaker broke onto the scene with North Texas in 2026, he tossed a 69% completion rate, 34 touchdowns, and 9 interceptions. Mestemaker has exceptional arm talent, can hit any throw on the field, and the former walk on QB/punter has a tremendous path to continuing his future. Mestemaker needs to work on his pre snap abilities, and he’ll have a tendency to play hero ball which can lead to bad throws, interceptions, and plays that don’t succeed in the NFL but he’s creative, extends plays, and can work in the pocket well. Mestemaker shows a good frame, uses his full body in the throw, generates a ton of velocity, and he’s also a capable runner as well. The sky is the limit for Mestemaker, and in his first season at Oklahoma State, there’s a lot of upside in his future but I’d expect he’s likely in the 2028 class instead of 2027. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss – 6’1, 200, Sr There’s no denying Chambliss really came out of no where in 2025. He entered the season at Ole Miss third on the depth chart after transferring from Ferris State (D2), then rose to the occasion with a 66% completion rate, nearly 4000 yards, 22 touchdowns, and three interceptions with production on the ground as well. He’s a quick quarterback, he has adequate arm strength, but a great understanding of defensive and offensive structure, is a creative playmaker, and he does a great job working on hitting concepts with clear pre snap looks. Chambliss is an older prospect, being 25 years old as a rookie, and 2026 is big to show he can continue to build on his first year in the SEC. Chambliss is athletic, he’ll work the pocket well, can play under pressure, and finds the open read. Chambliss is likely a late first, and was probably the same in 2026, but he’s shown NFL upside similar to Tyler Shough. CJ Bailey, NC State – 6’6, 210, R-So Bailey is extremely athletic, has a massive arm, and his technique is inconsitent but there’s a bright future ahead of him. He’ll need a breakthrough 2026 season to declare but he’s one to keep an eye on for 2028. Bailey’s talent as a runner, passer, and overall technique is reminiscing of Auburn Cam Newton at times. Darian Mensah, Miami – 6’3, 215, R-Jr Demond Williams, Washington – 6’0, 190, Jr LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina – 6’3, 240, R-Jr Sellers can easily land as a top five pick, he struggles under pressure, and 2025 was a poor season due to a ton of factors but the raw traits, athleticism, and flashes remain. An improved South Carolina offensive line, passing weapons, and structure are crucial in a very likely make it or break it year. Jayden Maiava, USC – 6’4, 235, Sr Julian Sayin, Ohio State – 6’1, 208, Sr This is lower on Sayin than others would put him, I’m not overly high on Sayin. He’s a capable quarterback, his technique is consistent, but Sayin doesn’t flash with his pre/post snap technique, he has average arm talent, and Sayin doesn’t show a ton of ability to work out of structure, largely because he’s not been asked too. Sayin can easily rise this season, but he’s also one I look for in 2028 compared to 2027. Byrum Brown, Auburn – 6’3, 235, Sr John Mateer, Oklahoma – 6’1, 225, Sr Seeking bounce back year off a hand injury in 2025 that limited him. Great athlete, changed his throwing form, stronger and drives the ball better, rushing game might be his best. Sam Leavitt, LSU – 6’2, 206, R-Jr Also seeking bounce back season after an injury in 2025. Now under Lane Kiffin at LSU, good scheme and weapons around him. Has first round talent at times, needs to be consistent. Other Names to Know: Aiden Chiles, Northwestern – Transfer from Michigan State, athletic,…

summary: As we all know, the Miami Dolphins have begun a major roster transition under the new leadership duo of general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Many older, high-priced veterans were shown the door this offseason, and in their places, younger, cheaper players have been brought in and given opportunities to prove they […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - SEPTEMBER 29: Jonah Savaiinaea#72 of the Miami Dolphins runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium on September 29, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we all know, the Miami Dolphins have begun a major roster transition under the new leadership duo of general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Many older, high-priced veterans were shown the door this offseason, and in their places, younger, cheaper players have been brought in and given opportunities to prove they belong in the National Football League. Every year, ESPN releases a ranking of all 32 NFL teams regarding how much talent they roster under the age of 25. Last year, the Dolphins ranked second-to-last — coming in at #31 on the four-letter network’s list. Heading into the 2026 NFL season, Miami has made a major leap up those rankings — sitting at #12 on this year’s list. In a curious move, author Aaron Schatz listed guard Jonah Savaiinaea as Miami’s only “blue-chip” player under 25, but also name-dropped guys like Patrick Paul, De’Von Achane, Kadyn Proctor, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips. Despite being ranked as the worst guard in the league last year by Pro Football Focus, Savaiinaea’s move to the right side of the offensive line in 2026 seems to have given ESPN hope that the young player will take positive steps forward this season. Despite the jump from #31 to #12, the Dolphins still sit behind both the New York Jets (#7) and New England Patriots (#1) on ESPN’s list. In fact, Schatz claims that New England’s quarterback — Drake Maye — is the NFL’s “most valuable young commodity” after leading his team to the Super Bowl in just his second season as a professional. title: SBN Prediction: J.J. McCarthy….traded?
summary: We’re truly in a brutal time in the NFL news cycle. Training camps haven’t opened up yet and free agency lists are more or less barren — unless you’re looking at the media landscape and/or previously worked for ESPN. This time of year lends itself to preseason predictions. Sometimes they’re bold, sometimes they’re beautiful, but […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JANUARY 4: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings speaks with teammates on the bench against the Green Bay Packers in the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re truly in a brutal time in the NFL news cycle. Training camps haven’t opened up yet and free agency lists are more or less barren — unless you’re looking at the media landscape and/or previously worked for ESPN. This time of year lends itself to preseason predictions. Sometimes they’re bold, sometimes they’re beautiful, but in the case of Jarrett Bailey’s piece that just dropped on main , they’re a bit of both. There’s no shortage of Vikings-adjacent angles therein. Bailey has Stefon Diggs signing with the Dallas Cowboys as his first prediction, for one. One particularly bothersome prediction — at least from this purview — is his No. 20 point: Justin Jefferson trade rumors begin. Bailey also predicts former Vikings edge defender Danielle Hunter will finish in the top five in the NFL in sacks, while Nahshon Wright appears in his top five in interceptions, as well. And while the Jefferson bit may be the thorn that sticks in the sides of Vikings fans most painfully, it’s Bailey’s No. 3 prediction overall that might prick up ears in a different manner. Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Ravens It’s not altogether surprising that outside observers are looking into McCarthy exit strategies. Heck, it’s not hard to find fans and media types locally who are doing the same. But does it make sense to trade McCarthy now with the season nigh and his trade value ostensibly at an all-time low? First, let’s consider what Bailey has to say: The writing is on the wall for J.J. McCarthy. The Vikings won 14 games with Sam Darnold, didn’t bring him back, and then watched him win a Super Bowl while they limped to a 9-8 record. McCarthy completed less than 60 percent of his passes with 11 touchdowns to 12 interceptions. He gets dealt to Baltimore and Jesse Minter, who won a National Championship with McCarthy at Michigan as the Wolverines’ defensive coordinator. My immediate reaction is that I’m not sure there’s enough smoke between McCarthy and his former defensive coordinator, but let’s table that for the time being. Bailey’s No. 58 prediction is “Murmurs of Lamar Jackson leaving Baltimore get loud” and in that case, I think, dovetails quite nicely with the Ravens acquiring a quarterback. Much more so than the Minter angle, anyway. If the Ravens have even the slightest idea that Jackson could become a squeaky wheel, having a backup plan in place is a reasonable idea. Baltimore’s depth chart at quarterback behind Jackson includes Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano and Diego Pavia. That’s not entirely different than the Vikings behind Kyler Murray, with McCarthy and Carson Wentz potentially interchangeable and Max Brosmer in the No. 4 spot. The Vikings are reportedly still “ bullish ” on Brosmer, according to Alec Lewis of The Athletic, and Wentz certainly has the acumen, personality and requisite toughness to be the team’s No. 2 quarterback for a full season. Assuming Wentz is fully ready to be active from the jump, is it that unreasonable to suggest McCarthy has one foot out the door? In my personal opinion, I do not think it makes sense to deal McCarthy. His value, again, is at an all-time low. Murray played five games last season and has played more than 16 just three times (and just once in the last five seasons). The diminutive but talented signal-caller is enough of an injury risk that pairing him with McCarthy and having Wentz as the third wheel is actually quite a nice, complementary trio. Keeping Brosmer around until the final cuts makes a ton of sense. Not only does he protect in case of injury — and considering Wentz had a terrible shoulder injury last year, besides — of any of the three passers ahead of him, but he would seem to have a reasonable chance of passing through waivers and joining the team’s practice squad. I’m willing to be wrong. I’m willing to hear people’s disagreements. Tell me where you stand in the comments below.

title: What signing Mitch Van Vooren and Riley Wilson means for the Patriots
summary: With training camp right around the corner, the New England Patriots are keeping busy. On Wednesday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel had six players in town for tryouts, ended up signing two of those, and released another to put a bow on an eventful day. While signing tight end Mitch Van Vooren and […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - MAY 10: Mitch Van Vooren #44 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during rookie mini camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on May 10, 2025 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With training camp right around the corner, the New England Patriots are keeping busy. On Wednesday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel had six players in town for tryouts, ended up signing two of those, and released another to put a bow on an eventful day. While signing tight end Mitch Van Vooren and linebacker Riley Wilson , and waiving fullback Brock Lampe, do not seem like major moves in the grand scheme of things, they do impact the club ahead of camp. So, with that said, let’s take a closer look at what the transactions mean for the Patriots. Needs addressed The Patriots did their best to fill out their roster this offseason, but they still had some question marks in the depth department heading toward camp. Two positions in particular were in the spotlight: tight end and linebacker, with the former specifically mentioned by Mike Vrabel as one that could see a further infusion of talent at some point. Van Vooren is that infusion, just like Wilson is at linebacker. Admittedly, they enter as depth pieces and possible camp bodies, but they do give the club extra options to prepare and take an up-close look at with more than a month to go until the 53-man roster deadline. Intriguing profiles He was not invited to the Scouting Combine and did minimal work during the pro day cycle ahead of the 2025 NFL Draft, but he didn’t need to: Van Vooren brings an intriguing athletic background to the NFL regardless of what his testing numbers would have shown. Before focusing on football, after all, the 6-foot-5, 255-pounder was a standout track athlete. Among his achievements was setting school records in the 400-meter hurdles at both St. Norbert and Marquette. He was also voted to the All-Big East Outdoor team in 2022, and named first-team All-American in 2023. Despite not having the same multi-sport history, Wilson nonetheless has a profile worth looking at. His 6.83 Relative Athletic Score may appear rather average, but a closer look at it shows that he actually tested very well in the 40-yard dash: the 4.57 seconds he ran at his pro day would have been the eighth-fastest time among all the Combine linebackers this year. In addition to his speed, he also brings some versatility to the equation. He played both as an edge and off-ball linebacker during his college career, offering flexibility reminiscent of ex-Patriots linebacker Jahlani Tavai. Writing on the wall As Van Vooren and Wilson come into the Patriots’ fold, Lampe exits it. For the second-year fullback, the writing unfortunately was on the wall even after what was a relatively promising start to his NFL career last spring. As the lone fullback on the roster at the time, Lampe saw some reps with the first-team offense during his rookie offseason and the early stages of 2025’s training camp. At that point, he seemed like a possible roster candidate despite having previously gone unselected in the draft. However, the season-ending injury he suffered in late July put an end to any such projections. When the team subsequently signed veteran Reggie Gilliam to a three-year contract in this year’s free agency, his road to the 53-man roster effectively became blocked. Lampe beating out Gilliam in training camp was never a realistic option. And so, his tenure in New England has come to an end. No cap change expected We do not know the full details of the contracts Van Vooren and Wilson signed with the Patriots, but an educated guess is that they are of the one-year variety and close to if not at the $885,000 minimum salary. With no guarantees expected to be part of the pacts as well, they would have no impact on New England’s salary cap at this point in time (i.e. while the NFL’s Top 51 rule is in place). The same is true for waiving Brock Lampe. He already cost $5,000 against the Patriots’ cap in 2026 and 2027 through his rookie contract signing bonus proration anyway, and nothing about that arrangement has changed. The only difference is that the money is now allocated to the “dead cap” section of New England’s books. Gabe Jacas effect? During the offseason, NFL teams are allowed to carry 90 players on their active rosters. The Patriots’ currently stands at 92 . So, what’s going on? One of the two extra players is German-born offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, whose international status means that he is eligible for a roster exemption. The second player is a bit of a mystery. Nobody else on the team qualifies for such an exemption, and no official announcement through the NFL transactions wire has been made that would answer the question about who No. 92 is. One option appears to be Gabe Jacas, though. The second-round draft pick has yet to sign a contract with the Patriots, and there has been no movement even as his fellow rookies have reported to training camp . Jacas not being in the same boat as them could mean he currently does not count against the 90-man limit, allowing New England to have two extra players signed for the time being.

title: Patriots sign tight end, linebacker ahead of training camp
summary: The New England Patriots keep fine-tuning their roster ahead of training camp. As part of this process, the reigning AFC champions made three transactions on Wednesday. Tight end Mitch Van Vooren and linebacker Riley Wilson were signed to the active roster, while fullback Brock Lampe was waived by the team. Van Vooren, 25, originally began […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2025; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Arizona Wildcats linebacker Riley Wilson (16) against the Kansas Jayhawks at Arizona Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The New England Patriots keep fine-tuning their roster ahead of training camp. As part of this process, the reigning AFC champions made three transactions on Wednesday. Tight end Mitch Van Vooren and linebacker Riley Wilson were signed to the active roster, while fullback Brock Lampe was waived by the team. Van Vooren, 25, originally began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He spent time in Seattle and Cleveland last summer, but has been without team since getting cut by the Browns in August. Before turning pro, the 6-foot-5, 255-pounder played college football at St. Norbert, where he appeared in 22 games and caught 65 passes for 1,045 yards and 13 touchdowns. Wilson, 24, entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie earlier this offseason. He initially intended to sign a free agency deal with the Buccaneers, but the club backed out after he failed his physical due to a groin injury. He previously spent three seasons at Hawaii, where he played 16 games over a three-season span before transferring to Montana. In two seasons with the Grizzlies, he appeared in 26 games with 13 starts and was named second-team All-Big Sky twice. He moved to Arizona for his final year of eligibility, adding 11 more games and four starts to his résumé while also registering 51 tackles, a trio of sacks, and two interceptions. Lampe, 23, joined the Patriots as an undrafted free agent in 2025. As the lone fullback on New England’s roster at the time, he did see some first-team practice reps during his rookie offseason but ultimately suffered a season-ending leg injury in early training camp. Van Vooren and Wilson were among a group of six players who participated in tryouts on Wednesday. Joining them were offensive linemen Ryan Mosesso and Kaylan Faumui, tight end ThomasOdukoya, and defensive lineman Derrick McLendon. The Patriots will hold their first practice of this year’s training camp on Saturday at 10:15 a.m. ET.

title: Patriots O-line deep dive: Center
summary: When New England Patriots training camp opens at the end of the week, there’s going to be one position group that a lot of eyes are going to be on, and rightfully so. There’s probably not a bigger question mark on the team right now than the offensive line. The possible outcomes for this group […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - NOVEMBER 13: Jared Wilson #58 of the New England Patriots exits the field after an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on November 13, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images When New England Patriots training camp opens at the end of the week, there’s going to be one position group that a lot of eyes are going to be on, and rightfully so. There’s probably not a bigger question mark on the team right now than the offensive line. The possible outcomes for this group are wildly different, and, depending on who you ask, people either feel a lot better about last year, about the same, or, in some cases, even worse. In this week leading up to camp, I’m going to do a deep dive into each position along the offensive line and let you know whether I think the Patriots improved, and what to expect from the position as a whole. Today is Day 3 and today we’re looking at center. Let’s get into it. Center deep dive 2025 starter: Garrett Bradbury Projected 2026 starter: Jared Wilson The right side of the line is solid; this is where the Patriots start to have some real questions. Jared Wilson has one year of starting experience under his belt, and he was decent for most of his 2025 rookie season, especially when you consider that he was playing out of position. However, playing center in the NFL is a tough job, and even though Garrett Bradbury certainly wasn’t great, and has since been traded to the Bears, he was a veteran at the position who could get the line on the same page. Wilson hasn’t shown that he can do that yet, and so this offseason and training camp will hopefully be a crash course in playing center at the NFL level. I believe that the talent is there, and that he should be a solid player, but it’s an important position, and one that he hasn’t yet played against pro-level competition and at NFL speed both physically and mentally. Another important reason for Wilson to play well is that there isn’t really a backup behind him. Ben Brown is back as the super sub, and he can do it, but he’s not the guy that you want starting at center for a playoff football team. They also signed undrafted rookie Jacob Rizy, but he is probably more of a camp body than anything else. Assuming that Wilson can make the mental leap to playing the position at an adequate level that is not a downgrade from Bradbury, the Patriots should be in a good spot at center. Wilson has a ton of potential, and should give them above average performance at the position, if things go well. He has the physical tools and abilities to become one of the better centers in the league in the next few years, and that would be huge for any team, but especially one that loves to run the ball, and also has a franchise quarterback taking the snaps.

title: 5 top position battles at Patriots training camp
summary: The New England Patriots are back at Gillette Stadium this week as they will hold their first training camp practice of the summer on Saturday. With things now officially ramping up in preparation for the 2026 season, jobs are ready to be won throughout training camp. Here are the top positional battles we’ll be watching on the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - MAY 20: New England Patriots linebacker Elijah Ponder (91) and New England Patriots linebacker Bradyn Swinson (43) arrive during New England Patriots OTA on May 20, 2025, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots are back at Gillette Stadium this week as they will hold their first training camp practice of the summer on Saturday. With things now officially ramping up in preparation for the 2026 season, jobs are ready to be won throughout training camp. Here are the top positional battles we’ll be watching on the practice fields. Third running back The top of the Patriots running back depth chart is set with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The third spot behind them, however, remains up for grabs. After getting off to a strong start last season before breaking his foot, Lan Larison appeared to be the top internal candidate this spring. But he will be pushed by seventh-round draft pick Jam Miller and highly paid undrafted free agent Myles Montgomery. Third-year pro Terrell Jennings should also remain in the mix despite beginning the summer on the non-football injury list. Special teams — particularly the kick return role — could play a significant factor in deciding the competition. Depth tight end Hunter Henry is locked in as the team’s top tight end. But after the season-ending loss of free-agent addition Julian Hill, New England needs someone to emerge behind him. Third-round rookie Eli Raridon is the top internal option, although the Notre Dame product may not be ready to immediately fill the in-line role Hill was projected to play. That could open the door for blocking specialists Tanner Arkin or C.J. Dippre, who will begin training camp on the PUP list, to earn a role. Jack Westover will also factor into the competition back at his natural position. With plenty of uncertainty behind Henry, head coach Mike Vrabel hinted this spring that the Patriots could look outside the organization for additional help at some point this offseason. Defensive edge The Patriots’ edge group continues to carry the most question marks on the roster. Those concerns only grew with veteran Harold Landry opening training camp on the PUP list while Gabe Jacas remains unsigned even after rookies reported on Tuesday. New England could use a young player — or two — to elevate their game this summer, with Elijah Ponder and Bradyn Swinson standing out as the top candidates after receiving significant praise from the coaching staff throughout the spring. Rookies Quintayvious Hutchins and Xavier Holmes also find themselves in the mix, while the possibility of the Patriots adding another veteran later this summer should remain on the table. Depth linebacker Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss return as the Patriots’ top duo along the second level of the defense. But after moving on from Jack Gibbens, Jahlani Tavai, and Marte Mapu this offseason, the depth behind them remains unsettled. During the spring, free-agent addition K.J. Britt got off to an impressive start before dealing with a minor injury. Chad Muma, a 2022 third-round pick who joined the team last December, then wore the green dot at times in relief of Spillane. The two veterans — both of whom bring extensive special teams experience — are considered the favorites for depth roles, while rookies Namdi Obiazor and Khalil Jacobs will look to make a push as well. Depth cornerback The Patriots return one of the league’s best cornerback trios in Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, and Marcus Jones. The competition for roles behind them could be one of the most competitive battles on the roster. This spring, free-agent addition Kindle Vildor served as the top backup on the boundary and showcased his experience with steady play. Charles Woods and fifth-round pick Karon Prunty will provide direct competition on the outside, while Marcellas Dial Jr., who is returning from a torn ACL, and Kobee Minor project to provide depth in the slot. Other battles to watch Wide receiver: The Patriots’ wide receiver depth chart is led by newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Plenty of spots and roles remain up for grabs behind them, with Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas, and Efton Chism III all factoring into the equation — while the future of Kayshon Boutte will need to be decided. Interior offensive line: Could first-round pick Caleb Lomu make a push for a starting spot along the offensive line this summer? If not, will Lomu continue to see time at guard and carve out a role in the reserve mix alongside Ben Brown? Interior defensive line: There will be plenty of competition behind Milton Williams and Christian Barmore along the interior of the defensive line, while Cory Durden looks to solidify himself as the team’s top full-time nose tackle. What do you think about the Patriots’ top training camp battles? Please make sure to participate in our survey and also head down to the comment section to share your thoughts with the community.

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for G Alijah Vera-Tucker
summary: Despite starting a pair of rookies on the left side, the New England Patriots offensive line performed at a decent level during the 2025 season. Unfortunately for the group, it failed to sustain the performance into the playoffs. New England’s postseason struggles particularly in pass protection prompted more investment into the group, including in that […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA- JUNE 11: Alijah Vera-Tucker #75 of the New England Patriots setups for a play during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Despite starting a pair of rookies on the left side, the New England Patriots offensive line performed at a decent level during the 2025 season. Unfortunately for the group, it failed to sustain the performance into the playoffs. New England’s postseason struggles particularly in pass protection prompted more investment into the group, including in that left side: with Jared Wilson moving to his natural position at center, a new left guard was needed. The Patriots opted for experience this time around, and for immense upside. Hard facts Name: Alijah Vera-Tucker Position: Guard Jersey number: 75 Opening day age: 27 (6/17/1999) Measurements: 6’ 4 1/2”, 308 lbs, 32 1/8” arm length, 9 5/8” hand size, 5.102s 40-yard dash, 7.70s three-cone drill, 4.63s short shuttle, 32” vertical jump, 8’10” broad jump, 32 bench press reps, 9.77 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL teams: New York Jets (2021-25), New England Patriots (2026-) | College: USC (2018-20) An Under Armour All-American in high school, where he played both offensive tackle and defensive end, Vera-Tucker committed to USC as a four-star recruit. Moving to offensive guard at USC, Vera-Tucker served as a reserve his redshirt freshman season appearing in 12 games. He then took over a starting role the following year at left guard, where he went on to earn AP All-Pac-12 First-Team honors. Named a captain in 2020, Vera-Tucker started all six games in USC’s Covid-condensed season back at left tackle. He again earned All-Pac-12 honors and won the 2020 Morris Trophy as the conference’s top offensive lineman. Declaring for the 2021nNFL Draft, Vera-Tucker was selected 14th overall by the New York Jets — with the team trading up one spot ahead of the Patriots, who went on to select Mac Jones. The first-rounder started 16 games at left guard his rookie season. Moving to right guard in his second NFL season, injuries up front forced Vera-Tucker to then start one game at left tackle and two at right tackle. He then suffered an injury of his own as a torn right triceps landed him on season-ending injured reserve in Week 7. Injuries have continued to plague Vera-Tucker as he suffered a torn achilles the following year before missing all of 2025 with a torn left triceps. Sandwiched in between those seasons was a healthy 2024, however, where he turned in an elite season at right guard. Scouting report Strengths: Vera-Tucker is a strong athlete at the guard position testing above the 90th percentile in Relative Athletic Score back at the 2021 NFL Combine. That shows in the run game as he can fire out of his stance and reach blocks in outside zone schemes and as a puller. Vera-Tucker’s athletic ability also allows him to keep up with interior lineman in pass protection while he also can win at times with his play strength. Weaknesses: Availability has been the biggest weakness of Vera-Tucker’s career as he’s suffered three season-ending injuries in his first five years as a pro. When healthy, he has proven to be a high-level guard. For those who wanted a big-body mauler next to Will Campbell, however, Vera-Tucker is a more athletic blocker who has 32 1/8” arms (8th percentile). 2025 review Stats : N/A Season recap: After his strong 2024 season, Vera-Tucker suited up for minimal starting action in the Jets’ first two preseason games — he was on the field for a combined 28 offensive snaps without giving up any quarterback pressures — before being held out of the finale. Just days before the start of the regular season, the then-26-year old suffered a torn left triceps during a 1-on-1 drill in practice. He was placed on injured reserve shortly thereafter and as a consequence forced to sit out the rest of the season without having appeared in any actual games that matter. 2026 preview Position: Starting left guard | Ability: High quality starter | Contract: Signed through 2028 (2029 UFA) What will be his role? The offseason trade of starting center Garrett Bradbury to Chicago allowed New England to move Jared Wilson back to his natural center position. This, in turn, opened a hole at left guard — one Vera-Tucker will fill. If healthy, he should make life easier for both Wilson and left tackle Will Campbell. What is his growth potential? A former first-round pick, Vera-Tucker has the potential to be one of the top guards in football. In his healthy 2024 campaign, his 2.8% pressure rate allowed was the fourth-lowest among guards. Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf noted after he was signed that “[he’s] still young and still has upside and is a really good player in his position. I would say Vera-Tucker, in 2024, was one of the best guards in the NFL.” Does he have positional versatility? As seen by both his time at USC and with the Jets, Vera-Tucker has the ability to play both guard spots and tackle in a pinch. He is best suited at guard, however. What is his salary cap situation? The three-year, $42 million contract Vera-Tucker signed was one of the Patriots’ biggest financial commitments of this year’s free agency, and carries a salary cap hit of just under $4.8 million in year one (1.4% of the total cap). That number consists of a $2.3 million base salary, $2.4 million signing bonus proration, and a $83,333 workout bonus proration. It also includes up to $4.25 million in not-likely-to-be-earned per-game roster bonuses. A combined $9.78 million of his 2026 compensation is guaranteed for cap purposes, including the roster bonuses (although they technically will still need to be earned). How safe is his roster spot? Health permitting, Vera-Tucker will be on the Patriots’ 53-man roster this fall and remain there throughout the season. Of course, as noted above, health has been the one big uncertainty in his NFL career after he appeared in only 43 of a possible 85 games in his career and not once played a full season. Summary: While his contract structure gives the Patriots some security, Vera-Tucker is still a high-risk, high-reward signing. The worst-case outcome is obvious and dependent on his availability. The best-case, however, is exciting: if healthy and playing to his abilities, New England has one of the better left guards in the NFL to protect Drake Maye and support youngsters Will Campbell and Jared Wilson along the offensive line. What do you think about Alijah Vera-Tucker heading into the 2026 season? Will he be available for every game? Or will his injury woes continue in New England? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts.

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for DT Isaiah Iton
summary: The New England Patriots entered this year’s free agency with 14 of their players in need of a new contract. Initially, only two of them — QB Tommy DeVito, TE/FB Jack Westover — were retained. Earlier this week, a third joined the mix: Isaiah Iton, who had remained on the open market since March, was […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 16: Isaiah Iton #68 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a play during an NFL preseason football game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 16, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots entered this year’s free agency with 14 of their players in need of a new contract. Initially, only two of them — QB Tommy DeVito, TE/FB Jack Westover — were retained. Earlier this week, a third joined the mix: Isaiah Iton, who had remained on the open market since March, was re-signed to effectively take the place of fellow defensive tackle Travis Shaw. For Iton, this will present an opportunity to pick up where he left off. Hard facts Name: Isaiah Iton Position: Defensive tackle/Interior defensive line Jersey number: 62 Opening day age: 25 (8/23/2001) Measurements : 6’2 5/8”, 300 lbs, 10 1/8” hand size, 34” arm length, 82 3/4” wingspan, 4.84s short shuttle, 32 1/2” vertical jump, 9’3” broad jump, 29 bench press reps, 7.62 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL teams: Tennessee Titans (2024), New England Patriots (2025-) | College: Northern Colorado (2019), Hutchinson (2020), Ole Miss (2021-22), Rutgers (2023) Typically, the term “journeyman” is used to describe NFL players bouncing between teams on a fairly regular basis. Iton, however, was a journeyman back in college. Initially a no-star recruit out of Pearland High School in Pearland, TX, he began his career at Northern Colorado but after playing in 12 games with three starts transferred to Hutchinson in 2020. While Covid-19 prevented him from appearing in any games for the Blue Dragons, his stint at the JUCO level allowed him to meet his academic requirements and find a spot at Ole Miss. In two seasons with the Rebels, Iton played 23 games with two starts. He entered the transfer portal following his junior campaign, moving to Rutgers to close out his college career. He spent only one season with the Scarlet Knights, but it was the best of his career: Iton started all 13 games in 2023, registering 38 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks and a fumble recovery — production good enough to secure him a spot with the Titans after he went undrafted the following spring. After one season on Tennessee’s practice squad, he joined the Patriots in the spring of 2025 but ended up missing the entire season on injured reserve. He has yet to appear in any games for the club. Scouting report Strengths: A compactly-built defender with a low center of gravity and good use of leverage, Iton has the length to be competitive at the point of attack. He uses his 34-inch arms well to get into blockers’ chests, and combines them with a strong initial punch to transfer his upper-body power into his opponent. His reach allows him to effectively two-gap up front versus the run, and to disrupt the ball carrier or quarterback even when engaged. He plays with good eyes against the run and some solid burst and leg drive out of his stance. He also can play multiple techniques up front. Weaknesses: Iton is not the most dynamic player, especially as a pass rusher. His lateral agility is limited and he lacks the foot speed to be much of a factor in pursuit or as a looper on stunts. In general, he is more of a power player than somebody able to win with finesse or technique: his use of counters remains underdeveloped and if he gets stymied on first contact, he can quickly turn into a non-factor. 2025 review Stats : N/A Season recap: Following the conclusion of the Titans’ 2024 season, Iton signed a futures contract with the team for 2025. However, he was let go by the organization in mid-April and had to spend the next month without a team. During that time, the Patriots brought him in to their rookie minicamp on a tryout basis and apparently liked what they saw: in mid-May, they signed Iton to their 90-man roster. The Rutgers product remained there through the early stages of training camp and preseason. However, his 44th preseason snap — 42 on defense, 2 on special teams — proved to be his last of the year: Iton suffered a hip injury against the Vikings in the second exhibition contest that led to him getting waived with an injury designation two days later. He went unclaimed, reverting to season-ending injured reserve. Moving to IR was a disappointing end to what had been a solid summer for Iton. Steadily increasing the quality of his reps and showing some promise against the run in particular, he appeared to be a dark-horse candidate for a spot on the practice squad if not the 53-man team. Iton ended his 2025 season with those two preseason appearances as well as three tackles, including one for a loss of yards. As noted above, he was not tendered by the Patriots as an exclusive rights free agent. 2026 preview Position: 3-/1-technique defensive tackle | Ability: Depth player/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2026 (2027 ERFA) What will be his role? Just like he did last summer, Iton will line up along the Patriots’ interior defensive line. There, he will be used as a 3- or 1-technique tackle who will see most of his actions on early down or as part of specific defensive packages. Whether or not he can help replace free agency departee Khyiris Tonga remains to be seen, but he projects as a rotational option behind the top trio of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore and Cory Durden. What is his growth potential? Iton has added 23 pounds to his frame since entering the NFL in 2024, a reflection of the fact that he is still a developing player even as a pro. How far that development will take him is anybody’s guess, but the best-case scenario appears to be as a two-down specialist capable of playing the run at a high level. Does he have positional versatility? While his usability as an all-around defensive tackle will depend on his growth as a pass rusher, Iton has decent flexibility from a lineup perspective. In his lone preseason in New England he lined up as a 3-technique, 1-technique and even at the nose. He also can play on the field goal/extra point blocking team. What is his salary cap situation? The Patriots signed Iton to a one-year contract, and even though the full details of the pact have yet to be reported the assumption is that it will be worth the equivalent of the exclusive rights tender he did not receive back in March. If so, he will be on a non-guaranteed $885,000 base salary that simultaneously functions as his cap number and will not qualify him for Top 51 status in the offseason. How safe is his roster spot? Iton was a roster bubble player in 2025, and he will be again in 2026. That being said, he did show some promise versus the run last summer. If he can pick up where he left off, he should at least make things interesting in what will be a six-player competition for playing time and roster spots behind the starter-level trio mentioned above. Summary: The Patriots’ interior run defense is a question mark heading into training camp, and Iton alone will not provide all the answers. However, his skillset and size suggests that he might get more prominent reps in training camp than the typical mid-July signing does. And from there, anything seems possible when it comes to making the 53-man roster or, more realistically, the practice squad. What do you think about Isaiah Iton heading into the 2026 season? Will he pick up where he left off? Or will his second stint in New England also be a short one? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts.

title: Patriots training camp preview 2026: Running backs searching for efficiency
summary: On paper, New England Patriots fielded one of the NFL’s most productive rushing attacks in 2025. Despite finishing sixth in rushing yards and fourth in rushing touchdowns, however, there was more to offer from the team’s designed run game.  Still, the potential upside of a second year of the Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson pairing […]
full_text: Feb 8, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson (32) warms up before the game against the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images On paper, New England Patriots fielded one of the NFL’s most productive rushing attacks in 2025. Despite finishing sixth in rushing yards and fourth in rushing touchdowns, however, there was more to offer from the team’s designed run game. Still, the potential upside of a second year of the Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson pairing left New England comfortable making minimal changes to the room this offseason. In the next edition of our Patriots training camp preview series, we’ll take a look at New England’s running back corps in its entirety and discuss the biggest takeaways heading into the summer practices. Veterans will report to the facility on July 24. *Denotes player on the Pats Pulpit 53-man roster projection Depth chart Starters: Rhamondre Stevenson (28)* , TreVeyon Henderson (23)* | Backups: Lan Larison (24)* , Terrell Jennings (25) , Jam Miller (22/R) , Myles Montgomery (23/R) Stevenson is projected to remain the starting back in 2026 after an up-and-down season. The sixth-year back lost three fumbles within the first five weeks; however, Stevenson fought through the hurdle and established himself as a dependable presence. En route to a Super Bowl appearance, Stevenson finished with the 10th-highest yards over expected percentage among running backs at 45% (a measure of the rushing attempts where a rusher gains more yards than are blocked for them). Alongside Stevenson is Henderson, who immediately established himself as one of the most explosive rushers in the league with four touchdown runs of 50 or more yards and 30 missed tackles. The 23-year-old had apparent lapses as a blocker and efficient runner between the tackles, but he’ll look to expand on a positive rookie season. Both Lan Larison and Terrell Jennings saw time as the third running back in the rotation during spring practices and will continue to compete with each other for that role heading into training camp. Jennings has over 36 rushing attempts for the Patriots over the past two seasons and will open camp on the non-football injury list , while Larison is returning from a season-ending broken foot he suffered in 2025 as a rookie. Rounding out the back end of the depth chart are powerful seventh-round rookie Jam Miller from Alabama and dynamic undrafted free agent Myles Montgomery from UCF. The two additions have worked with the third-team offense thus far and will continue to acclimate to the NFL as the offseason workouts progress. Key question: Can the O-line provide enough as a run-blocking unit? While the volume numbers reflect the run-game production near the top of the league, the efficiency metrics suggest otherwise. New England’s running backs performed at a league-average 4.4 yards per attempt. Yet, they only totaled an EPA (expected points added) per rush of -0.03, which ranks No. 17, meaning the offense wasn’t consistently creating favorable situations on the ground. Although that figure stems from a multitude of factors, New England’s offensive line played a noticeable role in that underperformance. The Patriots’ line needed more push and play strength at the point of attack to routinely create running lanes, leading to the signing of Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard. The former New York Jet slots in between left tackle Will Campbell and newly transitioned center Jared Wilson, who will be entering their second seasons. Padded practices during training camp, when the offense can begin integrating live designed runs, will be a measure of how improved the run blocking will be. X-Factor: TreVeyon Henderson Additionally, though Henderson proved he’s a dynamic playmaker who is a touchdown threat whenever the ball is in his hands, the ball carrier’s vision and pass protection ability held him back. The highly touted pass blocker out of Ohio State couldn’t replicate the same collegiate success during his rookie year. Furthermore, he lacked the proper field vision to improvise behind the line of scrimmage, resulting in stuffed attempts behind the line of scrimmage. In terms of improvement, Henderson identified similar areas of emphasis earlier this offseason. “The biggest thing I want to continue to develop, blocking and just during this time running routes out of the backfield, catching the ball out of the backfield,” Henderson said to reporters at the beginning of June. “This is a time when we can really just continue to enhance those skills. Specifically those two skills, I definitely want to continue to develop.” Much of the running back room’s potential relies on the development of Henderson entering year two. If he can find his stride, Henderson and Stevenson can make New England’s offense a significant two-dimensional threat in 2026.

summary: The New England Patriots are set to take another look at a former member of their practice squad. Thomas Odukoya, whose contract with the team expired in February, will be in town for a free agency workout this week. Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston was first to report the team’s interest in the 29-year-old. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 19: Thomas Odukoya #88 arrives to Nissan Stadium prior to the NFL 2025 game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots are set to take another look at a former member of their practice squad. Thomas Odukoya, whose contract with the team expired in February, will be in town for a free agency workout this week. Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston was first to report the team’s interest in the 29-year-old. A 6-foot-6, 253-pound tight end, Odukoya originally joined New England’s practice squad last October. He spent the remainder of the season with the team, but was moved to the practice squad injured reserve in December after suffering a broken leg in practice. Now fully healthy again, he will get an opportunity to showcase his readiness. Born in the Netherlands, Odukoya entered the NFL through the International Player Pathway Program in 2022. He spent his first three seasons with the Tennessee Titans, including two under now-Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, before being let go and reuniting with Vrabel in New England. The Patriots are entering their 2026 training camp with uncertainty at tight end. While Hunter Henry is entrenched into the starting position, the depth behind him is a collective question mark following the season-ending injury suffered by Julian Hill during offseason workouts. At the moment, Jack Westover and rookies Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin round out the group. Fellow tight end C.J. Dippre is also part of it, but he was placed on the active/PUP list on Tuesday . New England currently has a full roster, but Odukoya’s international status would allow him to join the club as a roster-exempt 92nd player. As such, he would join German-born Lorenz Metz, who currently hold spot No. 91. The Patriots will hold the first practice of this year’s training camp on Saturday at 10:15 a.m. ET.
