title: Stan Brock weighs in on Alvin Kamara’s future, Erik McCoy’s importance to Saints
summary: New Orleans Saints Hall of Famer and former offensive tackle Stan Brock recently spoke with Arizona Cardinals insider Kyle Odegard in an exclusive one-on-one interview for Action Network, where he talked about some of the most significant story lines in the Big Easy with training camp one week away. Brock believes confidence will be a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 13: Tackle Stan Brock #67 of the New Orleans Saints looks to block defensive lineman Reggie White #92 of the Philadelphia Eagles during a game at Veterans Stadium on October 13, 1991 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Saints defeated the Eagles 13-6. (Photo by George Gojkovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images New Orleans Saints Hall of Famer and former offensive tackle Stan Brock recently spoke with Arizona Cardinals insider Kyle Odegard in an exclusive one-on-one interview for Action Network , where he talked about some of the most significant story lines in the Big Easy with training camp one week away. Brock believes confidence will be a major factor in Alvin Kamara’s 2026 season following the Saints making the splash signing of running back Travis Etienne Jr this offseason in free agency. He said today’s NFL creates unique challenges for veteran players as teams increasingly turn to free agency and trades to bolster their rosters. “It’s different now than when I played,” Brock said. “There was no free agency, so there wasn’t a big problem because they weren’t bringing in free agents to replace you. Just with a draft pick. Now, the mentality is different, and guys start feeling that. I’m not as needed and I’m not as wanted as I once was. And anything that chips away at your confidence hurts your performance.” Brock said Kamara could begin feeling isolated if he believes the organization is questioning his abilities, particularly after adding another accomplished running back to the backfield that is known for playing in a similar manner to what Kamara was once known for. “If they start questioning what he can do, whether it’s catching the ball out of the backfield, getting outside, it’s going to chip away at his confidence,” Brock said. “That makes it a lot harder to go out there and give it everything you’ve got for that group.” The former Saints offensive tackle also acknowledged that if the relationship between Kamara and the organization deteriorates, a split could ultimately be the best outcome. “Sometimes it’s easier to go find somebody who wants you,” Brock said. “Hopefully, just out of respect for him, I hope they treat him right.” Brock also emphasized the importance of Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy remaining healthy, calling stability along the interior of the offensive line essential for the Saints’ offense to succeed. “When you’re playing with a backup center that’s not quite as good, or if we moved this guy from guard to learn how to play center, there are a lot of questions,” Brock said. “What’s going to happen? (As a quarterback), you can’t be trying to take care of another position when you’re trying to do your job. He can’t be worried about the offensive line. He needs to stay focused.” With uncertainty surrounding Kamara’s role and the Saints counting on protecting their young quarterback this season, Brock believes both player confidence and offensive line continuity will be key factors in determining how successful New Orleans can be in 2026.
author: Nic Jennings

full_text: New Orleans Saints DE Cam Jordan will host his 3rd annual “An Evening with Cam Jordan” on Monday, October 12, 2026, at Generations Hall in New Orleans. The foundation’s signature fundraising event will celebrate Jordan’s remarkable 16-year NFL career while launching the next chapter of his lifelong commitment to serving the New Orleans community. The 3rd annual event will bring together Jordan’s current and former teammates, business leaders, corporate partners, community champions, and supporters from across Louisiana for an unforgettable celebration of gratitude, impact, and the future of the Cam Jordan Foundation. As Jordan enters his final NFL season, the evening will mark more than the end of an extraordinary football career, it will celebrate a legacy built through service, leadership, and an unwavering commitment to the city that he has called home since 2011. An event with Cam Jordan will serve as the centerpiece of the Foundation’s season-long “Thank You NOLA” campaign, a 16-week community initiative honoring the teachers, students, first responders, nonprofit leaders, lifelong Saints fans, and families who have supported Jordan throughout his career. “For the last 16 years, New Orleans has been more than a city to me, it has become family,” said Jordan. “This final season is about saying thank you. Football gave me a platform, but the people of New Orleans gave me a purpose. I want to celebrate this community while continuing to invest in its future.” 16 seasons. One incredible legacy.⚜️💪 Join us on October 12 for the Third Annual An Evening with Cam Jordan, as we celebrate @camjordan94 ’s impact on and off the field while investing in the future of New Orleans. Be part of an unforgettable evening of gratitude, purpose, and… pic.twitter.com/xKNoHhQPVi — Cam Jordan Foundation (@camjfoundation) July 21, 2026 Throughout the 2026 season, the Cam Jordan Foundation will expand its impact through 16 for 16, a weekly giveback initiative featuring school visits, surprise community activations, mentorship opportunities, neighborhood service projects, and special fan experiences celebrating Jordan’s lasting impact on New Orleans. Proceeds from the annual dinner will directly support the foundation’s growing community initiatives, including: ● The Legacy Fund, a long-term endowment supporting scholarships, mentorship, youth development, and community investments for generations to come. ● The Legacy Scholarship Program, providing up to $12,500 annually in tuition assistance, mentorship, professional development, and career opportunities for Louisiana students pursuing higher education. ● Sacks for Scholars, a season-long fundraising campaign where corporate partners and supporters pledge donations tied to Cam’s sack milestones, directly funding scholarships and educational programming. ● 16 for 16, a season-long initiative celebrating Jordan’s 16 years in New Orleans through meaningful community engagement and service. The evening will also recognize the Foundation’s 2026 Community MVP, honoring an individual whose commitment to serving others reflects the values of leadership, generosity, and community impact that have defined Jordan’s career both on and off the field. To learn more about the Cam Jordan Foundation, please visit Home | Cam Jordan Foundation For more information or to purchase tickets for the event, please visit An Evening With Cam Jordan | Cam Jordan Foundation

title: NY Giants news: 6 camp battles to watch, top 10 roster
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. Ian O’Connor: It’s becoming clear what John Harbaugh’s biggest challenge with the Giants will be | The Athletic Harbaugh had a vision of what that would look like. “I want to be in that parade,” he said in the […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. Ian O’Connor: It’s becoming clear what John Harbaugh’s biggest challenge with the Giants will be | The Athletic Harbaugh had a vision of what that would look like. “I want to be in that parade,” he said in the winter. “But with that being said, what I’m thinking about is what the team looks like that earns the right to be in that parade someday. What do we have to build to get there? That’s what I’m really consumed with.” After 18 years as a head coach in Baltimore and another 10 as an assistant in Philadelphia, the new guy believes he’s ready for this ultimate challenge. When practice starts next Wednesday at the Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia, millions of fans in the New York area will be wishing Harbaugh the best of luck. He’ll definitely need it. Harbaugh’s opening remarks to the 2026 Giants Fired Up 🔥 Giants Life: The Offseason drops tomorrow 👀 pic.twitter.com/sgE6OE1JXF — New York Giants (@Giants) July 22, 2026 Do the NY Giants have the best backup quarterback in the NFL? | The Record Beyond the ‘giggles’ and the jovial personality his new New York Giants teammates rave about, James Winston embraces everything that comes with playing quarterback in the NFL. The former Heisman Trophy winner is knowledgeable. He’s very serious when he needs to be serious, but at the same time he has a light energy about him, a calming essence both on and off the field. There’s also an accountability factor that Winston brings to the practice field and the classroom. He’s unafraid to call teammates out for not carrying out assignments or, say, for dropping passes, even on air during walkthroughs. PFF Tight End Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season | PFF 22. Isaiah Likely, New York Giants. Following an impressive four seasons as essentially the Ravens’ No. 2 tight end behind Mark Andrews, Likely followed head coach John Harbaugh to the Giants and will get his first real chance at being a starter. It was a rough 2025 season for Likely, as he missed three games due to a broken foot and registered a career-low 56.4 PFF grade. But in 2024, he placed seventh among all tight ends with 10 forced missed tackles, and his 75.6 PFF grade was sixth. 32. Theo Johnson, New York Giants. With Isaiah Likely joining the Giants, Johnson will likely get demoted to being New York’s No. 2 tight end. He was a worthy pass-catcher when he did start for the Giants last year, placing 19th with 528 receiving yards. Johnson’s five touchdown catches tied for 13th in the NFL, too. Giants roster bubble breakdown: Odell Beckham Jr., third QB question and draft busts hanging on | New York Post The NFL cliché is that no player’s job is safe after a regime change. Sometimes a new coach — especially one with final say over the roster, such as the Giants’ John Harbaugh — wants to send a message. Other times he just doesn’t care about an inherited hefty contract or high draft status that might have been saving a player on the bubble in the past. Giants legend raves about ‘great’ playoff expectations for Jaxson Dart and Co. | NJ.com The Giants need their prized quarterback, Jaxson Dart, to take the next step in Year 2, as coach John Harbaugh debuts in East Rutherford. And legendary former Giants quarterback Phil Simms thinks that will indeed happen. “I studied him a lot in college. As a pro — I watched him practice during the summer and play — and I just went, ‘Wow. This guy is a lot better than I thought.’ It caught me by surprise,” Simms said. “He really has the team in the palm of his hand. They all like him, they all know he’s really good, and he just has a way about him.” Re-Drafting the 2026 NFL Draft Before Training Camp: Flipping the First Round Upside Down | SI.com 5. New York Giants: Sonny Styles, LB (original selection: Arvell Reese). With Reese drafted by the Cardinals in this scenario, Sonny Styles becomes the straightforward selection for the New York Giants. In fact, with the Giants deciding to keep Reese at linebacker, you could argue choosing Styles, the more natural linebacker of the two, would have made more sense. John Harbaugh’s defense still lands a flexible front-seven defender. 10. New York Giants: Caleb Downs, S (original selection: Francis Mauigoa). We don’t necessarily have an issue with the Giants’ selection of Francis Mauigoa here, but safety Caleb Downs was the better overall prospect. Plus, knowing what we now know, keeping Downs away from their division rival Dallas Cowboys is a sweetener. If this scenario came to fruition, the Giants would feel inclined to sign a veteran starting guard like Kevin Zeitler. 50 days until the 2026 NFL season: Here are 50 under-the-radar players who could shape it | CBSSports.com 10. Darnell Mooney, New York Giants WR. Amid a disappointing 2024 for the Falcons, Mooney quietly impressed with 64 catches for 992 yards and five touchdowns while averaging a career-best 15.5 yards per catch — the seventh-highest mark in the league. Mooney dealt with lingering injuries in 2025, though, and finished with just 32 catches. The Giants would love to see him get back to his 2024 form, when he showed a well-rounded skill set that hadn’t been on display earlier in his career. 30. DJ Reader, New York Giants DT. For all the excitement surrounding Year 1 of John Harbaugh, Year 2 of Jaxson Dart and two first-round picks, the Giants still need to figure out a way to stop getting run all over; last year, they allowed an NFL-worst 5.3 yards per carry. They traded Dexter Lawrence away and didn’t find a replacement in the draft. Instead, the interior of the defensive line features Reader and other veterans. Join the conversation! title: ESPN: The NY Giants are top 10 in talent under age 25
summary: There are plenty of reasons for optimism around the New York Giants as training camp approaches. One of the biggest reasons for optimism as we march toward training camp? The youth on the Giants’ roster. In fact, ESPN’s Aaron Schatz ranks the Giants ninth in the NFL in terms of talent under the age of […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and running back Cam Skattebo | Brad Penner-Imagn Images There are plenty of reasons for optimism around the New York Giants as training camp approaches. One of the biggest reasons for optimism as we march toward training camp? The youth on the Giants’ roster. In fact, ESPN’s Aaron Schatz ranks the Giants ninth in the NFL in terms of talent under the age of 25 . The Giants feature one of the youngest rosters in the NFL and will be looking to their youngsters as contributors in every position group. The Giants have had a relatively young team for a while now, though that was masked by age outliers like Graham Gano, Russell Wilson, and Greg Van Roten. Now, the youth movement has become more obvious as the team has moved away from those veterans. ESPN summarized the Giants’ under-25 talent this way: Last year’s rank: 4 Blue chips: Edge Abdul Carter , QB Jaxson Dart , OT Francis Mauigoa , WR Malik Nabers , LB Arvell Reese Notable graduated players: S Tyler Nubin , Edge Kayvon Thibodeaux The Giants’ young talent is very top-heavy, with five recent first-round picks that I identified as blue chip players. The youngest among them is Reese, who is 20. Mauigoa is 21, and Carter is 22. Dart and Nabers are both 23. Below the first round of the draft, the Giants found running back Cam Skattebo , who is now 24. They also have cornerback Colton Hood (21) and nickelback Dru Phillips (24). Chris’ thoughts We’ve been saying for a while now that, despite an influx of veterans, the Giants have a lot of young talent. Seeing all their young players listed out like this just serves to drive that home, and it could bode well for their long-term prospects. In fact, the Giants may even have a deeper resevior of young talent than even Schatz lists. WR Malachi Fields is 22 years old and has the potential to be a go-to target in the endzone. Rookie LB Jack Kelly is 23, and has the chance to become a regular contributor on defense as well as special teams. If kicker Dominic Zvada returns to his 2024 form and proves to be a good NFL kicker, he could win the placekicking job. Zvada is 22 year. Longsnapper Ben Mann could likewise be a long-term answer for the special teams and is 24. As it stands, the Giants are the only team in the NFL with more than four “Blue Chip” players under the age of 24. If those other players can become significant contributors, half of their starters or regular contributors could be 24 or younger. That also, of course, doesn’t count players who would otherwise be considered “young” but are 25 and older. TE Theo Johnson , DL Darius Alexander and Bobby Jamison-Travis , and CB Deonte Banks are all 25, as are the aforementioned Thibodeaux and Nubin . TE Isaiah Likely , S Jevon Holland , RB Tyrone Tracy , CB Greg Newsome II, S Ar’Darius Washington and LB Micah McFadden are all 26. It’s also notable that the Giants are the only team in the NFC East that cracked the top half of the list. The Philadelphia Eagles ranked 18th, the Dallas Cowboys ranked 24th, and the Washington Commanders ranked 25th. In previous years, the Giants’ youth has been a double-edged sword, as mistakes and inexperience cost them games, and coaching staffs failed to develop the young talent. Now, however, the environment could be right for the Giants to finally get the most out of their youngsters. If the Giants can step up their player development, the fact that half of their (likely) 53-man roster could be 26 or younger cold set them up to be very competitive for a long time to come. Player development has, of course, been the Giants’ Achilles heel over the last decade and a half. However, if John Harbaugh can bring stability and an environment in which young players can reach their ceilings, the Giants’ youth could be one of their greatest strengths.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Cowboys, Eagles among NFL’s overrated teams, per The Athletic
summary: If prognosticators at The Athletic are correct, the New York Giants could be in the thick of a playoff race and perhaps a fight for the NFC East title in the final weeks of the 2026-27 NFL season. The commonly accepted over/under victory total for the Giants via oddsmakers has been 7.5. Using that number, […]
full_text: Dak Prescott | Getty Images If prognosticators at The Athletic are correct, the New York Giants could be in the thick of a playoff race and perhaps a fight for the NFC East title in the final weeks of the 2026-27 NFL season. The commonly accepted over/under victory total for the Giants via oddsmakers has been 7.5. Using that number, The Athletic’s Vic Tafur recently took the “over.” He wrote: I like to avoid crowds the older I get, but there’s no getting away from ( blows trumpet ) the most popular season-total bet of them all. Offensive guru Brian Daboll was pretty incompetent as the Giants’ coach and hit the bricks, and in walks Super Bowl winning coach John Harbaugh. He is going to have to tone down Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo — and hope Malik Nabers is back to full strength — but Harbaugh did bring along tight end Isaiah Likely to help. Harbaugh is also being gifted a nasty pass rush on defense. A big reason why I like this one so much is I also plan to get down on Abdul Carter at 50-1 as Defensive Player of the Year. He had more maturity issues than sacks (four) as a rookie last season, but the 18 QB hits and 66 pressures were impressive. Then, on Wednesday, Mike Jones of The Athletic took a look at overrated and underrated teams heading into the season. The Giants did not show up on either list. The NFC East rival Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles, though, both showed up on Jones’ list of “overrated” teams entering the year. Of the Cowboys, Jones wrote: Jerry Jones will tell you the Cowboys always have a shot at contention, and his team does generate plenty of buzz. But the Cowboys will have to jell in a hurry on defense, where new defensive coordinator Christian Parker inherits a unit that struggled mightily last season but added plenty of new faces, including veterans like pass rusher Rashan Gary, cornerback Cobie Durant, linebacker Dee Winters and rookie linebackers Malachi Lawrence and Jaishawn Barham. The offense, led by Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, should again put up points, but the much-needed defensive backing could take some time. Of the Eagles, Jones wrote: The Eagles have ranked among the elite teams of the NFC for the last 10 years, making the playoffs nine times and winning the Super Bowl twice. Even with last season’s regression, they won the NFC East for the third time in four seasons. But now they’re trying to re-tool on the fly, subtracting the disgruntled A.J. Brown and drafting Makai Lemon, rolling with their fourth offensive coordinator in as many years (rookie play caller Sean Mannion), and adding veterans Jonathan Greenard and Riq Woolen on defense while losing standouts Nakobe Dean and Reed Blankenship. The health of the offensive line is a concern, as is a tough late-season stretch . Although viewed as a bar-setter, the Eagles could hit a few snags this season. Valentine’s View Combine these two proposed scenarios, and it becomes probably the most optimistic scenario possible for the Giants in 2026. Can all of this happen? Maybe. The Giants have won a combined seven games the past two seasons. With John Harbaugh at head coach, I feel confident they can at least equal that total in 2026. My most optimistic predicted outcome is 9-8 . That might not get the Giants to the playoffs, but it would get them into the discussion. The Cowboys? I am well aware of all the hype. Honestly, though, isn’t it the same hype we have been hearing for three decades? Every year the Cowboys are supposed to be better than the year before. Every year is supposed to be the year they get back to a Super Bowl for the first time since 1995. Every year they disappoint. Wake me up when the Cowboys’ play actually matches the hype. As for the Eagles, I recognize what they have been for the last decade. They still have a ton of talent. They have, though, lost more than they have gained both on the roster and on the coaching staff. I have felt for a while that the Eagles could be in for some regression this season.

title: Survey: Which camp battle do you most want to see?
summary: The New York Giants 2026 training camp is almost here. The Giants are set at several positions, like quarterback and linebacker. However, the arrival of John Harbaugh means that the Giants done work in tinkering with their roster to make it more competitive. There are also a number of players getting clean slates and opportunities […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants receiver Malachi Fields catches a pass in practice | Thomas Salus-Imagn Images The New York Giants 2026 training camp is almost here. The Giants are set at several positions, like quarterback and linebacker. However, the arrival of John Harbaugh means that the Giants done work in tinkering with their roster to make it more competitive. There are also a number of players getting clean slates and opportunities to compete for starting jobs. In other words, this year might have more and more lively camp battles than we’ve seen in recent years from the Giants. So with that in mind, we want to know which camp battles you’re most interested in seeing this year? Cornerback – The headline here is free agent acquisition (and 2021 first-round pick) Greg Newsome II trying to hold off 2023 first-round pick Deonte Banks. Newsome entered the spring as the starter, however Banks has seemingly taken to the new scheme and coaching well. He’s earned more first team snaps over the course of OTA’s and minicamp, and reportedly looked good in the process. 2026 second-round pick Colton Hood is waiting in the wings as well, and could leapfrog both players if they stumble in camp. Defensive line – The Giants need to find three new starters on their defensive line following the departures of Dexter Lawrence and Rakeem Nunez-Roches, as well as the injury to Roy Robertson-Harris. One is expected to be veteran nose tackle D.J. Reader, but who will start next to him? 2025 third-round pick Darius Alexander has the inside track, as does veteran Shelby Harris. We haven’t seen Sam Roberts yet this off-season, but he was also one of the Giants’ first free agent signings. Likewise, rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis has the chance to surprise and be a primary rotational player. This position is wide open. Wide receiver – Another position in a state of flux. The Giants not only need to replace Wan’Dale Robinson, but also weather the period until Malik Nabers is able to return to the field. The Giants have 14 receivers on their 90-man roster, with a heady mix of young players like Malachi Fields and Calvin Austin III, big-name veterans in Odell Beckham jr. and Ju-Ju Smith-Schuster, and blue collar vets looking to reestablish their worth, like Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, and Isaiah Hodgins. The Giants’ first priority is building around around Jaxson Dart, so how will they construct their receiver room? Kicker – The Giants kicker position has been a sore spot for years now. The Giants have struggled to field a consistent kicking game thanks to the injuries suffered by Graham Gano and poor planning behind him. We thought the position was solved with the signing of veteran kicker Jason Sanders, but he was a surprise cut during the spring. Instead, the kicker competition is seemingly down to three-game veteran Ben Sauls and undrafted rookie Dominic Zvada. Teams typically like a their specialists to be proven with track records of consistency. The fact that John Harbaugh’s Giants are deciding between two inexperienced options is one of the biggest surprises of the offseason. Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys.

title: NY Giants training camp: Predicting 6 camp battles
summary: The New York Giants 2026 training camp is just a week away. In previous years, it’s seemed like the roster was pretty much set by the time that year’s draft wrapped up. There were a few opportunities for competition in training camp, but for the most part we knew what the roster and depth chart […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks in practice. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants 2026 training camp is just a week away. In previous years, it’s seemed like the roster was pretty much set by the time that year’s draft wrapped up. There were a few opportunities for competition in training camp, but for the most part we knew what the roster and depth chart would look like. That doesn’t appear to be the case for 2026. As things stand now, there is the potential for competition across the roster in John Harbaugh’s first year. Some position groups are likely set, but there are plenty where it remains to be seen just how the depth chart takes shape. We could be in for some real surprises once the preseason wraps up and final cutdowns are made. So, just for fun, we’ll take a stab at predicting how some of the most important camp battles could play out. Cornerback Deonte Banks is again fighting for a starting cornerback job, but with a couple of key differences from last season. To start, this time he’s the underdog fighting for a spot. Last year, he was the incumbent starter trying to fight off Cor’Dale Flott, who was trying to win a big second contract. This year, it was widely assumed that either Greg Newsome II or Colton Hood would take the starting job across from Paulson Adebo. The second difference is that the Giants have returned to the type of defense that Banks was drafted to play in. And so Banks has made a fight of it, earning starting reps through OTA’s and mini-camp. The training camp battle for the starting job seems to be Banks against Newsome, while Hood is developing on the second team. Prediction: Banks wins the starting job. I wouldn’t have predicted this a few months ago, but we’ve seen enough reports of him being a top performer in practices to think that he’s taking well to the new scheme and coaching. If so, his elite athletic traits and ability to force tight coverages work well with what Wilson wants to run. Likewise, Banks has primarily played the left side, which would allow Paulson Adebo to stick to the right side. Kicker Kickers are people too! And considering how important the kicking game has been to the Giants over the past few years, this definitely deserves to be mentioned early in our rundown. This camp battle is a straight-up kicker’s duel between undrafted rookie Dominick Zvada and wily veteran (of three games) Ben Sauls. Zvada comes into training camp with the perceived lead in the battle, as he has been the Giants’ most consistent kicker throughout the off-season program. That said, Sauls was perfect on field goals (8 for 8) and extra points (7 for 7) in three games for the Giants a year ago. Prediction: Zvada wins the competition outright. Sauls being reliable on gameday counts for a lot in his favor. Teams have little patience for inconsistent specialists, and Sauls being reliable in the regular season has to be considered. However, he hasn’t been consistent through the spring, and he won’t have much hope if he can’t be consistent in camp. Zvada, meanwhile, was inconsistent at Michigan last year — granted, that was a nightmare season for the program as a whole. However, he was truly elite in 2024, going 7-7 on attempts over 50 yards and his only miss being a blocked kick. His leg strength and consistency this spring and summer carry the day. It’s also worth noting that both players are also competing against every kicker who is in danger of being cut after the preseason as well. Wide receiver The Giants have a spectacularly crowded wide receiver room. This isn’t so much a camp battle, as a scrum to not only see how the depth chart shakes out, but which of the 14 receivers on the Giants’ 90-man roster will even make the final 53-man roster. Malik Nabers is entrenched at the top of the depth chart, while rookie Malachi Fields and veteran Darius Slayton are all but locks to make the roster. But there are nothing but questions everywhere else. The Giants have questions as to who will be the other starting receivers apart from Nabers, who will fill out the depth chart, and who will be special teams contributors. Prediction: Malik Nabers starts the season on the PUP list. Darnell Mooney, Darius Slayton, and Malachi Fields are the Giants’ (initial) top 3 receivers. Calvin Austin, Odell Beckham Jr., and Braxton Berrios round out the initial depth chart. Defensive tackle Much like the wide receiver position, the Giants have a lot of defensive tackles but few clear answers as to how this position shakes out. The Giants currently have 11 true defensive linemen on their roster (12 if you count Chauncey Golston), with plenty of opportunities for players to earn rotational or even starting jobs. The Giants’ plans at defensive tackle suddenly went sideways after Dexter Lawrence demanded a trade. Now it seems as though they plan to stock the front with space-eaters while their athletic linebackers and edge defenders create pressure and chaos. Prediction: DJ Reader is the starting nose tackle, as expected. Rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis emerges as the second nose tackle Darius Alexander and Sam Roberts emerge as the starting defensive tackles alongside Reader, with Shelby Harris and Golston playing a rotational role. Third safety There are probably some fans muttering “Really? Third safety? Who cares about that?” right now. The answer is “NFL Defenses”, particularly those in the “Ravens 2.0” mold. That means that the battle between Ar’Darius Washington and Jason Pinnock could become one of the most important in Giants’ camp. Having a versatile nickel defender who fits the “STAR” mold is key to the type of defense Harbaugh and Dennard Wilson want to run. Washington filled that role for the Ravens in 2024 and played exceptionally well. Jason Pinnock, meanwhile, played relatively well in Wink Martindale’s scheme (the Ravens 2.0 scheme’s immediate antecedent) for the Giants in 2022 and 2023. Washington more fully blends safety and cornerback skills, but Pinnock is a bigger player. Prediction: Ar’Darius Washington wins the third safety job outright and becomes a fan favorite. Not only does he have experience playing under Dennard Wilson and John Harbaugh, but we’ve seen him do so at a very high level. Jason Pinnock is a solid safety and a useful player to have around as high-level depth. However, Washington was playing at a near-elite level before being injured and could become one of the pivot players who allows the Giants to field a dynamic modern defense. Left guard So far, Jon Runyan Jr. has been the clear starter at left guard, with Daniel Faalele, Joshua Ezeudu, Evan Neal, and Aaron Stinnie filling out the depth chart. However, Runyan Jr. doesn’t really fit the mold for the type of blocking schemes Greg Roman uses in his run play designs. Complicating matters is the fact that Runyan carries an $11.75 million cap number, and cutting him would create $9.25 million in cap space. That would almost double the Giants’ cap space and give them the flexibility to sign players in the event of injury or perhaps even maneuver on the trade market. All of that means that a camp battle may in fact materialize once the pads go on and linemen can start run blocking for real. Prediction: Runyan becomes a cap casualty, with Faalele assuming the left guard spot. Faalele has experience blocking for Harbaugh as well as playing in Greg Roman’s schemes. It would also reunite Faalele with his former teammate John Michael Schmitz, who was his linemate at Minnesota from 2018 to 2021. It seems highly unlikely right now that Evan Neal will make real noise in his quest to continue his NFL career with the Giants; it’s possible that could change once the pads go on. He remains a massively powerful man with good feet for a guard and real ability as a run blocker. He could be a dark horse.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants news: John Harbaugh on Cam Skattebo backflip, Jaxson Dart
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. The Giants’ knucklehead circus is the NFL’s most fascinating powderkeg | SB Nation As much as there is to love, there are two intentionally absent names who are the most critical elements of a successful campaign in 2026: Jaxson […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. The Giants’ knucklehead circus is the NFL’s most fascinating powderkeg | SB Nation As much as there is to love, there are two intentionally absent names who are the most critical elements of a successful campaign in 2026: Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo, the frat-boy wild cards capable of either ushering in a new era of success in East Rutherford or tanking everything through their own foolishness. It’s unclear how much their penchant for stupidity is real or played up for the camera, but they are exceedingly good at raising eyebrows. To mesh that approach to football with two guys running on vibes is a powder keg. It’s not just simply that they’re willing to hurt themselves, but this loose approach to football is very difficult to manage. Once freedom and personality run supreme, it can be very difficult to pull that all in, and let it fester too long as a team can pull itself apart as everyone is looking out for No. 1 over everything else. John Harbaugh impressed by Jaxson Dart John Harbaugh on if he’s been surprised about anything after getting to work with #Giants QB Jaxson Dart: “I don’t know about surprised, probably just impressed more than anything. I do think he’s obsessed. I believe he really really wants to be good.” (Via Bleav in Giants) pic.twitter.com/WkNrg5ipdG — The Giants Report (@GiantsReport1) July 21, 2026 Giants leaders aren’t just telling Jaxson Dart to run more carefully. They’re showing him | Yahoo Sports So as new Giants staffers settled in, Nagy queued up clips to remind Dart that visits to the blue tent — in the preseason, in his first start and repeatedly through the season — compromise his availability. The goal is not to eliminate Dart’s confidence and swagger. But the Giants are working to hone their young quarterback’s risk-reward calculus. “You can’t just say, ‘Don’t run the football here, because you could get hurt’ — you have to show him the evidence,” said Nagy. ” ‘Where did you take the extra hits? Was it necessary?’ You have to show them clips.” Previewing the top storylines for 2026 NFL training camps | ESPN.com Five injuries to monitor. Malik Nabers, WR, New York Giants. No injury has made more offseason headlines than Nabers’. The Giants’ star receiver tore his right ACL in Week 4 of the 2025 season and underwent surgery to repair the ligament, as well as the damage to his meniscus, a month later. But this past spring, Nabers had to undergo a second procedure on the same knee — a sign that his recovery was likely not going well. Nabers was a highly impactful rookie: 109 catches on 170 targets for 1,204 yards in only 15 games. His evident ascent to the Giants’ No. 1 receiver role was a contributing factor in the team’s willingness to let Wan’Dale Robinson leave in free agency after a strong 2025 season. For depth, the Giants have added tons of veteran dart throws — Calvin Austin III, Darnell Mooney, JuJu Smith-Schuster, Braxton Berrios and even Odell Beckham Jr. — in the hope that someone will be able to fill Robinson’s snaps. If Nabers has to miss regular-season time, the Giants’ receiving core might be one of the oldest and least effective in the league. Assistant coaches who could break out in 2026 for all 32 NFL teams | The Athletic New York Giants: Charlie Bullen, outside linebackers/run game coordinator. John Harbaugh has always had an eye for coaching talent, and it speaks well of Bullen’s potential that he was retained from the previous coaching regime and even got an expanded role as run game coordinator. His position group already featured Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux; the team also drafted versatile defender Arvell Reese in the spring. Bullen will have every opportunity to show his impact on the defense. New York Jets Last year’s rank: 28 Blue chips: Edge David Bailey, OT Armand Membou Notable graduated players: RB Breece Hall, G Joe Tippmann Here’s our first team that doesn’t have a young quarterback, unless you want to count 22-year-old fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik. No, the leader of the youth for the Jets is No. 2 pick Bailey, who will be 23 in August. The Jets’ defense also has 24-year-old safety Malachi Moore, 22-year-old cornerback Azareye’h Thomas and 21-year-old nickelback D’Angelo Ponds. On offense, the young talent is led by the bookends of the line, with left tackle Olu Fashanu now 23 and right tackle Membou just 22. First-round wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is 22, and Adonai Mitchell — acquired from the Colts last season in the Sauce Gardner deal — is still just 23. At tight end, the Jets have 16th pick Kenyon Sadiq, who doesn’t turn 22 until March, along with 22-year-old Mason Taylor. Two things are notable to me. First is that as Schatz notes, the Jets are the top ranked team without a young quarterback, Obviously that will be a key piece to fill in, but it shows the team is attempting to build a new youthful core. I think the trajectory is worth noting. A year ago, the Jets rated near the bottom at 28th. It isn’t a huge surprise to see such a leap after four selections in the top 50 of the NFL Draft, but with three additional first round picks to come in 2027 the Jets could turn their team around quickly with the right picks.

title: Scouting Jets UDFA offensive lineman Courtland Ford
summary: Over the last few months, we’ve been breaking down all undrafted free agents signed by the Jets. We conclude today with former UCLA offensive lineman Courtland Ford. The 25-year Old Ford is listed at 6’6” and 315 pounds and played in 46 games in his career, starting 25 at three different positions. In addition to […]
full_text: PASADENA, CA - OCTOBER 04: UCLA Bruins offensive lineman Courtland Ford #77 celebrates the Bruins win following a college football game between the UCLA Bruins and the Penn State Nittany Lions on October 4, 2025, at the Rose Bowl in PASADENA, CA.(Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the last few months, we’ve been breaking down all undrafted free agents signed by the Jets. We conclude today with former UCLA offensive lineman Courtland Ford. The 25-year Old Ford is listed at 6’6” and 315 pounds and played in 46 games in his career, starting 25 at three different positions. In addition to UCLA, he also played for USC and Kentucky. Background Ford was a three-star high school recruit, who initially headed to USC in 2020. He would redshirt his first season, although he did start one game at left guard in his only appearance, with USC winning that matchup. As a redshirt freshman, he started the first eight games at left tackle but then only made one more appearance off the bench as he was sidelined by injuries and illness. In 2022, he played in 10 of 14 games, starting three, and opted to enter the transfer portal at the end of the year. Having moved to Kentucky, he was again affected by injuries as he was limited to two starts in two seasons. He only appeared in two games in 2024. He transferred again, this time to UCLA, and got a chance to start 11 games last season, albeit with mixed results. Having not been invited to the scouting combine, Ford was hurt at his pro day and wasn’t able to complete a full workout, hurting his already slim chances of being drafted. Ford was not one of the first round of undrafted free agents signed by the Jets but they signed him after he attended their rookie minicamp on a tryout basis. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Ford brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Ford has nice size and above average length but may need to bulk up and add some strength. He previously was reported to have worked hard on his body and physique at USC. His pro day workout was affected by an injury so you can perhaps throw out his disappointing numbers (12 bench press reps and 5.46 in the short shuttle). Usage Ford’s only action in his true freshman season was an emergency start at left guard, although that was the only time in his career he played inside. He otherwise played primarily at left tackle, other than at Kentucky where he started two games on the right in 2023. He played a few snaps as tight end in jumbo or unbalanced packages. Pass Blocking When Ford arrived at UCLA in 2025, he hadn’t given up a sack since 2021, but he gave up eight in his lone season with the Bruins. He had also given up three in his eight starts as a redshirt freshman. His pressure rate wasn’t too bad as a college player but it was higher in 2025 than the rest of his career, perhaps because he was left on an island more due to his experience. He moves his feet pretty well to stay in front of his man but struggles in particular against speed-to-power moves. One thing he does well is to redirect his man, or shove him to the ground to keep him away from the quarterback. His struggles to anchor can be a major weakness though. Run Blocking Run blocking was also an area where Ford was inconsistent. However, he displays good strength at the point of attack. He has the ability to execute on a combo block and then transition to climbing up to the second level. Ford also shows flashes of an ability to get out on the move and lock onto or angle off his man in space. Short Yardage UCLA didn’t have much success at the goal line last year with only eight rushing touchdowns all season as a team, including four by the quarterback. Ford did a good job on this 3rd-and-short run that he helped spring for a much bigger gain. Screen Blocking UCLA also didn’t have much success in the screen game last year, with two key turnovers on screens and no big plays. They were much more effective during Ford’s USC days, although most of these were receiver screens or plays where Ford was staying in to block rather than getting downfield. Footwork/Technique Pad level was a constant issue for the 6’6” Ford, who lets his base get narrow at times and this hurts his ability to anchor. His handwork needs some refinement, although he battles for leverage. He can be late or inaccurate with his hands and susceptible to swipes and chops. His footwork is pretty good, especially when mirroring in pass protection. He also impresses with his ability to fire off the line. He has previously said that he models his game on former Jets tackle Tyron Smith. Penalties Penalties had a tendency to come in bunches for Ford, who didn’t have any in his first four career starts but then had six in his next five starts. Last season, he had eight penalties in the first six games but then was penalty-free in the last five games. Those eight penalties included four for offensive holding and four of them came in one game. Special Teams Ford’s only special teams role during his career has been as a blocker on the placekicking unit, during which time he had no significant mistakes. He did not play special teams at all last season. Instincts/Intelligence Ford’s high school head coach has previously praised Ford for being smart with a great football IQ. At Kentucky, his offensive line coach called him “wise beyond his years”. He had mixed results in terms of reacting to and passing off stunts, though. Three of his penalties last year were false starts and one was for illegal man downfield on a pass. Attitude Ford became a leader with UCLA last year, as one of their older and more experienced players. He was previously praised by his high school’s running backs coach for his humility and work ethic. Injuries Ford had some injury issues over his career, the most disruptive of which was probably his 2024 wrist injury which required surgery and limited him to two appearances. In 2021, he missed one game with a leg injury and two due to illness (mono). He then had an offseason procedure after the 2022 season that limited him in the spring. His pro day workout was affected by an ankle issue. Scheme Fit Ford looks certain to be one of the third team tackles heading into preseason. His experience in multiple college programs should be useful and he has experience of zone and man blocking schemes. He has been a teammate of current Jets running back Chip Trayanum while at Kentucky. Conclusions Ford may not bring much in the way of college success or accolades and perhaps doesn’t have as much upside as some of the Jets’ other undrafted rookies but he’ll get a chance to compete for a role in camp. The Jets aren’t exactly overflowing with depth on the offensive line but there are enough experienced players ahead of him that it seems unlikely that Ford will sniff a spot on the 53 unless there are multiple injuries. His best bet is to establish himself as a dependable worker, who will practice hard and can show that he’s capable of holding his own in preseason. That could earn him a spot on the practice squad.

title: Eagles schedule preview: Steelers
summary: When and where: Week 10 at home following the bye Key additions: HC Mike McCarthy, CB Jamel Dean, RB Rico Dowdle, WR Michael Pittman Key subtractions: HC Mike Tomlin, G Isaac Seumalo, RB Kenneth Gainwell Last season: Energy vampire Aaron Rodgers came to town and took Mike Tomlin’s will to coach The question for this […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts during the first quarter of the game Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images When and where: Week 10 at home following the bye Key additions: HC Mike McCarthy, CB Jamel Dean, RB Rico Dowdle, WR Michael Pittman Key subtractions: HC Mike Tomlin, G Isaac Seumalo, RB Kenneth Gainwell Last season: Energy vampire Aaron Rodgers came to town and took Mike Tomlin’s will to coach The question for this team: How much of the Steelers was held together by Mike Tomlin? Mike Tomlin hadn’t won a playoff game since 2016. Over the years a growing segment of Steelers fans pointed to him as the reason why the team could not advance in January. His QBs were a collection of old guys: an aging Ben Roethlisberger, Kenny Pickett, the remains of Russell Wilson, and 42 year old Aaron Rodgers. Hard to win with that. And yet, Tomlin kept winning, infamously never having a losing season. Tomlin was probably past his expiration date, but the Steelers weren’t going to boot him unless they had to. Tomlin made it easy for everyone and decided to walk away. With no head coach or QB under contract but with the rest of the roster aging but playoff caliber, the Steelers had the rare opportunity to reset the direction of the franchise without having to reset the roster. Instead, they brought back Aaron Rodgers and hired 62-year-old Mike McCarthy. McCarthy has done absolutely nothing to shake the idea that he got the job in part because he spent a summer working a turnpike toll booth. Presumably the interview was catered by Primanti Brothers, if not at it. In no way, shape, or form is McCarthy an upgrade from Tomlin. He doesn’t bring any energy, new ideas, or an A-list staff. He isn’t a guy who just wins, as he’s had four losing seasons in his last seven, and was fired twice. Since Tomlin’s last playoff win McCarthy has just one playoff win and three appearances. Sometimes the most uninspiring hire of a coaching cycle turns out to be the best because no one knows who is a good head coach until they’re a head coach. There’s no mystery with McCarthy, we know who and what he is. He underachieved with Aaron Rodgers in his prime in Green Bay, and now he gets the totally cooked version of him in Pittsburgh. With little changes to the team other than head coach, we are going to find out this year just how important Mike Tomlin was to the Steelers. The guess is, quite important.

title: Eagles News: “There’s a huge mystery right now in Philadelphia”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Previewing the top storylines for 2026 NFL training camps – ESPNWhat does the Eagles’ offense look like? Two mainstays of the Eagles’ recent Super Bowl runs are noticeably absent from their 2026 offense. One is very apparent: wide receiver A.J. Brown. From 2022 to 2025, […]
full_text: Jun 10, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during minicamp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Previewing the top storylines for 2026 NFL training camps – ESPN What does the Eagles’ offense look like? Two mainstays of the Eagles’ recent Super Bowl runs are noticeably absent from their 2026 offense. One is very apparent: wide receiver A.J. Brown. From 2022 to 2025, no NFL receiver had a greater share of his team’s receiving yards than Brown (32.6%), and only two (Tyreek Hill and Puka Nacua) had more yards per route run. Brown was particularly valuable to quarterback Jalen Hurts as a safety valve against man coverage. Simply put, to remove him is to remove a keystone of the Eagles’ offense. With Brown goes Jeff Stoutland, the team’s offensive line coach since 2013. He’s a less evident absence, but perhaps a more impactful one. The Eagles’ offensive line was the best in the league during their championship runs, but last season’s group suffered mightily with injury and will have a lot asked of them in new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s under-center, play-action, motion-heavy system. This is the sort of modern offense that doesn’t immediately and obviously jell with Hurts’ strengths, as reporting has covered his commitment to more static offensive systems. Regardless of how highly Hurts ranks among league quarterbacks, there’s no question that Brown and the O-line were massive factors to the Eagles’ offensive success under Nick Sirianni. Enormous pressure is on the shoulders of Mannion, who doesn’t have much experience but did coach in Green Bay, where he helped Matt LaFleur wonderfully adjust the Sean McVay scheme for both Aaron Rodgers and Jordan Love. Pressure is also on Hurts and Nick Sirianni to help Mannion blend that offense with a Philadelphia system that has largely worked across multiple seasons and multiple offensive coordinators. Trickle-down pressure lands on players such as wide receiver DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley, too. There’s a huge mystery right now in Philadelphia. Eagles Rookie Review: Andrew Mukuba is a very important defender entering Year 2 – BGN I think Andrew Mukuba is one of the most important players on the Eagles’ defense heading into 2026. Not because he’s already one of their best defenders, but because there are still so many possible outcomes and he is expected to be ‘the guy’ at safety. The Bull Case: The instincts continue to stand out, the understanding of Fangio’s defense takes another leap forward, the tackling becomes more controlled, and the physical questions gradually fade away. If that happens, the Eagles will have found themselves a long-term starting safety with outstanding football intelligence and the kind of range that every modern defense covets. I mean, come on… 61 NFL predictions ahead of the 2026 season – SB Nation Eagles start season 0-2. After the back-and-forth shootout with the Commanders in which they fall short, the Eagles travel to Tennessee to face the Titans. In terms of survivor pools, many pick the Eagles with such hubris, but are stunned to see that Robert Saleh’s defense does what it did to Hurts in the divisional round this past January. Hurts struggles, throwing a pair of interceptions, including the game-sealing pick to Kevin Winston Jr which locks up a 20-17 win for Tennessee, putting the Eagles in an early 0-2 hole. NFL’s underrated and overrated teams in 2026: NFL South could rise; Bears, Bills, Patriots tumble – The Athletic Overrated — Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles have ranked among the elite teams of the NFC for the last 10 years, making the playoffs nine times and winning the Super Bowl twice. Even with last season’s regression, they won the NFC East for the third time in four seasons. But now they’re trying to re-tool on the fly, subtracting the disgruntled A.J. Brown and drafting Makai Lemon, rolling with their fourth offensive coordinator in as many years (rookie play caller Sean Mannion), and adding veterans Jonathan Greenard and Riq Woolen on defense while losing standouts Nakobe Dean and Reed Blankenship. The health of the offensive line is a concern, as is a tough late-season stretch. Although viewed as a bar-setter, the Eagles could hit a few snags this season. [BLG Note: The Dallas Cowboys are also in the overrated section.] Ranking the Eagles’ 20 most valuable trade assets – PhillyVoice 13) HC Nick Sirianni: Second-round pick. Man, I really struggled with where to put Sirianni on this list. And again, disclaimer, as noted in the Fangio section above, any trade of a head coach would require the coach’s consent. […] The pros: Sirianni has a 59-26 record as a head coach. He has never missed the playoffs, and he has been to two Super Bowls, winning one. That’s, uh, pretty damn good. The cons: He is coming off a really bad season in which the team appeared dysfunctional both from a culture and offensive scheme perspective, and he has a personality that won’t be for many owners. I landed on a second-round pick. [BLG Note: Would you be willing to trade Nick Sirianni for less than a second-round pick? Genuinely curious.] Year 3 for the D – Iggles Blitz We know Vic Fangio is a great defensive coordinator. The big question is whether the Eagles have the right players. There is no disputing they are very talented, but you still need the right combination of skill sets and personalities. I think the real key is Jalen Carter. He can be a true difference-maker up front. If he’s healthy and locked in, I think the defense will be great. Carter wasn’t in top form or completely healthy last season and the defense was erratic at times. When he’s right, the D is on a different level. The secondary should be one of the best in the league with Riq Woolen as CB2. Quinyon Mitchell might be the best CB in the league and is critical to how Fangio plans his looks and coverages. Jonathan Greenard: ‘We are working our tails off’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com The Eagles made headlines in April with the acquisition of outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard via a trade with the Minnesota Vikings. The Pro Bowl pass rusher is only one season removed from a 2024 campaign that saw him reach at least 12 sacks for a second year in a row. Greenard battled injuries last year in Minnesota but is expected to participate in team drills come Training Camp next week. “I had surgery back in December, so I’m just working back in,” Greenard said during June’s minicamp. “I feel pretty confident. (The team has) a good plan to get me back in and be ready to go for camp.” While Greenard hasn’t been able to participate in team drills, the former Florida Gator has been practicing with the team throughout the offseason in OTAs and minicamp. Already, he is impressed with the team culture. “We work as a championship team,” Greenard said. “Attention to detail is there, we are working our tails off. Even after practice, we’re doing extra drills just to make sure we’re all on the same page.” Taking a closer look at Eagles’ backup OL battle in 2026 training camp – NBCSP Michael Jordan. Age: 28. Experience: Year 7. Size: 6-foot-6, 315 pounds. Jordan is a former fourth-round pick of the Bengals who has some significant NFL experience. He has played in 78 games with 49 starts in his NFL career and started 9 games for the Buccaneers just last season. The Eagles brought him in for a tryout this spring and then signed him to a contract. That doesn’t mean he’s going to make the team, but the Eagles did look a little light on the interior of their line in the depth department so the signing made sense. Among 79 qualified guards last season, Jordan was ranked 69th by PFF. full_text: May 21, 2026; East Rutherford, NJ, USA; New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks at a press conference during organized team activities at Quest Diagnostics Training Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | John Jones-Imagn Images When and where: Week 9 at home, Week 18 in New Jersey Key additions: HC John Harbaugh, LB Tremaine Edmunds, WR Darnell Mooney, half of the Ravens roster Key subtractions: DT Dexter Lawrence, WR Wan’Dale Robinson, LB Bobby Okereke Last season: Brian Daboll, who was not fired a year ago for appearances, was fired The question for this team: Is John Harbaugh a magician? John Harbaugh is here and he is going to fix everything. Never mind that he’s coming off his worst season in a decade, and possibly his career. Never mind that he only won 4 playoff games in his last 13 years. Never mind that he thought he was taking Todd Monken with him only for Monken to take the Browns job, leaving him to turn to Matt Nagy. Never mind that he is leaving one of the better run teams from top to bottom to one of the worst. Because John Harbaugh is here and he is going to fix everything! There’s a lot that needs to be fixed. In 9 of Harbaugh’s 18 years in Baltimore, the Ravens had a top 3 scoring defense. The Giants were 26th in 2025 and haven’t had a top 3 finish in a decade. Harbaugh traded not just his best defensive player but one of the better interior defensive linemen for 1 (one) draft pick. The Giants signed 22 players in free agency, almost all to one year contracts, and most of those to minimum deals. And in addition to signing five former Ravens, the Giants also signed 11 players who Harbaugh coached against last year. In June the Giants brought in JuJu Smith-Schuster, Braxton Berrios, and Odell Beckham for workouts, which seemed like a joke. They signed all three. The Giants have speed run to the “sign guys the coach has heard of” phase of poor roster construction. The Giants also did the classic “it’s a new era” move and replaced their long snapper. Harbaugh does bring competence to the Giants, something they haven’t had in a decade. But you don’t give a coach top of the line salary to achieve competence. You don’t drag out contract negotiations, with details leaking out daily, just to get competence. For 2026, competence will be progress. A four or five win improvement would be significant, and give Harbaugh even more reason to sign some more former Ravens or guys he coached against in 2027. But for all their moves it’s not clear that the Giants even improved their roster. They haven’t significantly improved their skill position players to help Jaxson Dart, their defense has not only not significantly improved it has possibly gotten worse, and their playcallers are uninspiring. The Giants are putting a lot of faith in the magic beans of John Harbaugh. Ben McAdoo was fired in his second season, Pat Shurmur and Joe Judge after their second seasons, and Brian Daboll should have been fired after his third but John Mara didn’t want to seem reactionary and fire him in the offseason, instead firing him during the season. How long does Harbaugh last?

full_text: After a tumultuous first season in black and gold, it’s fair to wonder if the Steelers are having any second thoughts about the trade they made to acquire DK Metcalf last March. Pittsburgh sent a second-round pick to the Seattle Seahawks for the receiver, who they immediately handed a 4-year 132 million dollar extension. While Seattle went on to win the Super Bowl, Pittsburgh suffered another first-round exit, with Metcalf posting under 1,000 yards in his first season with the franchise. Pro Football Focus ranked NFL wide receivers entering 2026 , with Metcalf coming in at number 26. “In his first season with Pittsburgh, Metcalf led the Steelers with 850 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns.,” Wasserman and Chadwick wrote . “His 1.83 yards per route run ranked among the top 30 qualified wide receivers despite posting a career-low 11.3-yard average depth of target because of Aaron Rodgers‘ conservative tendencies. The additions of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard should help alleviate some of the pressure on Metcalf to carry the Steelers’ passing game.” DK METCALF MY GOODNESS MIAvsPIT on ESPN/ABC Stream on @NFLPlus and ESPN App pic.twitter.com/GXEbzt3p4h — NFL (@NFL) December 16, 2025 This ranking of Metcalf seems to be the consensus on him entering his second season with Pittsburgh. Jarrett Bailey and I tackled where we believe Metcalf sits among NFL wide receivers just a few weeks ago. The Steelers wide receiver one is in a similar range in both of our rankings, as compared to the PFF list. As the article mentioned, things are looking up for Metcalf in 2026. He will have another offseason with Aaron Rodgers under his belt, with some added weapons to the wide receiver room that should mean defenses won’t be able to key in on Metcalf as much as they were last year. Mike McCarthy’s offense is also traditionally much more pass-heavy and sees multiple receivers on the field at a time. full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 3: Kenny Pickett #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Acrisure Stadium on December 3, 2023 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been an eventful two years for former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Kenny Pickett. After the Steelers went 3-0 down the stretch to close the 2023 season under Mason Rudolph, clinching a playoff berth in the process, the writing appeared to be on the wall for the University of Pittsburgh product. The Steelers signed Russell Wilson on the first day of the 2024 league year, which led to Pickett requesting a trade. Pittsburgh sent him to Philadelphia, and he was the backup quarterback to Jalen Hurts when the Eagles defeated the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX. In the 2025 offseason, Pickett was traded once again, as he was dealt to the Cleveland Browns for a fourth-round pick. According to Pickett’s former college coach, Pat Narduzzi, the trade away from Philadelphia is a move that Pickett wanted very badly. “The Eagles did not want to trade him,” Narduzzi said on 99.9 The Fan . “He begged to be traded because he wanted to compete, and he felt like he wasn’t going to have a chance to beat out Jalen Hurts.” Pickett competed throughout the spring and summer of 2025 to be the Browns’ starter alongside Joe Flacco, Dillon Gabriel, and Shedeur Sanders. When it was made clear Flacco would be the starter, the Browns traded Pickett to the Las Vegas Raiders. He now finds himself with the Carolina Panthers after signing as a free agent. title: Ben Roethlisberger says Steelers should release Mason Rudolph
summary: As training camps around the NFL begin to open, the Pittsburgh Steelers have one of the NFL’s biggest quarterback questions. Aaron Rodgers will certainly be the team’s starter in 2026, but the Steelers have three players behind him who will battle for roster spots. Pittsburgh drafted Drew Allar in the third round in this past […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Quarterbacks Ben Roethlisberger #7 and Mason Rudolph #2of the Pittsburgh Steelers warm up before the start of their game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 01, 2020 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) | Getty Images As training camps around the NFL begin to open, the Pittsburgh Steelers have one of the NFL’s biggest quarterback questions. Aaron Rodgers will certainly be the team’s starter in 2026, but the Steelers have three players behind him who will battle for roster spots. Pittsburgh drafted Drew Allar in the third round in this past April’s draft, so his spot is as safe as any of the three backups, leaving Will Howard and Mason Rudolph to battle it out for the potential final roster spot. Former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger weighed in with his opinion on the latest edition of Footbahlin with Ben Roethlisberger , saying the best thing Pittsburgh could do at quarterback would be to keep Howard and Allar and release Rudolph. “Personally, I think [cutting Rudolph] the smarter move,” Roethlisberger said. “You want to have two young guys because one of those could be your potential quarterback for the next five to ten years.” Roethlisberger and Rudolph notoriously have a rough history. Roethlisberger wasn’t happy to see the team use a third-round pick on a quarterback in 2018 when they had just won 13 games the year before. Rudolph also made claims that Roethlisberger gave preferential treatment to other backups over him. Roethlisberger then said that he tried to help Rudolph, but that the Oklahoma State product indicated he didn’t want help. Howard has yet to take an NFL snap, exhibition or regular season, as he missed the 2025 preseason with a hand injury. Rudolph started one game in 2025 in a losing effort to the Chicago Bears, although he helped lead the Steelers to a win the previous week as he came in for relief of an injured Aaron Rodgers against the Cincinnati Bengals. title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy named coach on hot seat in 2026
summary: Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin sent shockwaves throughout the football world after announcing that he would be stepping down from his position after the team’s loss in the AFC Wild Card playoffs to the Houston Texans. Pittsburgh wasted no time, hiring Mike McCarthy in the coming weeks. Although McCarthy enters Pittsburgh with a solid […]
full_text: Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin sent shockwaves throughout the football world after announcing that he would be stepping down from his position after the team’s loss in the AFC Wild Card playoffs to the Houston Texans. Pittsburgh wasted no time, hiring Mike McCarthy in the coming weeks. Although McCarthy enters Pittsburgh with a solid coaching resume, some believe he is already sitting on one of the hottest coaching seats in the league. In an article from Rotowire , they ranked all the NFL coaches by how hot their seats are entering the season. McCarthy was labeled as having the third hottest seat in the entire league, ahead of only Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets and Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts. Interestingly enough, Ravens new head coach Jesse Minter was just one spot ahead of McCarthy on the list. Rotowire justified their McCarthy hot seat label by saying that he and Minter are “inheriting proud, veteran-run programs.” While this is a true statement, it’s hard to imagine that the Steelers and Ravens would seriously consider moving on from their coaches after one season, barring anything catastrophic. The Steelers have always prided themselves on being a well-run organization that does not make rash decisions with their head coaches. McCarthy is only the fourth head coach for the Steelers since 1969, and it’s hard to imagine that changing anytime soon. McCarthy does come into his first season in Pittsburgh with some pressure to win some meaningful games. Many expect the Steelers to once again be contending for the AFC North crown this season. The organization has not won a postseason game since 2016, and fans will only want the organization to make more changes the longer that drought continues. title: Ian Rapoport: Seahawks looking to make Devon Witherspoon NFL’s highest paid cornerback
summary: After another elite season, Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon is reportedly closing in on a potential record-setting contract. The Seahawks may be closer than ever to securing the long-term future of one of the NFL’s premier defensive players. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, negotiations between Seattle and Witherspoon have advanced significantly. The report also […]
full_text: After another elite season, Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon is reportedly closing in on a potential record-setting contract. The Seahawks may be closer than ever to securing the long-term future of one of the NFL’s premier defensive players. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, negotiations between Seattle and Witherspoon have advanced significantly. The report also states that the Seahawks have offered Witherspoon a contract worth around $32 million per year, a figure that would place him as the new highest paid cornerback in NFL history. From @GMFB : The #Seahawks are working to make star CB Devon Witherspoon the highest-paid CB in the NFL, and his looming contract has wide-ranging ramifications. pic.twitter.com/i3bfzLLLt2 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 22, 2026 Rapoport also mentioned the ongoing negotiation between the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez, whom like Witherspoon is represented by Athletes First , meaning each contract could influence the other as the top of the cornerback market continues to evolve. Seahawks appear ready to pay franchise-cornerback money The reported offer reflects the reality of today’s market. Trent McDuffie currently leads all cornerbacks with a contract averaging $31 million per year , followed closely by Sauce Gardner at $30.1 million and Derek Stingley Jr. at $30 million annually. If Seattle’s reported offer exceeds the $30 million threshold, Witherspoon would immediately join that exclusive tier and could even surpass McDuffie depending on the final structure of the deal. From Seattle’s perspective, there is little incentive to wait. Another major extension elsewhere could raise the market yet again, making an eventual agreement even more expensive. Another elite season strengthened Witherspoon’s case Witherspoon has done everything necessary to justify a record-setting extension. Despite missing time during the regular season, he finished 2025 with 72 tackles, one interception, seven passes defended and a fumble recovery in just 12 games, earning his third consecutive Pro Bowl selection and Second-Team All-Pro honors . His impact extended well beyond the regular season. During Seattle’s Super Bowl-winning playoff run, Witherspoon remained one of Mike Macdonald’s most versatile defensive weapons, capping the year with a sack in Super Bowl 60 and a hit that led to Uchenna Nwosu’s game-ending pick-six. Statistics alone fail to capture his value. Whether aligned outside, in the slot, blitzing off the edge or matching up against tight ends and receivers alike, Witherspoon has become the centerpiece of Macdonald’s defensive scheme. Few defensive backs possess his combination of physicality, versatility and playmaking ability, making him one of the rare corners capable of altering an opponent’s game plan on a weekly basis. A familiar timeline for Seattle The Seahawks have never faced immediate pressure to finalize a deal. By exercising Witherspoon’s fifth-year option , the organization already controls his rights through the 2027 season. Still, Seattle has often preferred to complete major extensions before the regular season rather than allowing negotiations to linger into the fall. With training camp approaching, the next few weeks could provide the ideal window to finalize an agreement.

title: Seahawks place running back Zach Charbonnet on PUP list
summary: Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet may be “progressing well” following his ACL tear in the NFC Divisional Round against the San Francisco 49ers, but it was always a formality that he would begin training camp on the injured list. On Wednesday, the Seahawks placed Charbonnet on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. While […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks scores a touchdown against Malik Mustapha #6 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet may be “progressing well ” following his ACL tear in the NFC Divisional Round against the San Francisco 49ers, but it was always a formality that he would begin training camp on the injured list. On Wednesday, the Seahawks placed Charbonnet on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list . While anyone can be activated off PUP at any time during training camp and preseason, Charbonnet’s placement was a formality given the severity of his injury. While Nick Emmanwori’s PUP placement figures to be short-term and is not expected to have any impact on his regular season availability, Charbonnet is almost a certainty to remain on the PUP list past preseason. If that’s the case, then Charbonnet will have to miss at least the first four games, but new PUP rules allow players to have a 21-day window for practice starting in Week 3, as opposed to after the fourth regular season game. Without getting too far ahead of ourselves, it’s possible that Charbonnet could be available as early as Week 5 versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Seattle’s current PUP list consists of Charbonnet, fellow running back Kenny McIntosh (who tore his ACL in last year’s training camp), cornerback Tyrone Broden, and the aforementioned Emmanwori.

title: Seahawks fan favorite Jake Bobo reveals offseason interest from Patriots
summary: The Seattle Seahawks nearly lost fan favorite wide receiver, Jake Bobo, to the Jacksonville Jaguars this past offseason. That was after Bobo, whom at the time was a restricted free agent, signed a two-year, $5.5 million offer sheet. Although many in the media expected the Seahawks not to match, Seattle ended up doing so, leading […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks nearly lost fan favorite wide receiver, Jake Bobo, to the Jacksonville Jaguars this past offseason. That was after Bobo, whom at the time was a restricted free agent, signed a two-year, $5.5 million offer sheet . Although many in the media expected the Seahawks not to match, Seattle ended up doing so , leading to Bobo returning to the Pacific Northwest. However, a new report by the Boston Herald states that the Jaguars were not the only team interested in Bobo’s services . In an interview with Greg Dudek, Bobo revealed the New England Patriots were eying Bobo, as well. Had that happened, that would have been a homecoming for the Massachusetts native. “They were,” Bobo told the Herald when asked if the Patriots were one of the teams to show interest in him during free agency. “And I made the mistake of telling my mom that, who then got very, very excited. She doesn’t realize there are varying degrees of ‘sniffing around.’ I think once the Pats realized what they might have to pay the slow, skinny white kid I think they bowed out of it.” Bobo may not be going back to his home state, but he’s very much developed a connection with the Emerald City. “(Massachusetts) is where I grew up. That’s where my friends and family are still based. But at the end of the day, I’d go play anywhere,” Bobo said. “I obviously have now this link emotionally to the city of Seattle, which is weird to even think about just being connected emotionally to a city that’s not Boston. It’s a little odd. But to be back in Seattle ultimately, that’s where I wanted to be and I’m very, very grateful that we were able to work that out.” Of course, the Patriots went in a different direction, trading for AJ Brown , as well as signing wide receiver Romeo Doubs in free agency. Although Bobo has not impressed on the stat sheet, he has proven to be a critical member (and leader) for Seattle these past few seasons. His impact is seen not only on special teams, but also in his blocking as a wide receiver. Bobo has also come up in the clutch when called upon. Just look at his 17-yard touchdown reception in the NFC Championship game last season against the Los Angeles Rams . That was only his fourth catch in all of 2025. Bobo looks to have a similar role this next season as he projects to be the fourth wide receiver on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, and Cooper Kupp. Depending on Tory Horton’s health, Bobo may even slide down to the fifth wide receiver position. Nonetheless, Bobo looks to be a significant contributor to the Seahawks, even if the stat sheet does not indicate as such.
