I don’t think it’s a given, just yet.” 49ers insider believes Deebo Samuel wanted a return to San Francisco “I do think Deebo had an interest in returning to the 49ers and was maybe even a little miffed that the 49ers so quickly signed Mike Evans as a free agent.” 49ers roster preview: Why Carver Willis needs a redshirt year “There are plenty of traits to like about Willis. His hand placement and punch timing are above average, even if his hands can occasionally get a little wide — likely Willis overcompensating. He does a great job on combo blocks, can easily redirect, and moves more like a second-rounder than a fourth-rounder. Best of all, Willis competes through the whistle and will look to finish whoever he is blocking. He stays engaged, which is a valuable trait to have. Some things happen to Willis that he cannot control. I saw one of the Ohio State players forklift him off the ground. Too often, his lack of length was problematic. And while changing directions isn’t an issue, the shorter arms allow defenders to close space on him, knowing that Willis won’t affect them….. When I watched him, Willis looked like a player who needed more sand in his pants to hold up in pass protection. Now, the 49ers could do different things upfront to hide him or minimize the number of 1-on-1s Willis gets. He was at his best when he was uncovered. When he could help somebody else out, or had help on combination blocks. That’s a center. Foerster is probably correct in viewing Willis as a starter, but that’s likely in 2027 to replace Brendel and become the 49ers’ center of the future. As a rookie, Willis should take advantage of a professional strength & conditioning program, as well as all of the nutrition that comes with being a pro. He’ll learn the ins and outs of playing a new position while going against NFL-quality linemen on the scout team.” One thought on Brock Purdy, Ricky Pearsall and every player on the 49ers offense (paywall) “Connor Colby: We’ll pencil in Colby as the team’s top left guard prospect, but we have to do it very lightly since several others are competing for that spot. It’s probably Jones, who started 17 games in a similar Dolphins offense in 2024 and has logged more than 2,000 offensive snaps in his career. Jones is coming off a neck injury that cost him the entire 2025 season.” We gave 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch offseason advice. How well did they follow it? That was a response to dissatisfaction players had expressed in the most recent NFLPA survey in which they grade their team in 11 categories.”

title: 49ers coordinator tabbed as 2026 breakout candidate
summary: The 49ers have an excellent track record when it comes to their coordinators and assistants going on to find more prominent roles elsewhere. Since he took over as head coach in 2017, six of Kyle Shanahan’s assistants have gone on to become head coaches. With Robert Saleh getting his second shot as a head coach […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 16: San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak watches the team warm up before a game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers have an excellent track record when it comes to their coordinators and assistants going on to find more prominent roles elsewhere. Since he took over as head coach in 2017, six of Kyle Shanahan’s assistants have gone on to become head coaches. With Robert Saleh getting his second shot as a head coach with the Tennessee Titans, Jeff Hafley landing with the Miami Dolphins, Klint Kubiak taking charge of the Las Vegas Raiders, and Mike LaFleur being appointed as head coach of the Arizona Cardinals, the 2026 season will see five former 49er assistants lead teams. As such, it is fair to have the expectation that, when next year’s hiring cycle rolls around, there will be interest in the 49ers’ current staff. That is, of course, at least partially dependent on San Francisco’s fortunes in the coming campaign. But the smart money says San Francisco will be among the best teams in the NFC again in 2026, with an offense that is likely to be one of the most efficient in football. Should that happen, then there may be head coaching chatter around Klint Kubiak’s brother Klay, who has the title of offensive coordinator with the 49ers even though Shanahan calls the plays. And The Athletic’s Jordan Rodrigue believes there is a possibility Kubiak could follow a similar path to his brother, naming him as an assistant coach breakout candidate. Rodrigue writes: “Don’t look now, there’s another Kubiak! The first-year offensive coordinator worked his way up after initially joining the 49ers as a defensive assistant in 2021. He also was an assistant quarterbacks coach and passing game specialist. External observers may see a natural path for Kubiak similar to that of his brother, now-Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who worked under 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan as a passing game coordinator in 2023.” While Shanahan is the man who has control of the offense on gameday, he has consistently said that game planning is a collective process. As such, if the 49ers’ offense does fire as it has consistently done so under Shanahan, there is likely to be intrigue around the younger Kubiak. On the defensive side of the ball, K.J. Wright could be considered a compelling breakout candidate. While defensive coordinator Raheem Morris might be out of chances to be a head coach, Wright may receive attention as a potential coordinator himself if he can get the best out of a 49er linebacking core that has plenty of questions around it going into the season. But in terms of moving into the big chair, or at least a coordinator role where he calls plays, it is Kubiak who has the most obvious avenue. Shanahan has had to deal with a lot of coaching staff turnover in his tenure, and more could be on the horizon should his offense thrive again this season.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Adam Schefter provides 3 ‘unresolved issues’ for the 49ers ahead of training camp
summary: ESPN’s Adam Schefter had training camp notes for every NFL team on his podcast. In the NFC West portion, Schefter spoke about the hurdles Aaron Donald and the Los Angeles Rams still have to clear — Donald is still owed $40 million from his current deal. According to Schefter, the 49ers still have “a lot […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers gets tackled by Eric Rowe #21 the Miami Dolphins during the second half of their NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on October 11, 2020 in Santa Clara, California. Miami won the game 43-17. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s Adam Schefter had training camp notes for every NFL team on his podcast. In the NFC West portion, Schefter spoke about the hurdles Aaron Donald and the Los Angeles Rams still have to clear — Donald is still owed $40 million from his current deal. According to Schefter, the 49ers still have “a lot of unresolved issues.” Here’s what he had to say: We still need to see if Brandon Aiyuk is going to apply for reinstatement. George Kittle is coming back from injury. He feels like he’s going to be ready for that season opener in Australia against the Rams, but the 49ers may be very careful. And let’s see if he can make it back. I don’t think it’s a given just yet. They have a new defensive coordinator in Raheem Morris, who will be the fifth different defensive coordinator in the last 5 years. Now, they love Raheem Morris. They’ve wanted him to do that job for a while. I think Kyle Shanahan is very happy to have him back there. But it’s another new defensive coordinator, as they try to work in some of their players coming back from knee injuries — like their former No.1 draft pick, Mykel Williams. A lot of players trying to bounce back. They do have Mike Evans, and that’ll be a big boost for the offense. For as active as Aiyuk has been on social media, he still must apply for reinstatement . A week ago, Schefter said he believed Aiyuk had scared teams off . He’s not getting traded anymore after his antics. Aiyuk won’t get the opportunity to play for another team until he files the paperwork to be reinstated. He’ll remain on the left squad list until that happens. Kittle should take all the time he needs. As impressive as it is to see him deadlift 660 pounds , those deadlift/squatting movements don’t have as much impact on the Achilles as you’d think, as there is no directional change in an explosive manner happening. Kittle said during OTAs he had a target date that would be 21 weeks out on June 23. Week 1 feels like a long shot. Speculating on Kittle’s return will drive you up a wall. As for having stability at defensive coordinator, it’s the first time there’s a former defensive back in the fold. I’ll be interested to see how Morris impacts the play of the secondary, and if we see more changes throughout the season if the results don’t follow.

title: Should the 49ers move on from John Lynch if they don’t make the playoffs?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Niners fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The San Francisco 49ers are projected to be a playoff team in 2026 once again. But…what […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 03: John Lynch General Manager of the San Francisco 49ers looks on during pregame against the Seattle Seahawks at Levi's Stadium on October 03, 2021 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Niners fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The San Francisco 49ers are projected to be a playoff team in 2026 once again. But…what if they don’t make it? What if, for whatever reason, things go awry this upcoming season? The 49ers have done an incredible job of moving off former draft picks or free agent acquistions that haven’t worked out. There is undoubtedly some luck involved — like stumbling upon an aggressive playmaker at quarterback in the seventh round. But having multiple core pieces and supplementing those players with key depth has kept the Niners afloat this decade. As long as Kyle Shanahan is at the helm, it feels like this team will always be competitive. We’ve seen injuries have their say and be too much for the Niners to overcome. Still, like in 2025, the team still found a way to make the postseason. Despite being one of the most successful franchises since the current regime took over, San Francisco has yet to hoist a Lombardi trophy. In a bottom line business, heads tend to roll when you haven’t won the big one. This regime took over in the 2017 offseason. We’re coming up on a decade. SB Nation’s Jarrett Bailey gave an explanation as to why the team would miss the playoffs: San Francisco’s core is just too old, and you can never bank on them being fully healthy. They overachieved in 2025 despite those injuries, but a lot of that had to do with Robert Saleh calling the defense. Without Saleh, any defensive shortcomings will severely hinder the 49ers. If that were the case, should the 49ers move on from John Lynch?

title: Which 49ers player is most likely to be a first-time Pro Bowler this season?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have multiple Pro Bowlers on their roster. Trent Williams, Christian McCaffrey, Fred Warner, Nick Bosa, and George Kittle are basically in the running each season they are healthy to make the Pro Bowl. In recent seasons, the Pro Bowl has lost some of its luster with selections of alternates for players […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Ricky Pearsall #1 of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have multiple Pro Bowlers on their roster. Trent Williams, Christian McCaffrey, Fred Warner, Nick Bosa, and George Kittle are basically in the running each season they are healthy to make the Pro Bowl. In recent seasons, the Pro Bowl has lost some of its luster with selections of alternates for players who either decline the invitation or are playing in the Super Bowl. Still, being a Pro Bowler is a great honor and can likely trigger extra money for players through incentives in their contract. Which 49ers player is most likely to be a first-time Pro Bowler? Deommodore Lenoir This selection seems logical given Lenoir’s importance as the 49ers’ best cover corner and the boost of Raheem Morris as the defensive coordinator. 2025 was a down season for the 49ers’ defense and Lenoir. Allowing five touchdowns in coverage after allowing zero in 2024 was a step back for Lenoir. The sixth-year cornerback is set for a bounce-back season, and if the interceptions start to increase, it will be hard to deny “The Hyena.” Dominick Puni 2025 was an interesting season for the right guard. His season was off to a weird start after suffering a freak injury during a preseason game against the Raiders. Puni was clearly playing through the injury, but his 2024 form flashed later in the season once he got clear of the injury. With a clean bill of health, if Puni can put together a full, healthy season, the former Kansas lineman will have a strong case to be a Pro Bowler. Ricky Pearsall There is no doubt about Pearsall’s talent. The concerns are injury-related, but now with Mike Evans in the fold as the primary “X” receiver, Pearsall has a chance to expand on his early-season success from 2024 and take the next step. With the attention on Evans, McCaffrey, and Kittle, Pearsall will have his opportunities against an opposition’s less talented corners and is fully capable of getting open and making plays. Honorable Mention: Colton McKivitz The reason I chose Puni over McKivitz is the competition across the NFC at right tackle. McKivitz has been very solid and, depending on which advanced stats you cite, sits fairly high compared to other more established right tackles. The amount of great players at the premium position is the biggest concern for McKivitz, but his play has been very solid, and the 49ers aren’t paying a premium for his production.

title: 49ers News: Wish we could just have throwback uniforms all season long
summary: How a gruesome injury helped 49ers leader Fred Warner find his purpose (paywall)“Warner is convinced his durability is a gift from the heavens. And a DEXA body composition scan taken last year helped him understand, revealing that his bones were six times denser than the average human. “Some guys have a freakish ability to run […]
full_text: MIAMI, : San Francisco 49ers quarterback Steve Young (R) celebrates with teammate Jerry Rice (L) after Young threw his fifth touchdown pass 29 January 1995 during Super Bowl XXIX. The 49ers defeated the San Diego Chargers 49-26 and becomes the first NFL team to win five Super Bowls. (COLOR KEY: Red jerseys.) AFP PHOTO (Photo credit should read JEFF HAYNES/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images How a gruesome injury helped 49ers leader Fred Warner find his purpose (paywall) “ Warner is convinced his durability is a gift from the heavens. And a DEXA body composition scan taken last year helped him understand, revealing that his bones were six times denser than the average human. “Some guys have a freakish ability to run fast,” he says. “My freakish ability, I guess, is having thick bones to help me stay healthier.” ….This offseason, Warner has been working on taking advantage of one-on-one pass-rush opportunities against running backs, which he hasn’t been asked to do frequently in the past. Holland hopes that Warner will have many more chances to rush against running backs this season. Warner believes he will reach a higher level in 2026 by increasing his competitive intensity, which was already near Goku level. He speaks of becoming more of a “maniac on the field” and breaking through age’s barriers. Thirty, the way he sees it, is an opportunity. So is coming back from injury.” Rams had eyes on De’Zhaun Stribling before 49ers drafted him “What’s interesting about this selection is there was some people that wondered if it was too early for De’Zhaun Stribling to go,” Schefter said on NFL Live . “And there were a couple of teams that I spoke to in the draft process, leading up to the draft, that felt that De’Zhaun Stribling was the best wide receiver in the draft. “Another team, supposedly the Los Angeles Rams, had eyes on him. So, the 49ers didn’t just come up with this pick out of nowhere. They knew that there were other teams that had a very high grade on Stribling when the 49ers declined to trade out the top draft slot in the second round and take him there.” Steve Young reveals how 49ers can help Brock Purdy reach the next level “His game is the first couple seconds,” Young said. “Process, get some protection, have some weapons—as good as it gets. To help him thrive—and every quarterback needs lots of help to thrive—we need some people that can get open quickly,” Young said. “Brandon Aiyuk was somebody who got open on the perimeter quickly—and that’s what his game is. Get open, show up, bam, get the ball to him and go.” “So, Mike, Ricky, they need to be people that can get off the line of scrimmage quickly, get open, get the ball out,” Young added. “That’s when he’s going to be deadly.” 49ers unveil 2026 uniform schedule, including throwbacks and Rivalries look “The 49ers will wear their red throwbacks twice during the regular season—on the road against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10 and at home against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 17. The white throwbacks will make one appearance in Week 15 against the Los Angeles Chargers, while the black Nike Rivalries uniform will debut in Week 14 against the Los Angeles Rams.” Explaining the biggest difference between the 2025 and 2026 49ers “While that’s partially true — Purdy was under pressure on 39% of his dropbacks — he had plenty of time to throw. On average, Purdy had a whopping 4.24 seconds to throw on 33 dropbacks. He only completed 55.6% of his passes because there was nobody to throw the ball to. I recently rewatched the game. And as someone who appreciates wide receiver play, it was painful. Some of the advanced stats match the eye test. Next Gen Stats has a “catch rate over expected” stat. Across the board, the wideouts were in the negatives. Ricky Pearsall’s numbers seem like they were entered in incorrectly; they were so low. When you’re relying on Jauan Jennings and Kendrick Bourne against an elite secondary, it’s a miracle that the Niners were in this situation to begin with. The wide receiver play for the 49ers will be night and day, and everybody will reap the benefits. Safeties crept closer to the line of scrimmage without fear of one of the Niners’ wideouts running past them. That same issue meant opposing defenses could shrink the field and turn their attention to George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey underneath. The lack of physicality showed up in the running game all too often. Because of that, McCaffrey had to be a magician behind the line of scrimmage. The margin for error in the running game was next to nothing because the receivers didn’t have the necessary passion as blockers. Mike Evans changes everything. He gives the 49ers a weapon on every down, and a go-to target on third down. It also means Pearsall is no longer the focal point and gets the other team’s CB2. When that was the case last season, Pearsall made mincemeat of lesser corners.”

summary: The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. full_text: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons speaks after mandatory minicamp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center in Nashville, Tenn., Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | ANDREW NELLES / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. We’ll be previewing several position groups until then. The Titans have 16 defensive lineman on the offseason roster. General manager Mike Borgonzi made big-time acquisitions at this position. In camp (16) : Jeffery Simmons, John Franklin-Myers, Jermaine Johnson II, Jacob Martin, Keldric Faulk, Femi Oladejo, Jordan Elliott, Solomon Thomas, Jaylen Harrell, Earnest Brown IV, Malik Herring, Jalyn Holmes, Timmy Horne, Cam Horsley, Truman Jones, Jackie Marshall. Biggest storyline: Head coach Robert Saleh was allowed to revamp this position in his vision. Borgonzi acquired five veterans via free agency and trades that previously played for Saleh with the 49ers or Jets. Franklin-Myers, Johnson, Thomas, Elliott and Martin were all brought here due to their familiarity with the scheme. The head coach also approved of trading up for Faulk at No. 31 overall. Most to prove: Femi Oladejo. Titans fans immediately questioned Borgonzi’s decision to draft him with a second-round pick. Oladejo was a raw prospect coming out of UCLA who made a position switch from linebacker to EDGE in his final college season. He didn’t register a sack with the Titans as a rookie and suffered a season-ending injury in Week 6. He’s officially on bust watch. Breakout star: We’re not necessarily sure the Titans have a breakout star on the defensive line. Simmons and Franklin-Myers are expected to be the dominant forces. Perhaps Oladejo breaks out. Perhaps Johnson regains form under Saleh after a 2024 Achilles injury limited his 2025 effectiveness. Martin is the darkhorse here, and Faulk is an exciting rookie. Training camp competition: Saleh has discussed rotating defensive lineman early and often. You’ll especially see Martin, Oladejo, Johnson, and Faulk rotating at edge. Perhaps Jaylen Harrell gets into that mix too after a strong conclusion to his 2025 campaign. Elliott and Thomas will play supporting roles behind Simmons and Franklin-Myers. Rookie Jackie Marshall is trying to make the 53-man roster. He’ll face competition from Cam Horsley and Jalyn Holmes. Everyone else is likely just a camp body.

title: Tyler’s Take – My two breakout players (offense and defense) for the 2026 Commanders
summary: The NFL draft is the lifeblood of your football team. Selecting and developing young talent is the number one job of an NFL general manager.  Adam Peters has been criticized a bit over his first two years in Washington for some of his higher draft picks. Some of those guys were expected to have a […]
full_text: The NFL draft is the lifeblood of your football team. Selecting and developing young talent is the number one job of an NFL general manager. Adam Peters has been criticized a bit over his first two years in Washington for some of his higher draft picks. Some of those guys were expected to have a MUCH bigger impact on the team than they have had to date. Conversely, some players who were picked a bit later shined early on. While we can make our voices heard in displeasure about some of Peter’s top 100 picks not preforming, we must be just as complementary of some guys who may have been overlooked in the draft, but came to Washington and did well. And, yes, I’m taking about BILL! Fans want to see players perform well. Some players take more time than others to develop, but the key to success is whether said player eventually gets to that “expected” level. With that said, below are my offensive and defensive breakout candidates for the upcoming season. Offense: TE Ben Sinnott Every time tight end Ben Sinnott touches the ball, good things seem to happen. The issue was that former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury didn’t often get him the ball, instead relying on the savvy veteran Zach Ertz to help move the chains from the tight end position. Ben Sinnott with a huge 36yd gain! pic.twitter.com/ZlfXJAzuqz — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) December 14, 2025 This new David Blough offense seems tailor-made for a player like Sinnott. He can be moved around the formation, deployed as a blocker and pass catcher, and use his unique open-field abilities after the catch to move the offense up and down the field. He’s best with the ball in his hands with some space in front of him. This new system should scheme him to do just that. I view tight end Chig Okonkwo as a JUMBO wide receiver, so John Bates could be the true (more traditional) tight end of this offense. That leaves plenty of opportunity for Sinnott. Breakout Barometer: 40 receptions, 450 yards, 5 touchdowns Defense: DL Johnny Newtown Make no mistake about it — Johnny Newton was an absolute FORCE in Illinois’ one-gapping, attacking front in college. Because of that disruptive ability, he was selected early, in round two of the 2024 NFL draft. He was dealing with a lingering foot issue from college as a rookie and never quite got going. Newton was healthy entering Year 2, but a rash of injuries along the defensive front and a scheme that didn’t fit his talents thwarted his sophomore campaign. There were some quality flashes, but the consistency was missing. Year 3 could potentially paint an entirely different picture. The new up-field, attacking scheme that defensive coordinator Daronte Jones is expected to use should be much better for his skillset. Also, not having to two-gap in an EAGLE front should be to his liking. Quickness off the snap, plus an ability to get into the backfield and cause havoc are Newton’s best attributes. Putting him in a 3-technique and letting him use that quick-twitch ability against slower, more unathletic guards will be to his benefit. Breakout Barometer: 45 tackles, 9 TFL, 7 sacks, 1 FF Breakout Bonus: Mike Sainristil If you know me, you’ll know there can never be enough rainbows and unicorns. With that, I give you my bonus breakout player. As many of you already know, I’m a BIG Mike Sainristil fan. I thought he showed really well as a rookie, despite bouncing between the slot and boundary. Mike Sainristil with the nice play downfield here! pic.twitter.com/eCVSjsI3p0 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 10, 2024 Last year was a big step back, but how much of that was the system and lack of continuity around him? Sainristil has shown a propensity for taking the ball away during his first two seasons. In this new defensive scheme, where he’ll be able to play a lot more with his eyes on the quarterback, I expect him to continue to be the guy creating turnovers. Mike Sainristil with the MASSIVE INT right before the half!!! Huge play! pic.twitter.com/xGRKp94ht8 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) January 19, 2025 We’ve all seen that, despite his lack of size, Mikey is not afraid to come up and hit guys. I believe we see a nice blend of coverage and run support from the third-year corner, and we can watch Uncle Nick (Saban)’s praise about him being one of the best pound-for-pound players in the 2024 draft class come to reality in the league. I know one thing – Mike Sainristil is NOT afraid to tackle… pic.twitter.com/Kl6m3mvnnY — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 27, 2024 Breakout Barometer: 65 tackles, 1 FF, 1 sack, 5 INT, 15 PD *Sainristil had back-to-back seasons of 93 and 85 combined tackles respectively. However, you don’t want to see your cornerback making that many tackles, as that usually means your front seven is NOT doing their job. So, while I have Sainristil with less combined tackles, I just think that means Washington’s defensive line and linebackers are doing their jobs better. Let us know what you think of Mark’s breakout candidates, or add other nominees, in the comments below:

(Photo by Mark Goldman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 O’Clock Club The 5 o’clock club is published from time to time during the season, and aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. With the amount of roster change that NFL teams undergo annually along with the unusually large number of head coach and coordinator changes in 2026, it seems useful to spend some time to review each of Washington’s regular season opponents. JAGUARS The Week 17 road game in Jacksonville features the matchup of two relatively young NFL QBs, Trevor Lawrence and Jayden Daniels, each trying to enhance the trajectory of his career. Lawrence enters the late-season contest following a season in which he became an MVP finalist under coordinator Liam Coen. For the Commanders, Daniels will be hoping to be finishing a healthy season reminiscent of his rookie year, and leading a re-tooled and re-energized Washington offense under David Blough. This game could serve as a late-season benchmark for both quarterbacks as their teams will hopefully be fighting for playoff positioning. Week 17 Preview: Washington Commanders at Jacksonville Jaguars Date: Date & Time TBD Location: EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida The official NFL Commanders 2026 Season Preview ends with this projection of what the Commanders season could look like if Jayden Daniels stays healthy and returns to his 2024 ROTY form: While this projected start to the season (0-3; 2-4; 3-5) would lead to a lot of people having to be talked down from a lot of ledges in the months of September and October, given the team’s two new coordinators and the distribution of expected tougher/easier opponents, this 12-win projection doesn’t look very dissimilar to my own recent 10-win projection; in fact, I had the same W/L projections for all the games except for the Texans and this one against the Jaguars. My point here, if I have one, is that the Week 17 game in Jacksonville, if the season is unfolding along the lines of an optimistic preseason projection, could take place amidst a lot of winning and optimism for a Commanders team that could be living by the mantra that “it ain’t how you start; it’s how you finish” in this first weekend of NFL football in the 2027 calendar year ( For what it’s worth, I looked at the Jaguars’ season preview video from the NFL, and their best case outcome has them winning 13 games and winning this Week 17 game as well ). The Jaguars won 13 games last year en route to the AFC South championship, and I imagine that Jacksonville fans will be expecting a similarly strong 2026 season. The Jags season over/under win total is 9.5, so oddsmakers seem to be expecting a good season from Liam Coen’s team. One familiar face that the Commanders will know when they fly south for this winter battle is that of RB Chris Rodriguez, former 2023 6th-round draft pick of the Commanders. He signed with the Jaguars as a restricted free agent from the Commanders this offseason, and Rodriguez should be a focal point of Jacksonville’s short-yardage committee alongside second-year back Bhayshul Tuten. Jayden Daniels will see at least one friendly face from his college days. His former teammate at LSU, Brian Thomas Jr, is a star wide receiver for the Jaguars — or, at least, like JD5, Thomas looked like a star when he had 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 TDs as a rookie in 2024 before falling back to earth quite a bit in ‘25 (707 yards, 2 TDs). He was Jayden Daniels’ primary deep threat during their record-breaking 2023 college football season at LSU, where Thomas led the nation in touchdown receptions and helped propel Daniels to his Heisman Trophy win. Both players entered the NFL together as first-round picks in the 2024 NFL Draft, and there has been a lot of fan & media buzz in recent months about the concept of the Commanders front office trading for Thomas to set up an NFL reunion between quarterback and receiver. Of course, Daniels has another former college teammate on the roster with him at the moment — Rachaad White, signed by Washington in free agency back in March, and Daniels formed a productive offensive backfield together at Arizona State during the 2020 and 2021 college seasons before Daniels transferred to LSU. Under head coach Liam Coen in 2025, Jacksonville transformed into an offensive powerhouse, highlighted by an explosive post-bye-week stretch. If they mirror last year’s late-season surge in 2026, this game will likely be critical for securing the AFC South or a top seed. Washington, for its part, enters the ‘26 season determined to erase memories of a tough 2025 season and find its footing under new coordinators on offense & defense. Commanders fans are hoping that fresh leadership and a rejuvenated and healthy roster will see the team re-acquire the playoff form it demonstrated in 2024. This Week 17 battle represents either a statement game to clinch an NFC playoff seed or — in the pessimistic timeline — a spoiler opportunity against an AFC heavyweight. The All-Time Series Numbers The historical discrepancy between these two franchises is shockingly one-sided. Washington completely dominates the all-time series 7-1 , with Jacksonville’s solitary win against the franchise occurring all the way back in 2002. The only NFL team that has played Washington fewer times than the Jaguars is the Texans — the Commanders’ Week 14 opponent. No team has been more thoroughly dominated by Washington than the Jaguars based on the all-time series W-L record. Still, when the games are looked at individually, things have been much more even between the two teams than the series record would indicate; in the 5 straight Washington victories since 2006, 4 of them have been decided by a margin of 6 points or less, and two of them went into overtime. In other words, despite the dominance in series wins, the past two decades has been witness to a hard-fought bunch of games between these two teams. Undoubtedly, Jacksonville will be looking to partially balance the scales with a key win in this Week 17 game. The Commanders, on the other hand, will be keen to add to the most lopsided head-to-head series advantage they enjoy against any team in the league. Jaguars Coaching Staff While there were some limited staff changes, the Jaguars coaching staff returns for the 2026 season substantially the same as it was in 2025, with the same head coach and coordinators. Both OC Grant Udinski and DC Anthony Campanile had multiple interviews for head coaching positions, but both returned to Jacksonville on new contracts. Hogs Haven will certainly make some this summer, possibly closer to the regular season and after we’ve gleaned some much-needed info from camp. SB Nation’s own Jarrett Bailey, who runs BehindTheSteelCurtain.com , didn’t wait for his, trotting out 61 bold predictions for the NFL season. He clearly has a high opinion of the Washington Commanders. Not, like, win-NFC-East-high, but there’s a strong sense that better’s on the way. That comes from three of his 61(!!) bold predictions about the upcoming 2026 season. They involved quarterback Jayden Daniels , linebacker Sonny Styles and the team overall . All of them are positive, and well within the realm of possibility. Daniels wins comeback player of the year. Styles wins defensive rookie of the year. The Commanders qualify for the playoffs with the NFC’s seventh seed. You can read all 61 of Bailey’s predictions right here — you won’t like who wins the Super Bowl — but we’ll highlight the Commanders related goodness below. “32. Jayden Daniels wins Comeback Player of the Year “Daniels reminds everyone that he is one of the best young quarterbacks in football, throwing 26 touchdowns and adding seven on the ground to just nine interceptions as he leads Washington back to the playoffs.” “34. Sonny Styles wins Defensive Rookie of the Year “Styles is the key to Dan Quinn’s defense getting back on track. The Ohio State product will be a top five tackler in the NFL, as well as pick off four passes to help Washington’s defense improve from finishing 28th in success rate.” “ 50. Commanders earn No. 7 seed in NFC “Off the strength of a rejuvenated and healthy Jayden Daniels, as well as a defense that is much improved with several new starters, Washington bounces back after a five-win 2025 campaign and gets back into the postseason in their first year back in their perfect classic uniforms.” And a Week 1 bonus from Bailey: “ 6. Jayden Daniels lights up the Eagles in Week 1 “The Commanders begin their season on the road in Philadelphia in the late-afternoon window on Fox, and man doesn’t that just feel right? Few things make me feel as nostalgic as the NFC East getting America’s Game of the Week. Commanders links Articles Commanders.com ‘GMFB’ has 1 burning question about Washington’s offense ahead of camp For the “Good Morning Football” crew, their focus is on one of the Commanders’ main offseason goals: getting the ground attack more involved in the game plan. “People have to remember that the Washington Commanders ran the ball pretty well last year,” said analyst and former offensive guard Willie Colon. “Their record was bad, but they got after it up front.” Although the Commanders’ offense regressed in 2025, largely because of the injuries to Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin and other key contributors, their run game remained one of the best in the league. They were fourth in yards per game, fifth in yards per attempt and eighth in rushing first downs per game. Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who paced the team with 805 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries, led the league in success rate — a stat used by Pro Football Reference based on the ability to gain required yardage on downs — at 53.7%. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A to Z Sports Another 10 burning questions ahead of Commanders training camp Can Rasul Douglas provide answers at cornerback? Douglas could end up being one of the bigger steals of the offseason. Trey Amos is expected to be ready for training camp but is still coming back from last year’s bad injury. Mike Sainristill and Amik Robinson are both coming off rough 2025 seasons, and there’s no starting-quality depth behind them. Douglas’ addition creates instant competition on the outside, and he can also play inside if needed. He’s got to show that his strong 2025 season can carry over into 2026 and the Commanders secondary will be in much better shape if he does just that. How long will it take the front seven to establish itself? The Commanders totally retooled the front seven, and on paper it looks pretty sick. Odafe Oweh and K’Lavonn Chaisson appear to be entering the prime of their careers and should represent an upgrade at the EDGE position. Up front, Daron Payne should be motivated in a contract year, Tim Settle has always been underrated, and Javon Kinlaw was good in Year 1 with the Commanders. At linebacker, Washington arguably has the NFL’s strongest rotation in Sonny Styles, Leo Chenal, Frankie Luvu, and Jordan Magee. This group has to be the driving force on defense and can’t slow-walk its development whatsoever. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE QUICK READER POLL Heavy.com Rachaad White has clear ambition with Commanders Luke Easterling of Athlon Sports …made a compelling case for why the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers back can eventually replace Croskey-Merritt. The most interesting note from Easterling’s take on White is the statement the 27-year-old left Tampa because he’s “seeking a bigger role.” It means White is unlikely to embrace the running back by committee approach the Commanders appear to have built this offseason. That makes sense after White found himself usurped with the Bucs by second-year pro Bucky Irving. White still tallied 132 rushing attempts and 40 receptions, but if he’s wanting more, that means the 6-foot, 214-pounder has his sights set on the lead-back role in Washington. Winning the job won’t be easy when there’s so much competition , but White has already made a strong start . A positive first impression only adds to White’s case to be the Commanders’ go-to back. A case boosted not just by his receiving skills, bur also by the natural vision and patience to thrive in the zone-based running schemes new offensive coordinator David Blough is likely to employ. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Five Washington Commanders long shots with more roster hope than fans realize this summer Quentin Moore – Commanders TE The Commanders are expected to utilize the tight end position more under new offensive coordinator David Blough. They also have the options needed to ensure his schematic switch goes smoothly. With Zach Ertz no longer around, the Commanders signed Chig Okonkwo to a three-year, $27 million deal in free agency. He’s the new alpha and the No. 1 threat in the passing attack , boasting the speed and dynamism that could become a magnificent asset for quarterback Jayden Daniels. John Bates is the blocking specialist who can also catch passes when needed. Ben Sinnott could be in line for more work, and Colson Yankoff’s special-teams prowess also gives him a fighting chance of sticking around for a third season. That might be enough. But if the Commanders are intent on giving everyone a legitimate chance to stake a claim, it may be worth keeping a close eye on Quentin Moore’s progress this summer. Moore was a bit-part player over his five years with the Washington Huskies. It was no surprise that he went undrafted, but interest in the player was high enough for the Commanders to give him $250,000 on his rookie deal to ensure they got an extended look at him over the summer. He’s got all the size and athleticism one looks for in a productive tight end in all phases. There is a lot of hard work ahead, and the practice squad remains his most likely destination. title: Explaining why every Commanders training-camp roster battle matters
summary: In a little over a week, Hogs Haven will be buzzing with news about new Commanders additions in training camp. Naturally, the spotlight will focus the most on returning stars like QB Jayden Daniels, high-profile free agent additions such as OLB Odafe Oweh and TE Chig Okonkwo, and early-round NFL draft picks LB Sonny Styles […]
full_text: In a little over a week, Hogs Haven will be buzzing with news about new Commanders additions in training camp. Naturally, the spotlight will focus the most on returning stars like QB Jayden Daniels, high-profile free agent additions such as OLB Odafe Oweh and TE Chig Okonkwo, and early-round NFL draft picks LB Sonny Styles and WR Antonio Williams. For some fans, however, the more interesting camp stories are annual battles waged by players on the fringe, fighting their way onto the final 53-man roster and keeping their NFL dreams alive. Over the years, Washington football fans have witnessed some great camp and preseason stories of underdogs beating the odds, like Alfred Morris, Kyshoen Jarrett, Chase Roullier, Jeremy Reaves and Kam Curl. Each year at Hogs Haven we celebrate the efforts of early-career roster-fringe players to earn a place on the team – or at least convince us that they will – with the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award . This year a new crop or fringe hopefuls will try to make their case, along with a host of returning players. I highlighted the Mason/Brennan-eligible candidates among them in a three-part preview ( Front Runners , Chasing Pack , Dark Horses and Long Shots ) ahead of OTAs. This year’s camp promises some interesting position battles at kicker , center , wide receiver and defensive back, with opportunities for fringe-players to earn playing time. Names to watch at those positions include Drew Stevens, Matt Gulbin, Jaden Bradley, Chris Hilton, Malik Spencer, and Fred Davis II. But the real excitement of training camp and pre-season is that you never really know who might emerge from obscurity to claim a position on the final 53. While most Day 3 draft picks, UDFAs and other players on reserve/futures contracts will never make it as major contributors on an NFL team, it is a lazy take to dismiss their chances. The numbers are stacked against them. But every preseason we see players emerge from the bottom of depth charts to claim roster spots, and sometimes become starters and even stars in the NFL. To illustrate why every preseason battle deserves attention, this article diverts the spotlight for a moment from the early roster locks to focus attention on players who began their NFL journeys on the fringes, fighting for positions in camp, and went on to earn significant playing time on Super Bowl rosters. As the Commanders seek to return to the big stage, GM Adam Peters will need to fill out the roster with 53 competitors. As the data in my most recent article revealed, he is unlikely to do that entirely with early-round draft picks, marquee free agents, and trade acquisitions. He will most likely need some help from players who faced an uphill battle to earn their place on the team. To set the stage for battles for the last few places on the roster in camp, let’s take a moment to reflect on the contributions and journeys of former roster-fringe hopefuls to Super Bowl rosters. Former Roster-Fringe Players on Super Bowl Teams – 2020 to 2025 This piece took its inspiration from the analysis I did for my recent article on how Super Bowl teams acquired their players . One thing which really stood out as I was tracing the players’ journeys was the number of players acquired by Super Bowl teams as late-round NFL draft picks, UDFAs, waiver and practice squad claim, and as fringe free agent signings. The proportion of former roster-fringe players was particularly enriched among the special teams players. However, most Super Bowl teams had more of these players than I had expected on offense and defense. And the two teams which had made repeat Super Bowl appearances in the sample seemed to be particularly stacked. To confirm that impression, I broke down the Super Bowl roster data into “Mainstream” and “Roster-Fringe” acquisitions, on offense and defense. As in the previous article, I only included “major contributors” who played 20% or more of offensive or defensive snaps in the Super Bowl. “Mainstream” acquisitions included players drafted in rounds 1-6, veteran free agents and players acquired by trade. “Roster-Fringe” acquisitions included seventh-round draft picks, undrafted free agents acquired in their draft year, players claimed off waivers or another team’s practice squad, and “fringe free agent” signings. The last category was included to capture players signed as free agents in the first three years of their careers with negligible game experience on other teams. Fringe FA is a major acquisition route for special teams players. But only two players made it onto offensive or defensive Super Bowl rosters in this way: DL Cory Durden (Patriots, 2025) and OL Andrew Wylie, (Chiefs, 2020 and 2022). The following table shows the complete breakdown: In the six Super Bowls from 2020 through 2025, 48/353 (13.6%) of the major contributors on offense and defense initially made their way onto their team from the roster fringes. The average Super Bowl roster contained four former roster-fringe players on offense or defense. The maximum number was eight (2020 Chiefs) and the minimum was two (2025 Patriots, 2020 Buccaneers). It is worth noting that the decision to only count seventh-round draft picks as roster-fringe was arbitrary. Had I included sixth-round picks, the percentage of former roster-fringe players would have been even larger. The takeaway message from this analysis is, before anyone dismisses the chances of a seventh-round pick or UDFA making the final 53-man roster, remember, every one of the past 12 Super Bowl teams had at least two players who started out the same way making significant contributions on offense or defense. Two of the roster-fringe players who made good during this period went on to become stars in the league. Several became starters or major contributors on offense or defense. Even more became important rotational players, backups or special teams contributors. To weather a 17-game season and emerge as a championship contender, an NFL team needs all of the above. Now, let’s take a look at the journeys of a selection of these players from camp hopeful to the Super Bowl. We’ll end with five players who got their start with the Redskins or ended up on the Commanders’ roster. Impact Players QB Brock Purdy, 49ers – The last player drafted in 2022 began his rookie season as an afterthought, buried on the depth chart behind first-round trade target Trey Lance and veteran Jimmy Garoppolo. Following season-ending injuries to Lance in Week 2 and Garoppolo in Week 13, Purdy was named the starter. He led the 49ers to the NFC Championship game, where his season ended with an elbow injury. The following season he led the 49ers back to the big stage, becoming the lowest drafted QB to start in a Super Bowl. Purdy earned a Pro Bowl nomination that season and finished 4 th in AP MVP voting . LT Jordan Mailata, Eagles – Hailing from the Bankstown suburb of Sydney, Australia, Mailata made the jump from the South Sydney Rabbitohs NRL under-20’s team to the NFL International Player Pathway Program . After a summer at the IMG Academy, and despite never having played a down of American Football, he was selected 233 rd overall by the Eagles in the seventh round of the 2018 draft. Mailata took his first regular-season snap in Week 1 of 2020. He got his first start at left tackle in Week 4, filling in for injured starter Jason Peters, and went on to start 10 games until his season was ended by a concussion. The following season he signed a four-year, $64 million contract as the Eagles’ starting left tackle, allowing Peters to leave in free agency. Mailata has become one of the NFL’s best at his position, earning second team All-Pro honors in 2024, when he started in the Eagles’ Super Bowl win over the Chiefs. Starters and Major Rotational Contributors S Reed Blankenship, Eagles – Reed Blankenship signed with the Eagles out of Middle Tennessee after going undrafted in 2022. He won a roster spot in camp as a backup safety and…
